News.title: Chelsea sweat over Joao Pedro injury after missing Tottenham defeat
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Joao Pedro was left out of Chelsea’s squad for their London derby defeat to Tottenham and requires further assessment after picking up an injury in training on Friday.

The striker, who has scored five goals and made three assists in the Premier League this season, suffered a knee injury which ruled him out of Chelsea’s match with Brentford ahead of the September international break, and he withdrew from Brazil duty.

He returned to the Chelsea team to score twice against Bournemouth and then played 90 minutes against Everton last weekend. But Pedro is not involved for the clash with Spurs due to another fitness issue, which is being assessed by the club.

Manager Xabi Alonso told Sky Sports: “Yesterday in training he felt something, and at the moment he has some liquid, so we have to do some tests to know how big the injury is. It's disappointing, but we need to carry on.”

Chelsea went on to suffer their first home defeat to Tottenham since 2018 with Joao Pedro’s absence being felt up front, losing 2-0 following a late capitulation.

Speaking more on Pedro’s status after the match, Alonso added: “We don't know yet because he has a lot of fluid, so he felt it yesterday and we need to wait probably until tomorrow to do the test and to know the whole situation and the whole seriousness of the injury and we will know soon enough.”

Alonso made no mention of Pedro’s fitness during his pre-match press conference, but did confirm that Argentinian goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez ​will be out for several weeks after surgery on a fractured jaw, which brings Mike Penders into the side.

Martinez ​was ⁠taken to hospital following a collision with defender Jarrad Branthwaite during last weekend’s 2-0 win over Everton.

“He’s been better; ⁠he had the surgery. We still ​need ⁠to wait. (He will be ‌out for] a few weeks. Hopefully less than more,” Alonso told a press ‌conference on Friday.

News.title: Islam Makhachev makes huge UFC decision as unexpected title fight is confirmed
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Islam Makhachev will not be defending his welterweight belt anytime soon, with an interim-title fight announced for UFC 336 in January.

Saturday brought the unexpected news that Carlos Prates and Michael Morales will fight each other at that event in Toronto, Canada, with the interim welterweight belt on the line.

Makhachev had been rumoured to headline the card at Scotiabank Arena on 30 January, with Prates standing out as his likeliest contender.

However, the Russian, 34, will seemingly take more time out before returning to the Octagon, leading the UFC to announce Prates vs Morales during UFC 333 on Saturday.

The fight will be the co-main event at UFC 336, before Joshua Van defends his flyweight title against Manel Kape.

Makhachev is the UFC’s pound-for-pound No 1 fighter and last fought in August, outpointing Ireland’s Ian Machado Garry. With that, the former lightweight king retained the welterweight title for the first time and reached 17 straight wins, a UFC record. His win streak dates back to 2015.

Meanwhile, Prates is 7-1 in the UFC with seven KO wins, including against ex-champions Jack Della Maddalena and Leon Edwards. The Brazilian’s only UFC loss was a decision defeat by Machado Garry. The 33-year-old is 24-7 overall.

And Morales is 7-0 in the UFC with five KO wins. The Ecuadoran, 27, is 19-0 overall.

News.title: Kimi Antonelli on verge of F1 world title after pole in United States GP
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Kimi Antonelli soared to pole position for the United States Grand Prix on a weekend when he could claim his place as Formula One’s youngest world champion.

The Italian turned the tables on Ferrari as the Scuderia, who had led the way for all three practice sessions, again fell flat when it came to the crunch.

Antonelli pipped Max Verstappen – winner of the last two races – to first spot on the grid by 0.179 seconds with Isack Hadjar third in the second Red Bull.

For Antonelli to claim the crown in the Lone Star State is a tall order; he would need to win Sunday’s race and hope that George Russell finishes lower than ninth and Lewis Hamilton lower than fifth.

But he did the first part of his job in supreme fashion, delivering a stellar lap to blow away his rivals and underline why he is the champion-in-waiting.

Russell struggled and will line up sixth, while Charles Leclerc and Hamilton managed only fourth and fifth as Ferrari’s pace disappeared when it mattered.

Sunday represents the 20-year-old Antonelli’s first shot at clinching the crown but, with a 102-point lead and only 150 left up for grabs ahead of this weekend’s tussle at the Circuit of the Americas, it appears merely a matter of when the Italian becomes champion.

open image in gallery Antonelli is on the verge of the world championship

Ferrari have not been on pole since Leclerc in Hungary in 2025, while Hamilton’s wait for top spot in qualifying extends to that same race two years earlier – 1,190 days ago.

Top-10 - United States GP qualifying 1. Kimi Antonelli 2. Max Verstappen 3. Isack Hadjar 4. Charles Leclerc 5. Lewis Hamilton 6. George Russell 7. Oscar Piastri 8. Lando Norris 9. Arvid Lindblad* 10. Liam Lawson *Lindblad has a five-place grid penalty

Hamilton is a five-time winner around the Circuit of the Americas and an upgraded Ferrari appeared to have put him in the mix to end his long wait for a pole position.

Ferrari president John Elkann was watching on from the garage, with pressure on the team to finally deliver in qualifying after a difficult run of races and increased speculation over the future of boss Fred Vasseur.

But Hamilton, 41, whose sole Ferrari win came in Barcelona in June, and Leclerc were again unable to pull it out of the bag.

Both Williams were among the stragglers knocked out in Q1 as their miserable season continued, with Alex Albon fuming “what a s**tshow”.

Lando Norris topped the opening run but McLaren chief executive Zak Brown told Sky Sports that Ferrari were “in a league of their own”.

open image in gallery Ferrari had pace in practice but struggled in qualifying

Leclerc hit back to lead the way ahead of the final session but Mercedes duo Antonelli and Russell had also come to the fore to suggest the battle for pole would be a tight one.

Antonelli soared to the top of the charts after the first run in Q3 and the Italian’s challengers fell by the wayside.

Hamilton improved marginally on his final run to clinch fifth but serious questions will be asked again in the Ferrari garage.

Oscar Piastri and Norris qualified seventh and eighth.

News.title: Stephen Bunting darts off to watch Borussia Dortmund after making quarter-finals
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Stephen Bunting will celebrate making the European Championship quarter-finals by watching Borussia Dortmund in Bundesliga action.

The Liverpudlian eased past Kim Huybrechts, firing four 100-plus checkouts in a 10-3 win to set up a last-eight showdown with Gerwyn Price on Sunday.

The Westfalenhalle arena is located next to Signal Iduna Park, where Dortmund host Eintracht Frankfurt on Saturday evening.

open image in gallery Signal Iduna Park is opposite the Westfalenhalle in Dortmund (Nick Potts/PA) ( PA Archive )

Bunting, who supports Liverpool, has become a lucky mascot for the Bundesliga club and has never seen them lose.

“We have tickets. I’m looking forward to the game and hopefully, they have a good performance,” he said.

“I think quite a few years ago now I went to the Bayern Munich and Dortmund game, and Dortmund won.

“Dortmund said, ‘Stephen Bunting’s been to our game, and we’ve never lost when Stephen Bunting’s there’.

“So yeah, I think they enjoy me going. I’ve been a few times now. I’ve got a great connection.

“I’m really looking forward to it, it should be a good game. They should win, it’s going to be a special day.”

Price made it through with a 10-4 victory over Cameron Menzies.

Ross Smith, who is top seed in this tournament due to his performances on the European Tour throughout the year, is through to the last eight after beating Damon Heta 10-7.

News.title: Antonelli takes another step closer to F1 title with US GP pole position
News.content:
Welcome to our live coverage for qualifying for the 2026 United States Grand Prix at the Circuit of the Americas, just outside of Austin. This is one of the finest tracks that we have on the Formula One calendar and is a fitting place for the US Grand Prix. The races are usually entertaining, the drivers love the track (though have complained about the bumps this year) and it comfortably the best on-track action of the three races in the US.

What might we see this weekend? Well, Kimi Antonelli could be crowned world champion if results go his way. The way the results need to go make that fairly unlikely, but stranger things have happened in F1 and they often do. In any case, it would take a catastrophic implosion for Antonelli to lose the championship from here, so it is a case of when rather than if.

Who looks in good form? Well, Ferrari do. They have brought an updated car here this weekend it, so far, is paying off. Charles Leclerc had good pace yesterday and Lewis Hamilton, his team-mate, was fastest earlier today in final practice. Hamilton’s time of 1min34.893sec was a tenth or two quicker than the Red Bull of Max Verstappen, with Leclerc not too far behind. Then it was Antonelli, George Russell in the second Mercedes and Oscar Piastri making up the top six, though the Australian was nearly half a second off the ultimate pace of Hamilton.

Qualifying begins in about 50 minutes and we will be here with all the updates from that.

News.title: Sensational Spurs storm Stamford Bridge as Palmer loses his head
News.content:
Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso has told Cole Palmer he must learn from his red card that contributed to his team’s London derby defeat by Tottenham Hotspur.

Tottenham head coach Roberto De Zerbi insisted Palmer should have seen red for shoving his pelvis into the face of Mateus Fernandes. But, having got off with a yellow card, the Chelsea midfielder then fouled substitute Conor Gallagher.

“I haven’t seen them [the yellow cards] on TV, but as far as I have been told, he [the referee] probably got it right,” Alonso said. “So, for sure for Cole, but for everyone. We think [up until] now we haven’t received any red cards [this season] and we need to continue that way because we need to have this maturity to deal with difficult moments, when you have conceded 1-0, there was still 15-20 minutes to go, so we have to be calm. I need to check the action to talk with Cole, but it is one to learn for the future for sure.”

Asked if he thought Palmer should have been sent off for the first yellow card, De Zerbi, who was booked for his protests, replied: “Yep.”

Jordan Henderson had spoken to Palmer at the end of the previous week’s victory over Everton in which the forward could also have been booked for a second time and sent off.

But Alonso claimed he does not have any wider concerns about Palmer’s character. He said: “Today, for sure, yes, but it is not a [wider] concern. I think that Cole when he is focused on the game, when he is enjoying and today after the 1-0, it is a moment to keep calm, a moment to keep mature and for everyone.”

De Zerbi hailed his side’s character and claimed that Tottenham have “suffered enough” after two 17th-placed finishes and a slow start to the season until successive victories over Coventry City and Chelsea.

“We want to improve, improve and improve, to be better game by game, week by week. I think we have suffered enough,” De Zerbi said. “Changing the spirit of the group, changing the performance of the players, especially the more fragile players, maybe the younger players. We played very well. Great individual performances, great collective performance because we played very well. And then we put something different than Tottenham, I think, in the last period. Different attitude, different relationships with the players, different group.”

Chelsea were without João Pedro because of an injury and Alonso is waiting to find out how long the striker will be out.

“We don’t know yet because he has a lot of fluid,” Alonso said. “So he felt it yesterday [Friday] and we need to wait probably until tomorrow [Sunday] to do the test and to know the whole situation and the whole seriousness of the injury. We will know soon enough.”

News.title: Pollock at heart of scuffle that inspires Leicester to thumping win in feisty derby
News.content:
Hello and welcome to our live coverage of Leicester Tigers v Northampton Saints.

The Prem’s derby weekend continues today at Mattioli Woods Welford Road, where Geoff Parling’s side go head-to-head in with their East Midlands rivals.

Both Leicester and Northampton have two wins from the opening three rounds of the season and with both sides involved in a number of high-scoring encounters already in the new campaign, we could be in for a real treat.

Tigers started the season with a 38-40 loss at home to Saracens, but bounced back quickly with wins over Gloucester and Newcastle Red Bulls. They will be itching to right a few wrongs after suffering a chastening Champions Cup defeat in Pau last week.

Northampton, meanwhile, have notched up wins over Newcastle Red Bulls and Bath either side of loss to Bristol Bears.

A win today for Saints would be their first on the road since defeating Exeter Chiefs at Sandy Park in April.

“It (the East Midlands derby) means a lot to everyone, we know it will be a great atmosphere at Mattioli Woods Welford Road,” said Parling.

“I don’t think with this sort of game either team has to build it up too much emotionally because that just comes, so I think it’s actually about being really really calm in the moment.”

“Hopefully we can put the best of ourselves out there and I’m sure Saints will be able to do exactly the same.”

Saints are without a victory in Leicester since January 2023, when a single point decided the 18-19 result.

Since then, the last five meetings between the sides have been won by the hosts on the day – with Saints last taking home the bragging rights when a Tom Litchfield hat-trick helped Northampton to a 45-31 win on home soil in last season’s league play-off.

Kick-off gets underway at 3.05pm. Stay with us here for all the latest updates.

News.title: Saliba has fight on his hands to usurp ‘unbelievable’ Konsa
News.content:
Hello and welcome to coverage from the Emirates as Premier League champions Arsenal host Everton.

Mikel Arteta’s men produced a good performance in midweek to draw with Bayern Munich in the Champions League while David Moyes’s squad have had the week off following their 2-0 defeat by Chelsea last weekend.

Arteta said: “We’re having three games in six days so we know what’s happening, especially when the games are so demanding and the necessity is to win. We know that, so we prepare the players for those scenarios and do the best we possibly can.

“I know David so well and how he sets the team, the quality they have in their organisation and individually. It’s no coincidence they didn’t lose before their last game. They have a really good team, which we know because in recent clashes, it’s always been a really difficult game for us.”

Both teams enter this game having been beaten just once this season but eight points separate them with Arsenal in second and Everton in eighth.

Moyes said: “It’s not an easy game and never has been over many years. We look forward to it; they had a game in midweek, and we have to try and capitalise on that. I thought we did really well last year against them; we played really well down at Arsenal, and I hope we can do the same.

“When I look back at the team we had out, we were pretty threadbare at that time, but we did a good job, and I hope we can do it again. Obviously Arsenal have some many different tools in their bag and people they can use in different positions, so we’re fully aware of the team we’re up against and the level.”

Former Arsenal players Ainsley Maitland-Niles and Christian Norgaard could feature for Everton this afternoon.

News.title: ‘Tactical genius’ Emery outsmarts Maresca as City crash to first league defeat
News.content:
It was four years ago to the day that Emery grabbed this famous club by the shirt and collar and gave them an almighty shake. After a summer of much instability including many player sales, he appears to have already struck a formula with his newly assembled team.

There were a number of fine individual performances from many of the summer arrivals, such as Jackson, goalkeeper Zion Suzuki and Johan Manzambi.

Emery said: “We were very motivated and Manchester City is the best team in the world so this is the level. This year we started so poorly and we needed time to understand how we improve. The players showed the capacity to retrieve the level we’ve had over the last few years.

“Nicolas is more mature and very demanding of himself to improve. Earlier this season he was shooting over the crossbar but he is now finding the corners. There is still work to do and 11 points is not enough but we are feeling better.”

Villa were fierce from the start and ahead after six minutes. Guéhi’s mistake was punished by John McGinn, with the ball dropping to Jackson who crashed a shot into the roof of the net.

The home team did require Suzuki to produce saves to stop efforts from Iliman Ndiaye, Rayan Cherki and Abdukodir Khusanov as City responded. Ndiaye also struck the outside of the post and City were level seven minutes into the second half with Erling Haaland nodding in Ndiaye’s cross at the far post. Haaland had touched the ball just eight times in the opening 45 minutes but invariably only needs one chance.

News.title: England hammer France to keep Rugby League World Cup hopes alive
News.content:
With Samoa beating Papua New Guinea 64-6 earlier on Saturday, England’s task was put into stark and imposing focus. The Pacific Islanders have a points difference of plus-132. Courtesy of this mauling, England’s is plus-64. So they must see off Papua New Guinea by a big number next Friday and then pray that Tonga defeat Samoa two days later. That is their only route through.

In truth, that is as much as McDermott could hope after their initial shortcomings, as they seek to avoid missing out on the last four for the first time in the World Cup’s 72-year history.

“What we’ve done today, given the context, is just enormous,” McDermott said. “We had to win big but, as any coach will tell you, nobody thinks like that. You think, ‘we’ve got to win’.

“We had some real good, candid conversations this week about what that actually means and we’ve been able to do that without getting distracted in chasing points.”

It should be remembered that this was only McDermott’s second game in charge and, even allowing for the poor opposition, they were dramatically improved.

“We’ve been together for five field sessions only,” he said. “We’re building something here and there was a little bit of that on show today.

“Certainly the six tries we scored in the last 17 minutes or so before half-time are what we’ve been chasing. We can see how good that’s going to be.

“If this group’s together for a process or a long build-up to a tournament, we could achieve some special things but, over a short space of time, it’s been remarkable really.”

It is incredible to think that England took 22 minutes to break the deadlock, when the ever-excellent Dom Young burst through. From there, they averaged a try every four or so minutes, with France looking increasingly forlorn and fatigued.

News.title: How an aid initiative maimed thousands of children in war-torn Africa
News.content:
Tormented by pain from severe internal burns, Amza Kebbie is one of thousands of children in Sierra Leone damaged for life by an aid intervention which went horribly wrong.

It has been five days since the four-year-old boy drank caustic soda, one of the two main ingredients for making soap, after mistaking it for drinking water. The highly corrosive liquid, also known as sodium hydroxide, has stripped the lining of his oesophagus and part of his stomach, causing life changing damage.

He’s now in intensive care, clinging precariously to life. An intravenous drip provides fluids and there’s a nasal cannula that enables him to breathe. Medics and relatives look over him around the clock.

If he can gather enough strength (which the nurses say is by no means guaranteed) the dangerously sick child will undergo a gastrostomy, an operation that will see a tube directly inserted into his stomach so that he can be fed long term.

Amza drank caustic soda while being looked after by a neighbour who was making soap at home Credit : The Telegraph/SImon Townsley

He can no longer swallow properly and may never be able to do so again, say his doctors.

This is not an isolated tragedy. Across Sierra Leone, there are thousands of children like Amza, and their number is growing every year.

At the Goderich Surgical Centre in the capital Freetown, around 200 children are admitted annually with caustic soda poisoning. Many more are thought to die in remote regions where emergency medical treatment is unavailable.

Behind the calamity is a humanitarian initiative that has spectacularly backfired. It’s a prime example of the law of unintended consequences; of a seemingly sensible and undoubtedly well meaning public health intervention doing more harm than good.

Fatmata Kamara accidentally drank caustic soda at her grandmother’s house in 2014 and has had a feeding tube ever since Credit : SImon Townsley

The story starts in the aftermath of Sierra Leone’s vicious civil war, which ran between 1991 and 2002.

Fought between the government and the Revolutionary United Front – backed by Liberian warlord Charles Taylor – the war claimed an estimated 50,000 to 70,000 lives, displaced 2.5 million people and left the country brutalised and in ruins.

In its aftermath, international aid agencies and NGOs desperately sought ways to revive the country and alighted on DIY soap making as a way of killing two birds with one stone.

Siblings Aminata Fofana and Salieu Bangura help out with the family soap-making business Credit : The Telegraph/Simon Townsley

Organisations including UNHCR, UNICEF and World Vision thought the practice would both improve sanitation in the country’s disease-ridden shanty towns and provide home-bound women with the means to earn a sustainable income.

It seemed like an obvious “win-win”, and schemes to help women set up in the soap making business rapidly proliferated.

An annual report by the International Federation of the Red Cross, published in May 2002, promoted a micro-finance scheme to fund small-scale soapmaking.

Saieu Bangura, 13, with a tub of soap flakes Credit : The Telegraph/Simon Townsley

In 2005, the Centre for War Affected Women in Sierra Leone’s Kono district, backed by the UNHCR, listed soap making as one of the main training courses for war widows and female amputees.

And at about the same time, the Freetown-based Safer Future Youth Development Programme, supported by UNICEF and the charity War Child, provided “a tool kit for soap production” at its training workshops.

As recently as 2020, Action Aid ran a promotional article on its Sierra Leone website showing how soap making had enabled women to become financially independent of their husbands.

The article ran under the headline: “With Soap Making Skills – I'm Empowered!”

Mabinty Bangura is taken to theatre for an endoscopy Credit : Simon Townsley

It is for good reason that the ancient Greek physician Hippocrates urged doctors “first, do no harm”.

To follow the rule literally is not possible as all health interventions entail some risk but it's a reminder never to underestimate the capacity of a new intervention to backfire.

There are plenty of examples from history to choose from.

During the British Raj in India, the government offered a cash bounty for every dead cobra as a way of reducing the danger of venomous snakes.

The surgical team examine the internal damage via an endoscopy Credit : The Telegraph/Simon Townsley

But rather than leading to a decline in snake numbers, the plan resulted in entrepreneurial individuals breeding cobras just so they could kill them and then claim the reward.

Once officials realised what was happening and the scheme was stopped, thousands of the then worthless cobras were released into the wild, greatly increasing the risk of snakebite.

In the late 1950s, the Chinese Communist regime introduced an equally calamitous public health campaign involving sparrows.

They issued a directive ordering the birds to be destroyed because they were thought to spread disease and destroy crops.

A child’s gastrostomy scar with a feeding tube in place Credit : The Telegraph/Simon Townsley

What those behind the idea failed to consider was that sparrows are natural predators. As their numbers declined, the locust population exploded, decimating agriculture and contributing to the Great Chinese Famine in which millions died.

So what went wrong in Sierra Leone? What did those behind the soap making scheme fail to foresee?

Experts say the initiative simply failed to consider the danger inherent in encouraging people to use toxic chemicals in their homes.

The brightly coloured buckets in which caustic soda is made, and then mixed with oil and scent to make soap, are the same buckets used across the country to fetch and hold drinking water. And just like drinking water, the lethal solution is cool, clear and inviting.

Just a drop is enough to cause the most horrific burns. So when a thirsty young child like Amza runs in from play and mistakenly scoops up a cup of it to quench their thirst they will lose their oesophagus, if not their lives.

Giuseppe Meucci, chief surgeon at the Goderich Surgical Centre Credit : The Telegraph/Simon Townsley

Giuseppe Meucci, chief surgeon at the 56-bed Goderich hospital in Freetown where four year old Amza is being cared for, has been treating patients burned by sodium hydroxide nearly every day since arriving in Freetown in 2019.

Three quarters of patients seen by the hospital’s specialist programme for oesophageal burns, set up in response to the crisis and run by the Italian medical charity Emergency, are under five.

“It’s a struggle in this country,” says Dr Meucci. “Almost every family knows someone who has suffered because of this problem. But they just keep coming.”

Hospital director Jasna Sundic Credit : The Telegraph/Simon Townsley

“In most countries you remove the source of danger for the child, but here that doesn’t seem to happen,” he says.

“It’s one of the main health problems of this country. Soda is there with malaria, malnutrition and typhoid complications. It’s one of the reasons why so many children die before they reach five years old.”

Hospital director Jasna Sundic agrees.

“This is a very severe issue but one which is very preventable,” she tells the Telegraph. “[But] however much we do here, we have not been able to decrease the overall number of soda patients being admitted.

“We cannot stop mothers who have no other source of income except making soap.”

Ibrahim Kerah is fed by his father Mohamed Credit : SImon Townsley

In a handful of rare cases, burns victims are sent abroad for complex oesophageal reconstruction surgery but this is not an option for the vast majority of children injured in Sierra Leone.

More than 60 per cent require surgery, but for these children, like Amza, a feeding tube that bypasses the oesophagus is the only option.

The hospital has many of these gastrostomy patients.

Critically underweight Mabinty Bangura Credit : The Telegraph/SImon Townsley

In a ward dedicated to soda burns, four-year-old Ibrahim Kerah is being fed through his stomach tube by his father Mohamed.

They travelled together on the back of a motorbike taxi for nearly 10 hours to get here for his third check-up appointment.

The Telegraph watches as Mohamed carefully prepares his son’s meal, adding spinach leaves to the porridge-like mix which is fed into a syringe at the end of the tube.

At an adjoining bed two-year-old Mabinty Bangura is critically underweight after ingesting soda about six months ago. Nurses have put her on a high protein drip so she can regain enough strength to undergo the same bypass surgery.

In the courtyard outside, mothers whose children have just had a gastrostomy are being taught how to prepare the liquid food.

Ibrahim and his father Mohamed endured a 10-hour motorbike journey to attend his hospital check-up Credit : The Telegraph/SImon Townsley

Isatu Alie, 24, has been living with a stomach tube for 12 years, and now works for Emergency as a patient ambassador.

She is eight months pregnant with her second child and proud to have overcome her injury and the stigma of having to feed through a tube.

“I remember what happened so well,” she says. “I had just got back from school. I took my cup and dunked it into the water bucket. My aunt made soap and, on that day, I didn’t ask about the liquid in the bucket. The pain was incredible”.

More than a decade has passed since her surgery, and Isatu has adjusted well.

“I’m okay with it now. I feel like a normal human being; I’m blessed to be here,” she says.

“Now I speak to children and their parents who have just experienced the same thing and tell them not to lose hope.”

Pregnant Isatu Alie now works as a patient ambassador Credit : The Telegraph/SImon Townsley

A small proportion of the patients needing treatment following caustic soda burns are adults.

Among them is 21-year-old Junisa Bundeh, who is on a follow-up visit to check his stomach tube. He explains that he gulped down what he thought was a cup of water from a basin while eating at his grandmother’s house three months ago.

“It was so painful,” recalls Junisa. “I realised what it was straight away because it was so harsh. I tried to spit it all out but the liquid was already going down my throat.”

Mothers are taught how to prepare liquid food; Junisa Bundeh shows his feeding tube Credit : SImon Townsley

In the muddy lanes of Freetown’s Waterloo district there are makeshift soap making operations all over.

The coloured plastic buckets full of either soda or water are everywhere.

Against the backdrop of the rainy season’s persistent gloom, the containers symbolise a measure of cleanliness for families sheltering from torrential downpours under mouldy concrete awnings.

As the Telegraph watches Yabom Kapro, a village elder, making soap, the risks involved are immediately obvious.

Chief Yabom Kapro makes soap at her Waterloo town home, near Freetown Credit : The Telegraph/SImon Townsley

As she tips a purple bucket of caustic soda solution into a large basin and then adds palm oil from a plastic jerrycan, local children hover round the cluster of colourful containers.

Yabom uses a wooden paddle to stir the mixture into a creamy paste and then pours it into a mould held in place by an old motorcycle tyre.

Buckets containing caustic soda dissolving, top. Caustic soda crystals, below Credit : The Telegraph/SImon Townsley

Once set, the beige-coloured cake of soap is cut into blocks which are then grated on a wire mesh contraption to be sold at the local market.

“When you dilute the caustic soda, it is completely clear like water at first,” says another soap maker, 43-year-old Cilina Bangura.

“Afterwards a white scum forms on the top, but you cannot be watching all of the time, [even] with all of these children around.”

Cilina knows the risks but says she can't afford to stop making soap. It has, as the NGOs intended, become an economic lifeline for her and her family.

“I want my children to continue making soap when I stop working,” she says. “I took out a loan to buy everything I needed, and now it is the only way I can make a living.

“Of course, I know how dangerous soda is – it has burned my skin many times – but I don’t have another option.”

Home-made soap, in Waterloo Credit : The Telegraph/SImon Townsley

Maimunatu Sankoh, three, whose family lives in a nearby tin-roof shack, is sadly too well aware of that danger from her own bitter experience of soda poisoning.

As she feeds her daughter through a stomach tube, Maimunatu’s mum Iyesatu complains: “I have never seen any public information about soda.

“There are warnings on the packets but that is no use once the product is dissolved in water. They need to tell people to keep buckets out of the way.”

Iyesatu Kamara feeds her daughter Maimunatu Sankoh at their home Credit : SImon Townsley

Incidents of children consuming harmful chemicals are not confined to developing countries and were once common in the west.

In the US, the Poison Prevention Packaging Act was introduced in 1970, mandating childproof containers and the labelling of harmful household products.

The UK followed suit in 1975 with the introduction of child-resistant safety caps on containers of caustic soda and most other noxious household substances.

Despite the risks, Cilina says she can't afford to stop making soap Credit : The Telegraph/Simon Townsley

Such legislation is still a long way off in Sierra Leone and is anyway far too late for four-year-old Amza.

Under heavy sedation in the intensive care unit, his glazed eyes open only occasionally.

The only visible evidence of his injuries is some scarring on his lips, but the doctors say his throat, oesophagus and stomach have all been seared by several large gulps of soda.

The boy’s mother, Mamie Kebbie, 30, keeps a watchful vigil, stroking his listless head tenderly. She says he used to be a playful and vivacious child.

If they are taken to hospital quickly, children with soda burns are normally given an oesophageal dilation endoscopy – a procedure which aims to keep the oesophagus open – but for Amza this has not been possible.

Freetown, Sierra Leone Credit : Simon Townsley

“This is a very severe case,” explains nurse Annette Turay, who heads the hospital’s intensive care unit. “When he was brought in, about 10 hours after he had ingested the soda, we were unable to conduct an endoscopy because he already had respiratory problems.

“He has pneumonia and he cannot feed through his mouth. He cannot even swallow his own saliva.

Mamie Kebbie keeps a vigil at her son's bedside Credit : The Telegraph/Simon Townsley

“It will be a week before he is strong enough for us to be able to operate. We will insert a gastric tube into his stomach. He will have to keep this as his main way of being fed for a long time, potentially forever.”

But nurse Turay has seen worse.

“I have seen so many children suffering a lot after ingesting soda, so many dying too.

“A few weeks ago, we had a child in the ward who died because his stomach was completely gone”.

The Telegraph contacted all the NGOs involved in the setting up of and promotion of soap making schemes in Sierra Leone that are mentioned in this story for comment.

Sports.title: Liverpool loanee Harvey Elliott sent off after receiving two yellow cards in 20 seconds for Valencia
Sports.content:
Next

LIVERPOOL loanee Harvey Elliott’s struggles continued in Spain as he was sent off with two yellow cards within seconds during a crunch LaLiga clash.

Elliott, 23, was shipped out on loan to Valencia on transfer deadline day as he didn’t figure into the Reds’ new manager Andoni Iraola‘s plans.



This came after the playmaker failed to shine during his temporary stint at Aston Villa last season as he only managed one goal in nine appearances.

The ex-England youth international’s fortunes haven’t really improved at Valencia as he has only managed a total of 152 minutes in all of his six appearances for the club.



And Elliott’s misfortunes extended during the Derbi de la Comunitat with rivals Villarreal at the Mestalla Stadium.

The Liverpool loanee came on as a second-half substitute in the 70th minute.



The score was 1-1 as Villarreal’s Alex Freeman cancelled out Pepelu’s opener for the hosts.

And Javier Aguirre’s side soon picked up an advantage as the visitors lost Pape Gueye to a red card.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick baffled by fascination with Man Utd’s running stats as boss insists he trusts players ‘100 per cent’
Sports.content:
Next

MANCHESTER UNITED are one of the worst running sides in the Premier League.

But do not mention the word “pressing” to under-fire boss Michael Carrick.



Fitness has been a recurring issue at Old Trafford since David Moyes told the players at one of his first-team meetings he would “make them run more”.

Carrick was in the dressing room when Moyes outlined his blueprint in July 2013 and took exception to it.



United players — like former midfielder Carrick — felt their tendency to end games strongly was down to LIMITING their workload in the first hour.

However, a string of bosses post-Sir Alex Ferguson have wanted their sides to run more.

Ole Gunnar Solskjaer wanted his United players to be the “hardest-working”.

Jose Mourinho praised Marcus Rashford in December 2018 for running like a “mad dog”.

And six years later, Ruben Amorim urged his Old Trafford stars to “run like mad dogs”.

Ralf Rangnick attempted to incorporate ‘gegenpressing’ into United’s style but gave up after two Premier League games in December 2021.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Erik ten Hag inflicted a punishing 13km run on his stars in training after Brentford outran them by the same distance in a 4-0 thrashing in August 2022. This term United players have covered 487.4 miles across their seven Prem games.

Only Liverpool (482.5) have run fewer miles but Andoni Iraola’s men are fifth while United are 15th.

Carrick’s men have been outrun by every opponent this season except one — Manchester City in the 1-0 defeat at Old Trafford.

And Enzo Maresca’s side played with ten men from the 23rd minute after Phil Foden’s red card.

Carrick, whose struggling team host Bournemouth today, is clinging to his job, with Brighton’s Fabian Hurzeler considered the standout Prem coach to replace him although Eddie Howe remains favourite with the bookies.



The 48-year-old has been without a club since leaving Newcastle in the summer.

Hurzeler’s high-flying Seagulls went viral last month for a pressing sequence in their 3-0 dismantling of champions Arsenal.

Little wonder Carrick has downplayed the concept of pressing.

The former Middlesbrough boss said: “I think you’ve got to be careful with saying ‘not running’.



“We’ve won a lot of games over a period of time.

“And this pressing thing that suddenly everyone thinks about pressing . . . pressing is one small part of football.

“There’s all sorts of different ways of what people class as a press. What actually is it?

“What are you doing it for? Is it to your strength? Is it covering up other spaces?



“You don’t necessarily need to press to win games of football.

“Sometimes you do, sometimes you don’t. It’s just a word that gets thrown about. We’ve got to be a bit careful with that. It’s not necessarily just running stats that define football games, either.”

Despite United’s horror start putting him in grave danger of the sack, Carrick said: “I trust them 100 per cent. I definitely trust the players.

“It wasn’t a good night in Como for many reasons, we all know that.



“We will be a different team on Sunday. We have to be a different team.”

Captain Bruno Fernandes questioned Carrick’s tactics when the Champions League capitulation to Como left them winless in seven games.

It came days after Lisandro Martinez was fined for an astonishing blast at director of football Jason Wilcox.

Old Trafford boss Carrick has refused to rule out dropping Fernandes for this afternoon’s Prem visit of Bournemouth.



Changes are inevitable after Wednesday night’s debacle.

Carrick bickered with forward Matheus Cunha in the first half of United’s 4-1 thrashing before hooking him at half-time.

Fernandes has played in four different positions in as many games and was taken off in Italy.

Carrick’s emotional address on Friday lasted almost six minutes before he took questions in a press conference that ran to almost 20 minutes.

The gaffer explained he wants United’s history to provide inspiration.



He stressed: “I fully understand the situation and my position and I know what this club means to so many people.

Sports.title: Legend says Pierre Sage will be sacked if Crystal Palace get hammered by Newcastle but one man can save him
Sports.content:
Next

CRYSTAL PALACE legend Clinton Morrison says Pierre Sage will be sacked if they suffer another hammering against Newcastle.

The Eagles were thumped 5-0 by Brighton last week – their biggest loss to their rivals since 1956 – and have the worst defensive record in the league, conceding 17 goals.



Pressure is mounting on French boss Sage, who only replaced Oliver Glasner this summer, as they prepare to take on fellow out-of-sorts Toon at Selhurst Park.

But former striker Morrison, who made 316 appearances for Palace and scored 112 goals, says it will be the end of the line if they capitulate against Newcastle like they did last week.



Speaking exclusively to Sun Sport via BetSelect, he said: “He’d be gone. If they lose 4-0 or 5-0 to Newcastle, he’ll be sacked, because that’s no improvement on the last Premier League game, so you’re not learning your lesson.

“So what are you coaching in training? I know everyone can have back-to-back defeats, but it’s the manner of it. If you’re conceding four or five goals again, then what are you working on? Or are the players buying into what you’re trying to do?

“At the end of the day, I hope the manager does become a success. I’ve met him, and he seems like a nice guy, and I hope he can turn things around. But if you lose back-to-back Premier League games 4-0 or 5-0, you’ll be under big pressure, and you could be leaving.”

A 4,000-mile round-trip to Besiktas in the Europa League on Thursday was hardly the ideal preparation for Palace ahead of the crunch clash.

But Morrison says the gruelling trip to Turkey is no excuse not to beat the Mags, who have had eight days to prepare for the journey south.

Morrison said: “There’s no excuse. Newcastle have lost their last two games. I’m not saying it’s the perfect game to go and play Newcastle, because Newcastle are in a transition period.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“The new manager has come in, and they’ve got a few injuries too. But the Premier League’s the bread and butter at the end of the day.

“He [Sage] knows these next two games are crucial to him. He’ll have until probably the international break, and if he’s not in a good position, then they’ll make a change.

“That starts with the weekend against Newcastle. He has to get a result against Newcastle. It’s a massive game for both teams, but in particular Crystal Palace.”

The only bright spot from the embarrassment at the Amex was the return of striker Jean-Philippe Mateta following injury.



And Morrison says the wantaway Frenchman, who scored in the 2-2 draw at Besiktas, could be the man to save Sage’s job.

He added: “Yes, I do. He needs to get fit. I’ve got so much time for JP, but too often we’re talking about Mateta wanting to leave the club. Eventually he will leave because his contract’s running out, but he scored the winning goal last year in the Europa Conference League, and he’s a big-game player.

“If they can get him fit and firing, I think he’ll make a big difference and score goals. He’s competing with Strand Larsen and Eddie Nketiah, but at the moment he’s the main man because he’s done well in previous seasons.



“He just needs to get fit, firing, and hungry again. Stop talking about leaving the club and focus solely on scoring goals for Crystal Palace. Because if you do your job on the pitch for Crystal Palace, you’ll get that move that you want.”

MICHAEL CARRICK has spoken to Manchester United great Sir Alex Ferguson and former colleague Ole Gunnar Solskjaer amid the team’s spiral.

Carrick is battling to remain in charge of United, who have gone seven games without a win and host Bournemouth in the Premier League on Sunday.



United have won two of their 11 games this term and Bournemouth are unbeaten in six against them, having won 3-0 twice and drawn 4-4 in their last three fixtures at Old Trafford.

Carrick namechecked Ferguson in his stirring opening monologue at his pre-match press conference on Friday and played under the Scot for seven years.



Solskjaer kept Carrick on as a first team coach when he managed United for nearly three years before Carrick succeeded him as caretaker in November 2021.

Carrick and Solskjaer, who played alongside each other in the current boss’s first season at United in 2006-07, were up against each other to replace Ruben Amorim in January and remain friends.

Ferguson, who was in attendance for United’s 1-1 draw with Leeds United last week, and Solskjaer remain in constant contact with Carrick.

Sports.title: Newcastle star Joelinton takes leaf out of departed pal Bruno Guimaraes’ book to help ease pressure on Matthias Jaissle
Sports.content:
Next

JOELINTON is taking a leaf out of Bruno Guimaraes’ book to help stop the rot at Newcastle.

And the 30-year-old issued a passionate rallying call to his battered team-mates ahead of a crunch trip to the capital to face Crystal Palace.



The midfield hardman wore the captain’s armband during last week’s crushing 1-0 home defeat to Aston Villa – Toon‘s third defeat in four.

The Brazilian has endured turbulent times before on Tyneside since his arrival from Hoffenheim in 2019. And he insists the Magpies must keep their heads high when they march into Selhurst Park.



Joelinton has spent the past five years learning the leadership ropes from former skipper Guimaraes and veteran right-back Kieran Trippier.

Now, alongside club captain Dan Burn, he is using every trick he learned from his compatriot to help drag Newcastle out of the mud.



He said: “He [Bruno] had a lot of qualities. His best quality was always to be there, always present in the moment, always fighting till the end. That’s what I’m trying to do.

“We had other leaders too, great guys like Kieran Trippier in the past, we have Dan Burn, a great leader, and you try to learn something from everyone.

“But the most important thing is just be myself and do the things that I always have done.”

The Toon Army are desperate for a spark to reignite a season that is falling flat under new boss Matthias Jaissle. Joelinton insists the answer is simple — stick together and fight to get the job done in South London.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

The veteran admitted picking up the squad has not been easy, but declared: “When we win, we are not the best team in the world, and when we lose, we’re not the worst.

“That’s got to be the mentality to get ourselves up, work hard, and keep going.”

With pressure mounting on Jaissle and his tactics, some fans are calling Sunday’s clash at Palace a potential make-or-break affair.

However, Joelinton spat back at that suggestion and says the squad are not feeling any extra pressure.



He said: “Every game is a must-win. We are competitors, we want to win every game. It’s football, it’s life, sometimes things don’t go in your way, sometimes you are not at your best.

“Now it’s time to stick together and stay positive and work hard. We hope to have a better performance at the weekend.

It has been a nightmare start to the campaign for the combative fan fave following the departure of close pal Guimaraes and fellow midfielder Sandro Tonali.



After being handed the vice-captaincy by Jaissle, Joelinton found himself sidelined with a frustrating recurring hamstring injury.

And watching from the stands as Newcastle struggled to hit their stride under the new manager was pure torture.

He said: “Yes, it’s not been easy. It’s been difficult for me. New season, but I have a similar problem that I had last season and before, so it’s been a challenge.

“I always keep going and just glad to be back now and I hope I can improve. I hope I can help the boys.”



His return to full fitness — alongside towering defender Burn — has provided a massive double shot in the arm for Jaissle ahead of the trip south.

And Joelinton feels Burn’s return to the pitch could prove game-changing. He said: “We hope so, but it’s a question that you have to ask the manager if he’s coming back in the starting XI or not. But, of course, to have him back is a great lift for everybody.

“He’s a great leader, great player, and he’s so important for the team.”

Joelinton has survived tough times at St. James’ Park before and gone on to enjoy famous Champions League nights and Carabao Cup success.

Despite the team being jeered off last Saturday, he told worried supporters the good times will be back again soon.

Sports.title: Peter Crouch & Abbey Clancy eying up buying football club & charting progress in TV doc after £5m minnows deal collapses
Sports.content:
Next

EX-FOOTIE star Peter Crouch and his model wife Abbey Clancy want to buy their own team to feature in a reality telly show.

The pair hope to join some of his old teammates and other pals to take on a small club and transform it.



Lanky Crouchy, a striker for Liverpool, Spurs and England, is said to be determined to go ahead after coming close to signing a £5million deal to snap up minnows Farnham Town FC.

Peter, 45, and Abbey, 40, joined a consortium including former Chelsea and England star Joe Cole for the failed bid to take control of the Surrey-based National League South outfit.



Telly pundit Crouch, who retired from football in 2019 while at Burnley, told friends he was not disheartened and is keen to get back to the heart of the sport he loves.

A source said: “Peter was approached about the Farnham Town opportunity a couple of months ago.



“Their league is a long way from his Prem days but he loved what he saw.

“He spent some time down there getting to know the club and even appeared on the pitch as a mascot for a charity day. He saw taking them on as a great opportunity.

“Sadly some spanners in the works late on meant that the deal couldn’t be finalised.

“Now he’s on the hunt for another deal elsewhere because he’s very excited by the idea.”



Peter and his 44-year-old pal Joe, alongside their wives Abbey and Carly Cole, would join a growing set of star name owners if they do get involved.

Actors Ryan Reynolds and Rob McElhenney’s successful purchase of Wrexham became a hugely popular Netflix ­documentary series.

Will Ferrell, meanwhile, has a stake in Leeds United, ­rapper Stormzy is a co-owner of Croydon Athletic and ex-NFL ace Tom Brady has bought into Birmingham City.

Sports.title: Business Secretary held talks with Premier League chiefs two weeks after meeting with fund run by Man City chairman
Sports.content:
Next

THE Business Secretary had talks with the Premier League soon after meeting the Abu Dhabi fund run by Man City’s chairman.

Jonathan Reynolds met Prem chiefs on February 4 last year, Government records show.



It came while City were awaiting the verdict in the League’s case against them.

Two weeks earlier, Mr ­Reynolds met Mubadala Investment Company, run by Man City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak, at the World Economic Forum in Davos.



The Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade said of the earlier talks: “The Business Secretary did not discuss Manchester City in his meeting with the Premier League.

“The meeting was crucial in discussing the Government’s growth agenda and the ­Football Governance Bill.”



The bill, creating England’s first independent football regulator, was going through the Lords at the time.

Prem bosses had raised concerns over the watchdog’s powers, including the ability to step in over how cash is shared with the EFL, which controls the Championship, League One and League Two.

The regulator was formally launched in July 2025.

The Sun on Sunday revealed last week that Mr Reynolds met Mubadala twice while City’s financial rules case was being heard or was awaiting a verdict.



Last month the independent commission that carried out the probe found City guilty of more than 100 financial breaches.

The case was heard in secret in 2024.

The club deny wrongdoing and are appealing.

Mr Reynolds, MP for Stalybridge and Hyde in Greater Manchester, was replaced as Business Secretary in ­September 2025, but returned to the post in July this year.

Sports.title: Antonelli takes surprise pole to boost chances of sealing title in USA
Sports.content:
Kimi Antonelli beat Max Verstappen to pole position for the United States Grand Prix to boost his chances of sealing a maiden world championship in Sunday's race.

The 20-year-old Mercedes driver is all but certain to become Formula 1's youngest ever champion but could clinch the title with five rounds to spare if he wins in Austin on Sunday and other placings go his way.

It was perhaps the most unlikely of Antonelli's seven poles this season as he came from nowhere in Q3 to surge ahead of Verstappen, who had appeared for most of the weekend to be battling Ferrari for the front-row positions.

Verstappen's Red Bull team-mate Isack Hadjar equalled his best qualifying result by taking third, leaving Ferrari's Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton fourth and fifth, respectively.

George Russell will start from sixth, with the Brit needing to finish in the top eight to ensure Antonelli won't be crowned champion if he wins on Sunday. Hamilton would also need to finish fifth or lower in the event of an Antonelli victory for the title to be confirmed.

Oscar Piastri took seventh ahead of his McLaren team-mate Lando Norris as the latter was demoted from sixth after having his final effort deleted for breaching track limits.

Racing Bulls took the final two top-10 places but Liam Lawson will inherit ninth from his team-mate Arvid Lindblad, who has a five-place grid penalty for exceeding his engine component allowance.

Sports.title: Littler powers past Aspinall to reach European Championship quarter-finals
Sports.content:
Luke Littler remains on course to win the one major title he's never won as he beat Nathan Aspinall 10-5 in the second round of the European Championship Darts on Saturday evening.

Littler produced the second-best average in the competition's history - his 114.47 has only ever been bettered by Phil Taylor's 118.14 - as he secured an impressive victory in Dortmund.

Aspinall produced ten 180s in the match - three more than his opponent - but it wasn't enough to survive the onslaught from the world No 1, who won the first four legs of the match in 12 darts or fewer.

Aspinall briefly rallied to reduce the score to 5-4, but Littler controlled the second half of the game and, despite one brief interruption to deal with a vocal fan in the crowd, he ultimately closed out the match on D10.

"I felt really good from the off," Littler told ITV.

"I knew the start was good. I was gutted at giving him a leg and going into the first break at 4-1 when I wanted 5-0.

"Nathan is always there and is always going to come back at you. I couldn't afford to drop off. I felt confident and had to get the job done."

European Championship: Saturday's results

Round Two

Littler arrived at this tournament following shock defeats at the World Series of Darts and the World Grand Prix which ended his dreams of a perfect season in the majors.

However, he remains on track to win the European Championship for the first time after exiting in the last 16 of his debut campaign last year.

"I'm playing well. I'm feeling really good. There was only one issue in there, but other than that the crowd have been really good," he added.

"I've had a long time off and past results haven't gone my way. I've seen on social media some memes that 'Luke's finished' and this and that.

"I've had long enough to look at them, get on the practice board and forget about it all. Hopefully if I do lift the trophy I can say I've not gone anywhere.

"I've definitely not gone anywhere here with that performance."

Littler will face Krzysztof Ratajski in the quarter-finals after the Pole fought from behind to beat Kevin Doets 10-8.

Ratajski lost the first four legs of the match and trailed 8-6 in the closing stages before clinching four legs in a row to seal a victory over the man who stunned Michael van Gerwen in round one.

Home favourite Martin Schindler kept alive his hopes of winning the title in Dortmund as he powered to a 10-4 win over Jermaine Wattimena.

The German averaged just 90, but relied on finishing stats of more than 52 per cent - including a brilliant 121 in the ninth leg - and the support of a raucous crowd to reach the last eight on home turf for the first time.

He will face Jonny Clayton on Sunday after the Welshman beat Josh Rock 10-8 in the final match of the day.

Clayton wasted a series of match darts in the closing stages, but clinched the win in brilliant fashion with a 121 checkout on the bullseye.

Afternoon session: Van Veen's reign ended by Woodhouse

Image: Defending champion Gian van Veen suffered an early exit

In the afternoon session, Luke Woodhouse ended Gian van Veen's reign as European champion, as he coasted into the quarter-finals with a 10-6 victory.

Woody will face top seed Ross Smith on Sunday in a bid to reach the semi-final after the 2022 European champion held off a Damon Heta fightback.

A scintillating start saw Smith average in excess of 112 to storm into a 5-0 lead before Heta rallied, only to succumb to a 10-7 loss. Smith finished with six 180s and an average of 96.19.

Gerwyn Price averaged 95.75 to reach the quarter-finals for the first time in three years with a dominant 10-4 victory over Cameron Menzies, which included three ton-plus finishes.

It was tight after seven legs which all went with throw, but 'The Iceman' shifted through the gears to pull clear, winning seven of the last eight legs.

Stephen Bunting produced a finishing clinic (56 per cent) to defeat Kim Huybrechts and reach the quarter-finals for the first time since 2014.

'The Bullet' hit 10/18 on the doubles and four ton-plus checkouts to set up a blockbuster showdown with Price on Sunday.

If Price wins the title this weekend, he will provisionally be ranked higher than Luke Humphries, who withdrew from this event through illness. That would open up the possibility of a Luke vs Luke semi-final at the World Darts Championship.

Sports.title: Smith beats Puello in thriller to retain WBC title and stay unbeaten
Sports.content:
Dalton Smith retained his WBC light-welterweight title with a thrilling, split-decision victory over Alberto Puello on Saturday night.

On his homecoming at Utilita Arena, the Sheffield man was taken the distance in his first title defence, but kept his unbeaten record in tact as judges Kieran McCann of England and Spain's Jon Llona both scored the bout 115-113 in his favour, while Filipino Ray Danseco had it 116-112 to Puello.

Puello - is a former WBA and WBC champion - suffered only his second defeat in 27 fights. Smith has won 20 from 20, including beating Subriel Matias in New York in January - who inflicted Puello's only previous loss - to become world champion.

The 29-year-old had been due to fight mandatory challenger Puello four months sooner in June, but an injury to the Dominican Republic fighter resulted in a postponenment.

Smith, speaking to DAZN after retaining his title, said: "We knew what we were coming in for, he's a two-time world champion [and] look at the names he's beat.

"We knew it wasn't going to be a show, he was going to be an awkward opponent, but a champion has to do what he has to do.

"These are the best in the world and I'm proving why I'm number one now."

He added: "I got his rhythm early on. I think he respected my power, but, look, he's experienced.

"He's a lot more experienced than me, and that's what I'm gaining now. I switched off a little bit in the early rounds, but I did what a true champion did and win the last couple, so I'm very proud."

Sports.title: Alonso 'out-coached', 'petulant' Palmer and Penders howler: Chelsea's horror night
Sports.content:
They say bad things come in threes. That was certainly the case for Chelsea on a miserable evening at Stamford Bridge as they lost 2-0 to Tottenham and were described as "awful" by Gary Neville.

Spurs had won only one of their previous 34 Premier League visits to Chelsea but dominated Xabi Alonso's side from start to finish, with an own goal from Mike Penders and a stunning late strike from Mathys Tel securing a well-deserved win for Roberto De Zerbi's side.

To add to their woes, on an evening where the dismal weather matched their performance, Cole Palmer was sent off for a second bookable offence after already escaping a straight red card earlier in the game, having barged into Spurs midfielder Mateus Fernandes.

"Tottenham outplayed Chelsea. Out-coached, everything. None of us expected Tottenham to come here and win today, but after 10-15 mins, that confidence did start to grow," said Neville while on commentary, in a game that was also described as the worst performance of Alonso's short tenure so far.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Cole Palmer was shown a second yellow card and sent off

"Chelsea have been awful, really. On the ball, they've been well short. Nowhere near the level. I am stunned."

Chelsea started without a recognised striker after Joao Pedro was unexpectedly absent.

Both Danny Welbeck, who started as the striker in the 3-0 loss to Brentford when Joao Pedro was also out injured, and Estevao were on the bench. Chelsea didn't bring on Welbeck until the 88th minute when they were 2-0 down.

Neville added: "Welbeck must be thinking, 'How do I get a game here?' Disciplinary problems have cost him [Alonso] today, but I don't think that's the biggest problem.

Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso speaking to Sky Sports: “I feel for everyone.



"This is collective, this is a team thing.



"We are all disappointed, but we need to move on."

"The biggest problem is that Tottenham have come and outplayed them. They've made them look really ordinary.

"Where Tottenham have absolutely battered Chelsea is in midfield. Cole Palmer, [Morgan] Rogers, [Jordan] Henderson and [Moises] Caicedo have been able to get nowhere near. Spurs' midfield has run the game.

"They absolutely bossed the game. I usually say when it's bad weather and teams are getting pressed, knock it long. I think it's mad.

"But you could just see that Chelsea wouldn't be able to keep that pressure on. Tottenham's combinations and patterns in midfield were really good."

'Petulant' Palmer and Chelsea's frustration

Chelsea's frustrations, and Palmer's in particular, were clear throughout. After Fernandes deliberately handballing to stop him on the counter, Palmer confronted the Spurs midfielder after the whistle.

The England international barged into Fernandes, sparking a melee between the two sides. Sky Sports News understands the incident was checked and cleared by VAR John Brooks.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Should Palmer have seen a straight red earlier for shoving Mateus Fernandes?

"I think that could be a red. If this wasn't at Stamford Bridge, I think it's a red," Neville said at the time of the incident, which ended in only a yellow for Palmer.

Jamie Redknapp said the reaction was "petulant" and out of character for a player who is usually known for his cool and composed nature.

Just three minutes after Penders' own goal, the forward then caught Conor Gallagher late and was swiftly shown a second yellow by referee Chris Kavanagh.

"They started to lose their heads. It was frustration as they couldn't get near them," Redknapp continued. And that spread across the team as a whole, not just with their talisman Palmer.

Morgan Rogers was also booked after catching Gallagher, the same player who was the target of Palmer's second tackle, in an incident Neville believed could have reduced Chelsea to nine men.

"I think that's a red. I do," Neville added. "He's absolutely wellied him with no intent. That's ludicrous from Rogers. They have lost it. Xabi Alonso needs to get them off."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jamie Redknapp analyses Palmer’s red card and Morgan Rogers’ booking

'Monumental' error from Penders - but he's their only option

Penders' howler, punching the ball into his own net from a corner, came in his first start, replacing the injured Emiliano Martinez.

After falling behind 1-0, Chelsea unravelled. But with Martinez set to be sidelined for the foreseeable future after facial surgery following a jaw fracture against Everton, the goalkeeper will need to bounce back quickly ahead of facing Liverpool in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday, live on Sky Sports.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mike Penders punched the ball into his own net

"He made a monumental mistake; it's as simple as that. The ball comes in and where he goes wrong is that he comes with no authority," Redknapp said.

"He, to a certain extent, gets bullied. There is hesitation. It's hard. It has to become character building for him. He has to fight within himself.

"They will need to put their arm round him; he is going to play again next week.

"Of course you will make mistakes but it is how you handle it. He has to get on with it and show some character."

Chelsea sanctioned Robert Sanchez's loan move to Como after Martinez arrived from Aston Villa in the summer.

Their other option in goal against Spurs was 23-year-old Teddy Sharman-Lowe, who spent last season on loan at Bolton and has not made a competitive senior appearance for the Blues.

Gabriel Slonina remains at the club but has not been named in the squad since pre-season.

Sports.title: Hits and misses: De Zerbi's 'complete team' and 'genius' Emery impress
Sports.content:
Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from the Premier League match between Chelsea and Tottenham Hotspur.

Was this the result when Roberto De Zerbi truly started to turn Tottenham's miserable decline around? Was this the performance when he discovered how to get the best out of his £185m midfield signings? Was this when his players' personality and motivation changed?

"Why not?" said De Zerbi after Tottenham's 2-0 win over Chelsea. It was a "different Tottenham", he said.

"Not a different attitude. Different relationships with the players, different group."

Tottenham have been threatening to improve. They should have won at Manchester United. They beat Coventry at home as expected. But this was a proper test albeit against a Chelsea side also finding their way under a new head coach. Spurs stood up to it.

"Before Man Utd, we spoke a lot in a big, big meeting, removing the mask and speaking honestly, clearly in front of ourselves," said De Zerbi. "And from that moment, I think we changed something in ourselves.

"We want to improve, improve, improve, to be better game by game, week by week. I think we have suffered enough."

From the moment Spurs changed ends at kick-off, a decision home fans groaned at, they had Chelsea where they wanted them despite the relentless wind and rain in their faces.

Omar Marmoush's first-half miss threatened the same old story, but perhaps their luck is changing now too. Mike Penders' error was a gift, but one that was deserved. Spurs will also argue a big decision went against them before the own goal, when Cole Palmer barged into Mateus Fernandes' head.

Fernandes also delivered the corner that Penders punched in. The midfielder was at the heart of everything. Playing at the base of Spurs' midfield three, he was outstanding. He had the most touches, passes, successful tackles and successful dribbles of any player on the pitch. His performance typified an evolving Tottenham side.

"We are working to change the last part of the club's history," said De Zerbi and they are heading in the right direction.

David Richardson

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the Premier League match between Arsenal and Everton.

Arsenal's perceived over reliance on set pieces was used as a stick to beat them with last season as they scored 25 goals from deadball scenarios, excluding penalties, en route to lifting the Premier League title.

It is an ominous sign for the rest of the league, then, that 'Set Piece FC' are level on points with leaders Manchester City having just scored their first set-piece goal, excluding penalties, in their eighth match.

Mikel Arteta warns that Ezri Konsa's goal from a corner in the 2-0 win over Everton will "unlock" Arsenal from set-pieces moving forward.

What chance do the rest of the league have if this Arsenal side, that have found ways to win without set-pieces, have rediscovered their not so secret weapon? Brace yourself, you're going to be seeing a lot more of set-piece coach Nicolas Jover on your TV screens.

Zinny Boswell

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from the Premier League match between Aston Villa and Manchester City.

Nicolas Jackson has always been a striker who gives you plenty to like and plenty to scream at. The running, the movement, the willingness to stretch defences and make life miserable for centre-backs have never really been in doubt. It is what happens when the ball reaches his feet in front of goal that has tended to leave manager's tearing their hair out.

But Unai Emery appears to be working his magic again.

Image: Nicolas Jackson celebrates his match-winning goal

Jackson's double in Aston Villa's 2-1 win over Manchester City took his tally to seven goals in eight starts for the club. It's not what we usually expect from Jackson.

Villa weren't buying a goalscorer. They have acquired a forward who brings so much to Emery's attacking structure. Jackson runs the channels relentlessly, occupies defenders and creates space for those arriving around him. Centre-backs do not get a quiet afternoon when he is leading the line. Man City, and especially Marc Guehi, found that out.

That industry has always been there. The difference now is the end product.

Villa have a striker who could take them to some special places this season. The hard yards were never the problem. Now the goals are following, too.

Lewis Jones

There was a time when Gianluigi Donnarumma felt like a goalkeeper that was unbeatable. He was being talked about as one of the best in the world before he had even reached adulthood, making his Italy debut aged just 17 years and 189 days. That was 10 years ago.

His mistake in Aston Villa's 2-1 win over Manchester City was another reminder that there are cracks in the armour. Since the start of last season, no goalkeeper has made more errors leading to shots in the Premier League than Donnarumma, with seven. Three of those mistakes have resulted in goals.

That is a worrying trend for a goalkeeper operating at the very highest level. Errors happen, of course, but the frequency is becoming difficult to ignore.

There is an increasingly erratic element to his game with moments of uncertainty creeping into performances that once seemed defined by authority.

Perhaps the demands of English football are exposing weaknesses that were less obvious elsewhere. Perhaps it is simply a dip in form. Either way, City need their goalkeeper to be a source of security.

Lewis Jones

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from the Premier League match between Ipswich Town and Nottingham Forest.

Nottingham Forest are becoming the Premier League's most frustrating watch. Not because they are playing badly, but because they are doing almost everything right apart from the bit that matters most.

Their 1-1 draw at Ipswich was another case of dominance without the reward. Forest racked up 2.31 expected goals, won the shot count 17-7 and had enough opportunities to put this game to bed. Instead, Neco Williams' first-half strike was all they had to show for their superiority, allowing Ipswich to snatch a point.

This is becoming a worrying habit. No Premier League team has underperformed its expected goals tally more than Forest this season, scoring just six goals from chances worth 13.4 xG. That is a staggering shortfall and goes a long way towards explaining why they have managed just one win in eight games.

However, do not confuse poor finishing with poor football.

Forest rank sixth in the Premier League for expected goal difference, the measure of chances created minus those conceded. Opta's expected points model suggests they should have twice their current tally of six points. In other words, the underlying numbers paint the picture of a team performing considerably better than their results suggest.

Under an elite manager in Oliver Glasner, they are creating chances, controlling games and limiting opponents.

Forest are leaving points on the table. When their forwards finally start converting the opportunities their football deserves, they could be a very different proposition.

Lewis Jones

Sports.title: Knicks employees to get NBA championship rings after phishing email 'mistake'
Sports.content:
The New York Knicks have sought to clear up what they've labelled "misinformation" regarding the awarding of their NBA championship rings after employees received a phishing email posing as an opportunity to claim one.

The Athletic reported on Thursday that some employees received an email in September that said: "Your Employee Championship Ring is here". But those who clicked on the link in the email were informed that they had failed a phishing test and would have to attend a mandatory cybersecurity class.

A Madison Square Garden (MSG) spokesperson admitted on Friday that "using the rings as a lure to gain employees attention was an unfortunate mistake".

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the NBA Finals Game 5 match-up between the New York Knicks and San Antonio Spurs.

In a further statement on Saturday, MSG conceded that using an email regarding the selection of rings to train staffers about cybersecurity was a mistake, though "reminding our employees to protect our IP was not".

Having secured the Knicks' first title since 1973 last season, players were awarded their rings on Tuesday night before losing their season opener against LeBron James' Philadelphia 76ers.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the NBA match between the New York Knicks and the Philadelphia 76ers.

MSG added that more than 275 employees were already set to be gifted rings "in about 4-6 weeks", worth more than $3.7 million.

"There is a great deal of misinformation regarding the championship rings," the statement clarified. "The plan has always been to distribute more than 275 rings and jewelry to the people in the organization who were part of last season's success."

Sports.title: Alonso urges Cole Palmer ‘to learn’ from red card in Chelsea’s defeat to Spurs
Sports.content:
Xabi Alonso said that Cole Palmer must learn from his red card during Chelsea’s shock 2-0 defeat to Tottenham, who claimed their first win at Stamford Bridge since 2018 thanks to an own goal from Mike Penders and a late effort from Mathys Tel.

Spurs, who had won on one of their previous 34 trips to west London, were already 1-0 up when Palmer earned a second yellow card for catching Conor Gallagher with a late tackle. The playmaker could have been sent off earlier – his first booking came during a clash with Mateus Fernandes – and Alonso agreed that this could be an important lesson for the 24-year-old.

“Absolutely,” Chelsea’s manager said. “I haven’t seen them [back] on TV but as far as I have been told probably he [the referee] got it right. We need to have this maturity to deal with difficult moments. When you have conceded for 1-0, still probably it was 15-20 minutes to go. I need to check the action to talk with Cole but it is one to learn for the future for sure.”

View image in fullscreen Cole Palmer clashes with Mateus Fernandes, earning his first yellow card. Photograph: Isabel Infantes/Reuters

Alonso said there are no wider concerns with Palmer’s character, even though Chelsea’s No 10 could have been sent off against Everton last weekend too. “Today, for sure, yes, but it is not a concern,” Alonso said. “It is a moment to keep calm, a moment to keep mature, for everyone.”

Chelsea struggled without João Pedro and do not know when the forward will return after picking up an unspecified injury in training on Friday. “He has a lot of fluid,” Alonso said. “He felt it yesterday and we need to wait to do the test and to know the whole seriousness of the injury.”

Alonso defended Penders after the goalkeeper punched a corner into his own net on his full Premier League debut. “We win, we lose together,” he said. “We support Mike and we support the rest of the team. He will learn from that.”
