Ghana News.title: Gender Minister calls for stronger Canada–Africa ties to boost women’s economic opportunities
Ghana News.content:
The Minister for Gender, Children and Social Protection, Dr Agnes Naa Momo Lartey, has called for stronger cooperation between Canada and African countries to improve women’s access to finance, markets and economic opportunities.

She made the call during a panel discussion at the Canada–Africa Policy Roundtable and Reception in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, held under the theme, “Building Inclusive African Economies: Advancing Canada–Africa Cooperation on Finance, Trade and Economic Opportunity.”

The engagement formed part of the Egumeni Dialogue, a platform for policy discussions and partnerships between Africa and its international partners.

Dr Lartey stressed that building inclusive economies requires more than increased investment and expanded trade, noting that structural barriers continue to limit women’s full participation in economic activities.

She acknowledged Canada’s support for initiatives in Ghana aimed at improving women’s economic opportunities.

These include the Making Trade Work for Women in West Africa project, the Enhancing Market Participation and Learning Opportunities for Young Women (EMPLOY) project, and the Climate Resilient Livelihoods for Women in Northern Ghana (CLIMB) project.

The Minister outlined three key areas for further cooperation: expanding access to affordable finance and investment for women-owned businesses, strengthening women’s participation in regional and international trade, and investing in skills development, technology, childcare, social protection and safe workplaces.

She also highlighted the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) as an opportunity to connect women-owned businesses to larger markets and regional value chains.

However, she emphasised the need to support women entrepreneurs to meet product standards, obtain certification, adopt digital commerce and establish connections with buyers and investors to take advantage of the opportunities offered by the continental market.

Dr Lartey further noted that women’s economic empowerment requires an integrated approach that combines financial support with skills development, market access and measures to address structural inequalities.

She said such interventions were essential to helping women sustain their businesses and benefit from emerging economic opportunities.

The Minister reaffirmed Ghana’s commitment to partnerships that bring together finance, trade, technical expertise and investment to support the growth of women-owned businesses, create jobs and contribute to national and continental economic development.

Ghana News.title: Mahama links Africa’s conflicts to struggle over natural resources
Ghana News.content:
President John Mahama says the struggle for control of Africa’s natural resources and the profits from their extraction are central to the continent’s security crises, warning that powerful interests benefit from prolonged instability.

Addressing the 12th Tana High-Level Forum on Peace in Africa in Bahir Dar, Ethiopia, President Mahama said Africa, the President said the continent risks remaining vulnerable if its leaders fail to take greater control of their resources and determine their own security priorities.

He said “Let me be clear, Africa is not an empty chessboard for foreign powers to play their games. We are not spectators,” he said.

“But unless we consciously decide to take up the pen and write our own script, someone else will write it for us, and we will not like how the story ends.”

President Mahama said the importance of African minerals to the global green energy transition and digital economy should give the continent greater bargaining power, but communities endowed with these resources often bear the consequences of exploitation without enjoying the benefits.

He argued that sovereignty must go beyond political independence and membership of international institutions.

“Real sovereignty means having the administrative, legal, and economic power to govern your strategic assets, negotiate fair terms, and ensure the wealth beneath our people's feet actually puts food on their tables,” he said. He added that anything less amounted to “cosmetic independence that masks economic subjugation.”

He says African leaders must look beyond weapons proliferation and military operations to confront the political and economic interests that sustain conflicts across the continent.

“The real disease is mostly in the arena of political economy,” President Mahama said when presenting the 2026 State of Peace and Security in Africa Report at the 12th Tana High-Level Forum on Peace in Africa in Bahir Dar, Ethiopia.

He challenged leaders to examine who controls natural resources, who benefits financially from their extraction and whose political and financial interests are better served by continued instability than lasting peace.

“In every single theatre of conflict across this continent today, if you want to understand why guns are firing, do not start by counting the rifles,” he said.

“Ask three basic questions, who controls the resource? Who cashes the cheque from its extraction? And whose political and financial fortunes are better served by perpetual chaos than by stable peace?”

President Mahama cited Sudan, the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), Somalia and Mozambique as examples of how resource competition, governance failures and economic marginalisation contribute to insecurity.

In Sudan, he said, the battle lines were drawn as much around gold extraction sites as around Khartoum.

In eastern DRC, he linked the resurgence and entrenchment of the M23 group to coltan, cobalt and the global competition for minerals needed for the green energy transition.

He also attributed the continued presence of Al-Shabaab in Somalia partly to governance failures that have created openings for the group to exploit.

In Mozambique’s Cabo Delgado region, he said, the area’s substantial gas wealth has not translated into meaningful benefits for local young people, who instead viewed it as another source of marginalisation.

“These are not separate, random brushfires. They are symptoms of a single, continent-wide firestorm,” he said.

Ghana News.title: CAGG demands retraction, apology from GoldBod CEO over alleged illegal mining remarks
Ghana News.content:
The Chief Executive Officer of the Gold Board (GoldBod), Sammy Gyamfi

The Ghana Coalition Against Galamsey (CAGG) has called on the Office of the Attorney-General to investigate the Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod) over statements it claims encouraged artisanal miners to operate without licences, provided they avoid forest reserves and river bodies.

In a press release dated October 24, 2026, the coalition condemned the reported remarks, describing them as unlawful and reckless, and warning that they could undermine efforts to combat illegal mining, popularly known as galamsey.

CAGG argued that Ghana's mining laws do not exempt miners from licensing requirements based on the location of their operations.

Citing Section 99(2)(a) of the Minerals and Mining Act, 2006 (Act 703), as amended by Act 995 of 2019, the coalition said anyone who undertakes mining without a licence granted by the Minister commits an offence.

It further cited Section 99, arguing that anyone who commands, instigates, employs or facilitates others to engage in illegal mining could face the same penalties as the illegal miner.

According to the coalition, offenders could face fines ranging from GH¢120,000 to GH¢180,000 and imprisonment of between 15 and 25 years, or both.

The coalition therefore wants the GoldBod CEO to immediately retract the alleged statement and issue an unqualified apology to the Ghanaian public.

It has also urged President John Dramani Mahama, the Minister for Lands and Natural Resources, and the Minerals Commission to publicly reaffirm that mining without a licence is illegal, regardless of where the activity takes place.

CAGG further called on the Attorney-General's Office to investigate the matter for possible abetment of illegal mining, insisting that no individual should be exempt from the law.

Beyond the legal implications, the coalition warned that the reported remarks could expose farmers and landowners to encroachment on their lands.

It has consequently called on the Ministry of National Security, the Ghana Police Service and the Ministry of the Interior to strengthen protection for farmers and landowners and establish rapid-response channels for reporting encroachment.

The group is also demanding a clear national plan to protect farmlands, including legal safeguards for agricultural lands, mapping and registration of farms, support for vulnerable farmers seeking to document their land rights, and compensation and restoration for those whose lands have been destroyed.

CAGG said GoldBod was established to formalise and regulate artisanal mining, not to encourage unlicensed operations.

It warned that normalising mining without licences would weaken the regulatory framework intended to distinguish legal small-scale mining from illegal mining.

The coalition comprises civil society organisations, professional associations, environmental advocacy groups and other stakeholders.

Ghana News.title: GH¢10,000 injection: Assafuah boosts Black Challenge’s World Cup campaign
Ghana News.content:
The Member of Parliament for Old Tafo, Vincent Ekow Assafuah, has donated GH¢10,000 to Ghana’s national amputee football team, the Black Challenge, as part of efforts to boost their morale ahead of the 2026 WAFF Amputee Football World Cup in Mexico.

Mr Assafuah made the donation during a visit to the team at their hotel in Achimota, Accra, where he also presented cartons of water and soft drinks to support the players.

The visit served as a show of solidarity and encouragement to the team as they intensify preparations for the international tournament, scheduled to take place in San Juan de los Lagos, Mexico, from November 13 to 22, 2026.

Mr Assafuah commended the players for their determination and commitment to representing Ghana on the international stage, stressing the importance of supporting their efforts to bring honour to the country.

He also pledged to help mobilise additional support for the team in the coming days, urging other stakeholders to contribute to the Black Challenge’s World Cup campaign.

The donation comes as the team continues preparations for the tournament, where Ghana will be seeking to make a strong impression against some of the world’s best amputee football nations.

The gesture highlights the importance of collective support from individuals, corporate organisations and public institutions in helping the Black Challenge achieve their ambitions and proudly fly Ghana’s flag in Mexico.

Ghana News.title: Nayi Alhassan retains NDC Tema North chairmanship as Salman Faris wins secretary
Ghana News.content:
Nayi Alhassan, popularly known as Ngbagu, has retained his position as National Democratic Congress (NDC) chairman for the Tamale North Constituency after securing 518 votes in the party’s constituency executive elections.

He defeated Salifu Mohammed, who polled 352 votes, and Abdul Halim Wayo Issahaku, who obtained 147 votes.

In the race for constituency secretary, Salman Faris Inusah emerged victorious with 598 votes, beating Baba Alhassan, popularly known as Mr Law, who secured 423 votes.

Mutala Hussein won the vice-chairmanship position with 476 votes, defeating Mohammed Nurideen Iddrisu, popularly known as Zaachi, who obtained 428 votes. Abdulai Abdul Rahaman received 107 votes.

Iddrisu Mohammed Nurideen won the deputy secretary position with 519 votes, narrowly beating Salman Iddrisu, who polled 502 votes.

For the treasurer position, Mateen Mohammed secured 639 votes, while Alhassan Adam, popularly known as Sahanaa, won the deputy treasurer position with 597 votes.

Baba Tahiru was elected communications officer after polling 774 votes to defeat Yussif Tikuma, who obtained 246 votes. Abdullah Abdul Rafiu, popularly known as Ras King, won the deputy communications officer position with 659 votes.

Results for other positions

In the organiser race, Mohammed A. Issahak emerged winner with 424 votes. He was followed by Issahaku Abdulai, popularly known as Captain America, with 279 votes, and Issahaku Alidu Bako, known as CR7, with 212 votes. Alhassan Abubakar, popularly known as Mr Abu, polled 88 votes, while Issah Zakaria Sasqo received nine votes.

Nashiru Iddrisu, popularly known as Prince Nash, won the deputy organiser position with 500 votes. Abdul Wadud Mohammed received 289 votes, Alhassan Abdul Latif Napari secured 123 votes, and Abdul Mumin Seidu, known as Hon Kporo, polled 106 votes.

Alidu Mohammed won the youth organiser position with 99 votes, ahead of Issahaku Amin, who received 16 votes. Husaifa Alhassan won deputy youth organiser with 82 votes, defeating Abdallah Jalil Yussif, who polled 32 votes.

Ayishatu Abdulai Yahaya emerged women's organiser with 63 votes, beating Ruhiya Adam, who secured 48 votes.

In the deputy women's organiser contest, Suweiba Iddrisu Alhassan won with 37 votes. Diana Alhassan obtained 35 votes, Memuna Sumani received 30 votes, and Sadia Abubakar polled eight votes.

Alhassan Mohammed Sadat secured 381 votes in the treasurer race, finishing behind winner Mateen Mohammed, who obtained 639 votes. In the deputy treasurer contest, Zakaria Abass, popularly known as Oly, received 423 votes, losing to Alhassan Adam, who secured 597 votes.

For deputy communications officer, Abdulai Ibrahim Danaa polled 187 votes, while Tahiru Lansah received 174 votes, both behind winner Abdullah Abdul Rafiu, who secured 659 votes.

In the Zongo Caucus election, Adizatu Suleman won with 555 votes, defeating Sulemana Ahmed, who polled 350 votes, and Amadu Mohammed, who obtained 166 votes.

The elections form part of the NDC’s nationwide constituency-level reorganisation exercise aimed at electing executives to coordinate party activities and strengthen grassroots structures ahead of the 2028 general elections

Ghana News.title: Ellen White Foundation brings free breast cancer screening to Bono East police women
Ghana News.content:
In a heartwarming display of commitment to women's health, the Ellen White Sustainable Foundation, in partnership with the Awat Foundation and the Police Ladies Association, has provided free breast cancer screening to nearly 100 female police officers across the Bono East Region.

The screening exercise, held at the Techiman Divisional Police Command, formed part of efforts to promote early detection and awareness of breast cancer among women in uniform.

The programme was held under the theme: "Investing in Women's Health, Investing in Stronger Communities."

Mrs. Ellen White Opoku, founder of the Ellen White Sustainable Foundation and a 2023 Joy Impact Makers Award recipient, said the initiative was born out of the need to reach officers who cannot easily access health facilities due to their busy schedules.

"This exercise is to help bring the screening to the doorstep of the police, who are unable to attend to health facilities for the same due to their busy work schedules," she noted.

Police Ladies Association Weighs In

ASP Beatrice Okrah, Crime Officer for the Jema District Police Command and a regional executive member of the Police Ladies Association, commended the organizers and encouraged women to prioritize their health.

She said the time had come for women to own up and get themselves screened to know their statuses and be treated when diagnosed with the condition.

"The time has come for women to own up and get themselves screened to know their statuses and be treated when diagnosed with the condition," she stated.

ASP Okrah added that the awareness talk had been helpful in creating awareness about what the condition is, equipping participants with knowledge to share with colleagues and family members.

"The talk has been helpful in creating awareness about what the condition is," she noted.

Service to Support Officers Diagnosed

In a reassuring message to personnel, ASP Okrah disclosed that officers found to have the cancer will be taken care of by the Police Service.

She explained that the welfare of officers remains a priority, and those diagnosed through the screening will receive the necessary support and care from the Service.

A Community Investment

The event reflects a growing push to make healthcare accessible to women in security services, who often sacrifice personal wellness for public duty. By investing in the health of these officers, organizers say the ripple effect will be felt across entire communities.

The Ellen White Sustainable Foundation has indicated its commitment to sustaining such initiatives, with plans to reach more districts in the Bono East Region and beyond.

Ghana News.title: Ghana’s U-15 Boys thrash Uzbekistan 4-1 as Abdul Aziz Issah and Jerry Owusu hit brace each
Ghana News.content:
The National U-15 Boys team made a flying start to the FIFA U-15 World Cup and Festival with an emphatic 4-1 victory over Uzbekistan in their opening Group W match on Saturday.

Abdul Aziz Issah and Jerry Owusu were the heroes for Ghana, scoring a brace each to secure all three points in Azerbaijan.

Ghana dominated proceedings from the blast of the whistle, showing flair, composure and attacking intent against their Asian opponents.

Aziz Issah opened the scoring before doubling Ghana's advantage, while Jerry Owusu added two more goals to put the game beyond the reach of Uzbekistan, who managed a consolation strike late in the game.

The win gives Ghana a strong start in Group W, which also includes Myanmar, Guam, Bahamas and Kazakhstan.

Ghana will next face Myanmar and Guam on Sunday, before wrapping up the group phase against Bahamas and Kazakhstan on Monday.

The FIFA U-15 World Cup and Festival, part of FIFA's Talent Development Scheme, is aimed at giving every talent a chance to showcase their skills on the world stage.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: How have Democrats’ policies shifted since the last major US election?
World.content:
From trans rights to Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza, the party’s candidates have responded to voter shifts on a slew of issues.

Share How have Democrats’ policies shifted since the last major US election? on social media

Two years after United States voters delivered a stunning rebuke of the country’s Democratic Party by electing Republican President Donald Trump to a second nonconsecutive term, some of the party’s midterm candidates are reassessing stances on a host of hot-button issues.

Whether they have dialled it back on issues like transgender rights or ramped up efforts to oppose Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza, Democrats in some of the toughest midterm battleground races are responding to voter concerns – or even breaking outright with party leadership.

Those shifts have resonated with some voters, while others have been alienated as the party tries to find its footing in Trump’s second term and wrestle away control of both houses of Congress from Republicans.

But in the time since Trump defeated former Vice President Kamala Harris in 2024, Democratic divisions have only grown deeper. Establishment and self-described moderates within the party have struggled to hold back a rising tide of progressive populism as voters increasingly demand stronger, bolder policies.

That movement, powered by groups like the Democratic Socialists of America, has forced a reckoning over what it means to be a Democrat in Trump’s second term, leading to significant differences among candidates on policies that often depend on where they are running.

Here’s how – and why – the party has shifted:

Democrats’ shifting views on Israel

The most notable shift among Democrats has, arguably, been on Israel.

Three years after Israel launched its genocidal war in Gaza and killed more than 74,000 Palestinians following Hamas’s October 7, 2023, attacks, polls have suggested that Americans hold increasingly negative views on Israeli military actions.



A Pew Research Center survey conducted earlier this year suggested that 60 percent of US adults had an unfavourable opinion of Israel. That number is significantly higher – 80 percent – among US Democrats.

In response, some longtime Democratic supporters of Israel – including Senator Chris Coons, who is likely to chair the Senate Foreign Relations Committee if Democrats retake control of the Senate next month – have shifted, as voters, especially younger ones, demand greater accountability from the US ally.

The moderate Delaware Democrat told Politico in an interview this month that he wants a “thorough reexamination” of the US-Israeli relationship and is even willing to impose sanctions on Israel’s prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu.

It is a marked change in tone after Harris rejected calls to feature a Palestinian American speaker at the 2024 Democratic National Convention in Chicago.

Earlier this year, 40 Democratic senators voted in support of a motion that disapproved proposed military sales to Israel. Only seven Democratic senators voted with Republicans to block it.

But as a new Congress may include even more progressive voices demanding the US rethink its relationship with Israel, those calls would likely be met with stiff resistance from some in the Democratic leadership, including Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer.

The New York Democrat, who would likely become majority leader if Democrats retake the Senate, has said that the US “commitment to Israel’s security and defense must be ironclad”.

Have Democrats changed their positions on transgender rights?

Following years of attacks from Republicans, Democrats in tightly contested US House or Senate races have downplayed – or outright dismissed – support for the transgender community, mostly when it comes to the participation of transgender students in school sports.

In Ohio, Democratic Representative Marcy Kaptur ran an  featuring her saying, “Boys should not play in girls’ sports”. And in North Carolina, Representative Don Davis released a television commercial in which the Democrat says there “should always be a safe and fair space for women and girls in sports”.

Next door in South Carolina, Democratic Senate candidate Annie Andrews, a doctor, said in a newly released  that she opposes “biological men playing in women’s sports”.

Trump’s return to the White House was fuelled, in part, by a now-famous  in the 2024 campaign that highlighted Harris’s support for transgender Americans.



“Kamala is for they/them,” a narrator said in the , referring to gender neutral pronouns used by some in the transgender and nonbinary community. “President Trump is for you.”

But the reassessment of transgender rights after the commercial’s airing is not taking place in every part of the party.

On Thursday at a “Students vs Billionaires” town hall in Portland, Maine, Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez addressed concerns from a transgender college student who told the New York progressive that they felt “abandoned” by Democrats.

“They’re wrong”, Ocasio-Cortez said about some members of her party. “First and foremost, I want to just let you know how shameful and sorry I am that there are people out there that scare so easily after an election”.

The congresswoman added, “The moment you compromise the rights of a trans person in America, you compromise the rights of every citizen.”

What has changed on immigration and border security?

During former US President Joe Biden’s term, Democrats encountered near-daily attacks from Republicans on the country’s immigration system.

US Customs and Border Protection (CBP) recorded more than 8 million encounters at the US-Mexico border between 2021 and 2025, fuelling concerns among some voters that the Biden administration had ignored the issue.

In Texas’s closely watched Senate race, candidate James Talarico has positioned himself as a “border security Democrat”, advocating for stronger border enforcement and comprehensive immigration reform.

Third Way, a US-based organisation that pushes for moderate policies, said stances like Talarico’s resonate better with voters because they have taken a proactive, rather than a reactionary approach.

“I remember very clearly when Harris came out and spoke at the DNC in 2024; she… said we need order at the border and to have a strong immigration system”, Third Way’s senior political adviser, Lucas Holtz, told Al Jazeera.

“The problem is, after that, the Harris campaign really did not stick with that line in the sand… They stopped taking a stand on these issues, and more voters thought that she was too far to the left.”

“[Talarico] is making the case in a lot of his ads that the Biden administration failed on securing the border… It’s putting Republicans on their back foot in some of these races.”

But among progressives, Trump’s response to the nation’s immigration issue has also prompted a strong swing to the left.

After several high-profile incidents earlier this year – including federal immigration agents in Minneapolis, Minnesota, shooting dead US citizens Renee Good and Alex Pretti – calls to abolish, or drastically overhaul, US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) have gained momentum.

Left-leaning political groups and politicians have united behind a message of “abolish ICE”, which would dismantle the federal agency and end its enforcement authority.



Do Democrats support Medicare for All?

As cost-of-living issues remain paramount for voters, Democrats of all stripes have coalesced behind the need for more government intervention in the country’s healthcare system.

But how exactly the party addresses rising medical costs remains up for debate.

Some progressives, including Michigan Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed, have championed policies like Medicare for All, which would expand the nation’s federal health insurance programme for seniors so all US citizens would be guaranteed healthcare.

Others running in more conservative states, like Andrews, have called for the return of Affordable Care Act subsidies that lapsed during Trump’s second term, as well as limits on health insurance companies’ profits.

Polling released by the independent health organisation KFF suggested that 66 percent of US adults now support Medicare for All, a 13-point increase from October 2020.

“Everybody’s going to have their own approach to this, but by and large, all Democrats want to move to a universal healthcare system in the best way possible”, Holtz said.

“We’re in agreement that we need to do better than what the Trump administration has done.”

World.title: Brazil’s Lula, Bolsonaro draw thousands to election-eve rallies
World.content:
The pivotal run-off will determine whether Brazilians stick with their left-wing leader or shift towards the right.

Brazil’s presidential candidates Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and Flavio Bolsonaro have rallied thousands of supporters in a final show of campaign strength in advance of the country’s closely contested run-off election.

Donning a red hat, Lula addressed hundreds of supporters at Rio de Janeiro’s Copacabana Beach on Saturday, waving a Brazilian flag from a campaign truck as crowds gathered on the final day of campaigning.

“The people must choose either someone who kisses the national flag or someone who kisses the American flag”, the 80-year-old told the crowd as he referenced his opponent’s ties to US President Donald Trump.

Lula is seeking a fourth, non-consecutive term in Sunday’s run-off, which will task Brazilians with determining whether to stick with their incumbent left-wing leader or join a broader regional shift towards the right.

Bolsonaro, a senator and son of former far-right President Jair Bolsonaro, secured 47 percent of the vote in the first round, narrowly ahead of Lula’s 45 percent.

Recent polling shows Lula and the younger Bolsonaro remain about even on the eve of the pivotal election.

A CNT/MDA survey released on Saturday revealed Bolsonaro would receive 46.3 percent of the vote compared ⁠with 45 percent for the left-wing ⁠Lula. Last week, ⁠the poll showed a slightly closer race with Bolsonaro leading ⁠Lula 46.8 percent to ⁠45.9 percent.



The poll’s margin of error was 2.2 ‌percentage ‌points.

On Saturday, Bolsonaro’s supporters, including hundreds of motorcyclists wearing Brazil’s yellow national football shirts, gathered in the southeastern state of Minas Gerais.

One of those supporters, Ebert Dorigo, accused Lula’s Workers’ Party (PT) of encouraging dependence on government welfare, arguing a change in direction was needed for the country.

“The values we uphold are nation and family. Our country is divided today because, due to welfare-based policies, some people … haven’t grasped that improvement and achievement come only through hard work,” he told the news agency AFP.

The bitter campaign has exposed deep divisions over economic policy, crime and Brazil’s political future, which Bolsonaro has pledged to tackle with hundreds of thousands of more spots in prison and cuts to government spending.

His father, who served as president from 2019 to 2022, is serving a 27-year prison sentence for attempting a coup after losing that year’s election to Lula.

The two candidates struck a calmer tone during their final debate on Friday, although they traded accusations over the country’s economic difficulties and their respective records.

For some voters, however, the choice has been a difficult one.

“If there were any other candidate, that would be a better option,” Gabriela Ribeiro Viana, an event organiser, told AFP. “But we’re stuck choosing between the worst, the horrible, and the lesser evil”.

World.title: Brazil’s candidates hold final rallies before knife-edge run off
World.content: President Lula da Silva rallied in Sao Paulo and Flavio Bolsonaro in Minas Gerais, on the eve of Sunday’s runoff election. The candidates are now polling at 50% each, according to a Datafolha poll.

World.title: Iran blames US for deal failure, urges new try amid fear of new attacks
World.content:
Share Iran blames US for deal failure, urges new try amid fear of new attacks on social media

Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian has blamed Washington for the unravelling of an interim deal aimed at ending the war with the United States and Israel, amid growing fears that the fighting could resume imminently.

In comments broadcast by Iranian Press TV on Saturday, But Pezeshkian also said that both sides should return to the deal and “conclude it”.

His remarks come amid growing fears that military action could resume as soon as this weekend, after US President Donald Trump said on Friday that he “may do another little Epic Fury”, using the codename of the US-Israeli war against Iran that started on February 28.

Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) has warned that even limited strikes would trigger a response “several times greater”, according to comments reported by the semi-official Fars News Agency.

Iranian Armed Forces Chief of Staff Ali Abdollahi said on Saturday that the US military would not be allowed in the Gulf “under any circumstances and at any time”. Abdollahi said Trump could only “dream” of seeing US forces enter the Gulf, adding that he would take his dream to the grave.

Trump has suggested he could take further military action against Iran, while Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has said he remains committed to overthrowing the country’s government.

Both leaders face elections, with Israelis set to choose their next government on Tuesday. Meanwhile, Trump’s Republican Party faces crucial midterm elections on November 3, with Democrats potentially winning control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate. Such an outcome would be a major blow to Trump, who still has more than two years left in his final term in the White House.

Iranian government spokesperson Fatemeh Mohajerani said on Saturday that Tehran would not “wait for permission to defend itself”, adding that the country “seeks peace but will respond to any aggression with severe consequences”.



“Our position is clear: we do not flee from dialogue for peace, and we do not hesitate in defending the country. Those who harbour the illusion of destroying Iran must correct their calculations,” Mohajerani wrote in a memo.

Her comments came as Iranian judiciary chief Gholamhossein Mohseni Ejei met Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei. The pair discussed how to tackle corruption and pursue compensation for Iranians affected by the US-Israeli war, among other issues.

Khamenei replaced his father as supreme leader after the latter was assassinated during the opening strikes of the war on February 28. He has not been seen in public since assuming the position in early March.

Parliament Speaker and chief negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf was reported to have met Khamenei earlier this week.

World.title: Houthis launch attacks on Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s Aden
World.content:
Houthi fighters have launched a series of attacks on targets in Saudi Arabia and the seat of Yemen’s internationally recognised government in Aden.

In a Facebook post on Saturday, the Yemeni government’s Transport Ministry denounced what it described as the Houthis’ targeting of Aden International Airport with two ballistic missiles, calling it the “fourth such attack this month”.

The airport attacks pose “a threat to the safety of civil aviation” and have “humanitarian and economic repercussions for citizens” who rely on it, the ministry warned.

Yemeni authorities said that the coastguard headquarters and a second building were also hit.

The Houthis claimed attacks on the al-Nasr camp and Aden’s naval military base.

Yemen’s army said a Houthi missile killed three people when it malfunctioned and fell on a family home in Houthi-held Sanaa on Friday. The army said it was one of a number of missile malfunctions seen in recent weeks by the Iran-backed group.

Houthi-run Al-Masirah TV said on Saturday that Saudi coalition air strikes killed several civilians in Sanaa and in the port city of Hodeidah. The claim could not be verified and Riyadh has not commented on the alleged raids.

Saudi attacks

Also on Saturday, Saudi Arabia’s civil defence said on X that the Houthis had launched two ballistic missiles towards Mecca and Medina, warning of “the fall of shrapnel” following their interception.

Images shared on X by the Saudi Press Agency appeared to show a large, blackened missile-shaped object that had landed somewhere in Saudi Arabia.

Jasem Mohamed Albudaiwi, Secretary-General of the Gulf Cooperation Council, described the Houthi attacks as “heinous”, which embody “a blatant disregard for the lives and security of civilians” in a statement shared on Saturday.



The Houthis said the claim that they targeted the two cities – the holiest in Islam – was a “huge lie”. They said their targets were three Saudi airports, oil infrastructure, and an airbase.

The Houthis have persistently targeted Saudi energy infrastructure and airports across the country with long-range strikes since a fragile ceasefire agreed in 2022 fell apart in July.

Fighting rages

Intense fighting is continuing on Yemen’s front lines as the Houthis battle forces of the internationally recognised government for control of key areas.

On Saturday, Yemeni army spokesman Colonel Majed Abdullah al-Nazili said that government forces had carried out more than 700 “targeting operations” over the last 24 hours across Yemen, “neutralising” 300 Houthi fighters and disabling military vehicles.

Al Jazeera could not independently verify those figures.

Operations targeted field command centres, Houthi gatherings, weapons depots, and supply lines in Taiz, where intense clashes have been ongoing for days, the spokesman added.
