The competition attracted 157 entries from musicians, songwriters, vocalists, music producers and other creative talents, with 20 entries selected for cash prizes following an assessment by a panel of judges.

Princess Ndidiamaka Okafor came second with Peter Mbah Bụ Agụ, winning ₦1 million, while Kelechi Obeta, popularly known as Kelycool, placed third with Ndi Enugu Onye Ka Unu Ge-eso Na’azụ?, winning ₦750,000.

Ejike Okonu took fourth position with Aafụm Onye Kwerụm Nkwa Merụ Mee, winning ₦600,000, while Solomon Chukwuebuka Ojobor came fifth with It’s Time for Us to Reward Our Governor Peter Mbah, winning ₦500,000.

The next five winners, each to receive ₦250,000, are Blessing Okolo Ogadimma, whose Enugu Na Ihe Ọma Abia placed sixth; Ijeoma Agbo, with Ndi Enugu Kunie Nụ, Nke Ọchiri Achi Dụ Anyi Mma, in seventh position; Chizoba Okorie, whose Ndụ B’anyi N’Oruwo placed eighth; Hon. Esther Ugwuefi, with Onyeze, in ninth position; and Maduekwe MaryJane Chinasa, popularly known as Jane C, whose Okwute Ndigbo Binie placed tenth.

Ten additional entries were selected for consolation prizes of ₦100,000 each. They are APC – Ebe Esere Aziza by Ejike Okonu; Peter Mbah Chant by Shepherdman Iyioku; Peter Mbah Chirụ Gaba by Patience Nnamani; Peter Mbah Makwarụ Ụzọ by Princess Chinwe Nnamoko; Peter Mbah Bụ Onye Nke Anyi, Omeru K’Okwuru by Ijeoma Agbo; Ogbom Eze Kam Kamanụ Gu Oo by Mrs. Martha Chidiebere Ugwu; Peter Mbah Carry Go by Mokwe Kingsley Chidiebere; Onye Ge-eme Enugu State Ka Ọdi Mma Ọzọ? by Stanley Ugwu; Governor Peter Mbah Is Good to Go by Destiny Wonder Kids; and APC, Ebe Esere Aziza, Ka Anyi Zapụ Ụbiam N’Enugu by Hon. Sunday Chinemeze Ezugwu.

The competition, announced in July, was designed to discover and promote home-grown musical talents and encourage creative expressions of the achievements, vision and developmental programmes of the Enugu State Governor, Dr. Peter Ndubuisi Mbah, while mobilising support for his re-election in the February 6, 2027 governorship election.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The entries were assessed on originality, creativity, lyrical content, musical quality, memorability and overall campaign appeal.

The organisers commended all participants for their creativity and enthusiasm, noting that the selected jingles could be deployed for publicity, campaign and mobilisation activities by the organisers and other authorised pro-Peter Mbah and pro-APC support groups, in accordance with the published competition rules.

The competition was jointly coordinated by Dan Nwomeh, Senior Special Assistant to the Governor on Mainstream Media, and Hon. Tony Okonkwo, State Coordinator of the Tomorrow Is Here Movement.

The organisers said the date of the award ceremony would be communicated to all the winners.

World.title: Six players secure scholarships as Ajayi Elebire basketball camp ends
World.content:
The fifth edition of the Ajayi Elebire Elite Basketball Camp ended in Ado Ekiti, Ekiti State, on Friday, with six players securing scholarships and the state’s Commissioner of Police, Michael Falade, praising the organisers for providing opportunities for young people.

The four-day camp, which began with trials in Lagos, brought together more than 40 players selected from across Nigeria to compete for scholarship opportunities and improve their skills under the guidance of coaches from Nigeria and the United States.

The programme ended with an All-Star game at the Ekitikete Pavilion in Ado Ekiti.

Mr Falade, who attended the closing activities, said the initiative could help keep young people away from crime by engaging them in productive activities.

“If you look at the rate of people that are involved in crime, they are youths, and for engaging them in this sport like this, at least you have taken them off the streets,” he said.

“And when somebody is engaged, you can never do otherwise; you have to do the right thing. Secondly, this is providing work because when you have the foundation, then there is no way you can miss it.”

Coaches praise players

Scott Adubato, one of the American coaches invited for the programme and a former coach of the camp organiser, Olalekan Ajayi, said the event gave talented players an opportunity to improve their game.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He said the coaching team worked with the players throughout the camp, introducing them to different principles of basketball and preparing them for the final game.

“The players were prepared every day. We worked on the training. We did everything we needed to teach them different principles of the game. They were very receptive. They played hard to the last game. And I think they earned everything that they earned, especially the MVP and the All-Star players. So, a thumbs up to the organisers,” he said.

Ajayi recounts journey

Mr Ajayi said the camp was organised in honour of his father, Ajayi Elebire, adding that his own basketball journey began with a similar camp through which he was discovered.

He thanked those who supported the initiative and said it was designed to help talented Nigerian players access opportunities that might otherwise be difficult to find locally.

“Every year we come here, we impact the lives of these Nigerian kids. We have, you know, a lot of talented players; we have five scholarships guaranteed. The sky is the limit. And this is a record call. The NBBF refused to do what they’re supposed to do to get the house in order and do what is good for Nigerians.

“People like me and the rest of them, we’re going to keep coming from America and get these players out of this country. To give them an opportunity that they refuse to provide for them.”

Six players secured automatic scholarships at this year’s camp. They are Ejirinade Neuman, Igwe Ikechukwu, Muiz Salami, Felix Jackson, Destiny Eze and Lucky Anyaorah.

The scholarships are expected to give the selected players opportunities to further develop their basketball careers.

World.title: NDC says 80% of its candidates couldn’t afford nomination forms, blames APC
World.content:
The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has said 80 per cent of its 2027 candidates could not afford the party’s expression of interest forms.

The NDC spokesperson, Osa Director, in a statement on Saturday said the candidates could not afford the party’s forms due to the high level of hunger and poverty in Nigeria.

Mr Director suggested that the inability of the candidates to buy the expression of interest forms affected the NDC’s finances.

He blamed the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) for the hunger and poverty in the country.

“Our finances would have been more robust.

“However, contrary to speculations in the public domain, and due to the level of poverty, hunger and deprivation in the country occasioned by the rudderless APC and its amorphous economic policies, about 80% of our candidates could not afford the Expression of Interest forms,” he said.

“The party had to issue forms to such candidates free of charge.”

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The spokesperson, however, did not identify the NDC candidates who were given the forms “free of charge.”

Presentation of NDC account

Mr Director said the NDC’s National Treasurer, John Odey, would release and present the party’s statement of account on Monday.

“This is in deference to our avowed commitment to the principles of transparency and accountability.

“In this regard, we challenge other political parties, especially the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), to emulate this level of openness and transparency in the management of their finances,” he said.

The spokesperson said the statement of account would be presented during the NDC’s Third National Executive Committee (NEC) meeting in Abuja.

He said the NDC would use the opportunity of the NEC meeting to unveil its National Campaign Council (NCC).

“As a party of innovation, our NCC is all-encompassing. It covers the Presidential, National Assembly, Governorship, and State Houses of Assembly Campaign Councils.

“Our various candidates will be presented with Certificates of Return for their respective offices,” he said.

“The NDC is turbo-charged and ready to give Nigerians the altruistic leadership the nation deserves.”

APC silent

Felix Morka, the national APC spokesperson, did not respond to calls and a text message seeking his response to the allegations that the party was responsible for hunger and poverty in Nigeria.

World.title: Tinubu blames opposition for hunger, poverty in Nigeria, Atiku kicks, says president delusional
World.content:
President Bola Tinubu has accused opposition politicians of causing the hunger and poverty Nigerians are experiencing, insisting that his administration is working to address the problems as he formally launched his 2027 presidential campaign in Kaduna on Saturday.

Mr Tinubu made the remarks at the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign flag-off at Ranchers Bees Stadium (also known as Kaduna Township Stadium), ahead of the 2027 general elections.

“I have heard the opposition talking about hunger and poverty. Who caused them? They did! They caused hunger and poverty. We are trying to eliminate them,” the president said.

He also urged his supporters to be wary of statements from the opposition, particularly criticism of his decision to remove the petrol subsidy, insisting that the country would not return to the previous system.

“Be careful; watch them. Don’t let them lie to you. What is past is in the past.

“Fuel subsidy is in our past: no more corruption, no more falsification of invoices, no more lies, no more smuggling of fuel,” Mr Tinubu told supporters at the rally.

The president’s remarks come amid persistent public concerns over high food prices, inflation and declining purchasing power, issues expected to feature prominently in political debates ahead of the 2027 elections.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

In a swift reaction to the president’s remarks, the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), former Vice President Atiku Abubakar, described President Tinubu’s claim “as a delusional, shameless attempt to dodge responsibility for the misery his own government has inflicted on Nigerians.”

He said a president cannot light the fire of hardship with his own policies, then blame the neighbours for the smoke.

Tinubu defends petrol subsidy removal

Since assuming office in May 2023, the Tinubu administration has implemented major economic reforms, including the removal of the petrol subsidy and changes to the foreign exchange regime.

The government has defended the measures as necessary to reduce public expenditure, tackle alleged corruption associated with the subsidy system and establish the foundations for sustainable economic growth.

While Mr Tinubu insists that the removal of the subsidy is irreversible, critics continue to demand evidence that the savings and additional revenue generated by the reforms are translating into improved living conditions for ordinary Nigerians.

At the rally, the president also said salaries were being paid on time and praised APC governors for their development projects.

Tinubu thanks Kaduna residents

At the rally, Mr Tinubu thanked the people of Kaduna State for supporting him in the 2023 presidential election, saying their backing contributed to his victory.

“You gave me the joy of remembering the victory you gave me to become president. I have returned to thank you once again,” he said.

He urged Nigerians to give him another opportunity in 2027, promising to continue pursuing his agenda of prosperity, development and national growth.

Tinubu has a long history of supporting the North – VP Shettima

Vice President Kashim Shettima defended Mr Tinubu’s political relationship with northern Nigeria, saying the president had supported politicians from the region for years, including those who contested the presidency in previous elections.

Mr Shettima cited Mr Tinubu’s political relationships with former Vice President Atiku Abubakar and the late President Muhammadu Buhari to argue that the president had consistently supported northern political figures.

“President Bola Tinubu is one person who has fiercely identified with the North over the years. It is pertinent to mention that when former Vice President Atiku Abubakar was harassed and chased off the PDP with his tail between his legs, he ran to the Lion of Bourdillon, who gave him political succour, support and a platform to contest for the presidency of this country in 2007.

“In 2011, Asiwaju supported another northerner, Nuhu Ribadu, and in 2015 and 2019, he supported our late President Muhammadu Buhari,” Mr Shettima said.

The expression, “Lion of Bourdillon,” refers to Mr Tinubu, whose residence on Bourdillon Road in Lagos has become associated with his political influence.

Atiku contested the presidency under the Action Congress (AC) in 2007 after leaving the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), with support from Mr Tinubu and other party leaders.

In 2011, Mr Ribadu contested the presidency under the Action Congress of Nigeria (ACN), a party led by Mr Tinubu. In 2015 and 2019, Mr Tinubu supported Mr Buhari’s presidential bids under the APC.

However, Mr Tinubu and Atiku subsequently became political opponents, particularly during the 2019 and 2023 presidential elections, when the former vice president contested under the PDP while Mr Tinubu was in the APC.

Mr Shettima’s remarks were part of the APC’s effort to highlight Mr Tinubu’s history of political alliances and support for politicians from Northern Nigeria as the party seeks another presidential term for him in 2027.

Top government officials attend the rally

The event attracted senior federal government officials, APC governors and party leaders from different parts of the country.

Those in attendance included Vice President Kashim Shettima and Kaduna State Governor Uba Sani, who received Mr Tinubu upon his arrival in the state.

Secretary to the Government of the Federation George Akume was also among the senior officials at the event. Other attendees included ministers, senators, members of the House of Representatives, APC governors and prominent party figures.

APC National Chairman Nentawe Yilwatda and Abdulaziz Yari, director-general of the party’s presidential campaign council, were among the party leaders involved in preparations for the rally and efforts to mobilise support for Mr Tinubu’s re-election.

The event marked the official launch of the APC’s presidential campaign, as the party seeks to consolidate its support base ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Controversy over the cost of the rally

Meanwhile, the APC campaign rally took place amid controversy over its alleged cost after a letter circulated on social media claimed that the Kaduna State Government had allocated and released ₦2.3 trillion to organise the event.

The state government rejected the allegation, describing the purported letter, said to have been written by Governor Sani to Mr Yari, the director-general of the Tinubu presidential campaign council, as fake.

The Kaduna State Commissioner for Information and Culture, Ahmed Maiyaki, said the governor did not write the letter and had not authorised the alleged release of funds.

The government also pointed out that Kaduna State’s 2026 budget stood at ₦985.92 billion, substantially below the ₦2.3 trillion allegedly spent on the rally.

The APC Presidential Campaign Council also dismissed the allegation, describing it as fabricated information intended to discredit Mr Tinubu, Governor Sani and other party leaders.

Dele Alake, a spokesperson for the campaign council, accused Atiku and the ADC of being involved in the circulation of what he described as false information; an allegation the ADC denied.

Atiku says Tinubu’s claim delusional, shameless

Meanwhile, in a statement by the Director of Strategic Communication, ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Phrank Shaibu, Atiku described President Tinubu’s claim that the opposition created hunger and poverty “as a delusional, shameless attempt to dodge responsibility for the misery his own government has inflicted on Nigerians.”

The former VP said a president cannot light the fire of hardship with his own policies, then blame the neighbours for the smoke.

“Mr President, blaming the opposition for hunger is either delusion or a staggering case of political amnesia. The APC governed Nigeria for eight years before you took office. You have added another three and a half years. Nigerians know who has been in power, and hardship did not begin when the opposition started talking about it. Stop insulting their intelligence and answer for your record.

“The hardship your administration has brought upon Nigerians is real. You cannot deny it by blaming others.”

Atiku listed some of the policies of the Tinubu administration that he said have impoverished Nigerians.

“Which administration removed the petrol subsidy and watched the naira fall from about ₦471 to ₦1,329 to the dollar?

“Which administration has presided over a rise in poverty that led the World Bank to estimate that 63 per cent of Nigerians will be below the national poverty line in 2026? Which administration extended the 2024 budget into 2025 while also operating a separate 2025 budget?

“Which administration recorded ₦7.13 trillion under ‘energy security’ in 2024 and faces questions over ₦11.2 trillion in NNPC pipeline related spending? Nigerians deserve to know who received these sums and what was delivered.

“Which administration must explain the $12.4 billion gap flagged in Nigeria’s external accounts for the first half of 2026? Which administration paid $22.5 million in ‘other charges’ on the Abu Dhabi financing facility?

“Which administration is responsible for the killings, kidnappings and displacement that continue to terrorise communities? These are the questions Nigerians are asking while your government blames the opposition.

“You cannot govern for three years, make life harder, and then blame others for describing the hardship. You asked who created the hunger. Nigerians are asking what you have done to end it.

“The people will judge your government by the lives they are living, not by the excuses you offer at campaign rallies.

The ADC flagbearer said the decision of the president to commission the unfinished Abuja-Kaduna Expressway from the venue of the APC campaign rally showed how far he had been removed from reality.

“Your decision to commission the unfinished Abuja to Kaduna Expressway from inside a stadium shows how far removed you are from the daily reality of Nigerians. A road cannot be completed with a speech or a ribbon cutting ceremony,” he said.

Atiku stated that the 16 January election would be a referendum on President Tinubu’s record.

“The 2027 presidential election will be a referendum on your record. Nigerians have felt the cost of your leadership in their homes, markets and communities. Their verdict is already clear: they have rejected your administration,” Mr Shaibu wrote.

World.title: EPL: Bassey, Iwobi celebrate Fulham win as Villa stun Man City
World.content:
Nigerian internationals Calvin Bassey and Alex Iwobi emerged victorious in the Premier League’s Nigerian derby on Saturday as Fulham secured a late 1-0 win over Coventry City, featuring compatriots Taiwo Awoniyi and Frank Onyeka.

Oscar Bobb scored the decisive goal in the 80th minute to hand Fulham all three points in a closely contested encounter.

Bassey played the entire match, while Iwobi was substituted in the 74th minute. Awoniyi and Onyeka both came on in the 67th minute as Coventry sought to change the course of the game, but Fulham held on for victory.

The result continued Fulham’s gradual climb up the table, moving them to 13th with eight points from eight matches.

Elsewhere, Aston Villa ended Manchester City’s perfect Premier League start with a 2-1 victory, allowing Arsenal to draw level with the champions at the top of the standings.

Nicolas Jackson scored twice for Villa, opening the scoring inside six minutes before restoring the hosts’ lead after Erling Haaland had equalised in the second half.

The victory extended Villa’s impressive run to six wins in seven matches across all competitions, strengthening their position after a difficult start to the campaign.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

City’s defeat provided Arsenal with an opportunity to close the gap, and Mikel Arteta’s side took full advantage with a 2-0 home win over Everton.

Ezri Konsa opened the scoring after seven minutes, ending Arsenal’s wait for a set-piece goal in open play this season. Gabriel Magalhaes sealed the victory with a header in the 68th minute.

The result moved Arsenal level on points with Manchester City, with goal difference separating the two sides.

Tottenham Hotspur also continued their resurgence with a 2-0 victory over Chelsea at Stamford Bridge, securing their second league win of the week.

Chelsea goalkeeper Mike Penders inadvertently turned the ball into his own net to give Tottenham the lead before Cole Palmer was sent off in the 80th minute for a second bookable offence.

Mathys Tel added a late second to complete the victory, lifting Tottenham to 12th place and extending Chelsea’s difficult run.

The weekend’s results further intensified the competition at both ends of the Premier League table, with Arsenal keeping pace with Manchester City and Fulham gaining valuable ground after their victory over Coventry.

World.title: Alvarez apologises to Atletico fans after summer exit attempt
World.content:
Atletico Madrid’s Argentine forward #19 Julian Alvarez shoots during the Spanish league football match between Club Atletico de Madrid and RC Deportivo de la Coruna at Metropolitano Stadium in Madrid on October 24, 2026. (Photo by Oscar DEL POZO / AFP)

Julian Alvarez apologised to Atletico Madrid fans on Saturday for trying to leave the club during the summer, admitting he understands why supporters were angry with him.

The Argentina international was heavily linked with Barcelona this summer and said during the World Cup he thought it would be best if Atletico sold him.

The Rojiblancos refused to accept an offer from the Catalan giants and Alvarez was whistled and jeered by the club’s own fans at the start of the season.

However, the tension has gradually eased and Alvarez netted his first goals of the season this week, firstly against Stuttgart in the Champions League and then on Saturday helping the club beat Deportivo La Coruna 1-0.

“I wanted to apologise to our people for my words during the World Cup,” Alvarez told Movistar.

“The truth is it was a mistake on my part, both in how I expressed myself and the timing. Above all because I understand people’s anger — I would have been angry too, as a fan.

“And also because of how they’ve stuck by me and supported me all these years and in these last few weeks. They’ve been very generous, and I really value that.”

Atletico signed the 26-year-old from Manchester City in 2024 and he has become a key figure for Diego Simeone’s side over the previous two seasons.

Alvarez put in his brightest display of the season against Deportivo and his goal split the teams at the Metropolitano stadium.

“I’m starting to feel good… I’m grateful to all my teammates because they’ve supported me,” continued Alvarez.

“They’ve really stuck by me throughout this whole time… and I’m working to improve.

“I’ve felt better in these last few matches… both physically and with the ball.”

AFP

World.title: Okpebholo threatens to sign death warrant of condemned kidnappers, cultists if …
World.content:
Governor Monday Okpebholo of Edo State

By Ozioruva Aliu, BENIN CITY

Governor Monday Okpebholo of Edo State has said he would not hesitate to sign the death of the four convicted Vegetable Market kidnappers if they did not appeal against the judgment within the stipulated time.

Read Also: Court orders speedy trial of 5 suspected kidnappers of NYSC members in Imo State

He said even if they appealed they were just postponing what would still come on them.

Speaking during a fellowship at God’s People Worldwide Prayer Ministry, while reviewing his administration’s efforts to curb kidnapping, cultism and other violent crimes in Edo State, said insecurity was one of the biggest worries he met on assuming office.

Okpebholo said that he raised the state of the roads and the security situation with President Bola Tinubu at their meeting who he said give him the approval to resolve the issues.

The governor said that when the gunmen struck at the Vegetable Market in Benin City, he called the President, who asked if he could handle it, and he said he could.

“I called the Commissioner of Police and told him I wanted these guys arrested, because I already have an approval from God, and they were caught within that time.

“They are already sentenced to death, and I pray they don’t appeal the judgment. Even when they appeal the judgment, they are only delaying time. If within the days stipulated, they don’t appeal, I will execute,” he said.

An Edo State Special Criminal Court on September 29 2026 sentenced four defendants to death for the abduction of a woman at the Vegetable Market along Airport Road, Benin City.

The governor said that before he began the campaign against kidnapping and cultism, he met prominent traditional rulers across the state to warn them against interceding for anyone involved in the crimes.

He recalled many strange incidents linked to spiritual forces after his administration pulled down a building associated with a cult group: “A black bird died in my office when I demolished their building. A vulture also died in my bed while contesting for governorship,” he said.

Founder of God’s People Worldwide Prayer Ministry, Apostle Ehijele Umuahia, during the event urged church members to vote for the governor and his preferred candidates in the 2027 elections.

Citing Proverbs 29:2, he told the congregation that prayer for the governor should go together with active participation in the electoral process. Christians, he said, should come out in large numbers to vote.

Umuahia described Governor Okpebholo as a humble man whose commitment to the things of God predates his time as governor. He said he has known him for over 15 years, from the days of the late Chief Tony Anenih.

“Whenever Chief Tony Anenih came to visit me, he was one of those who accompanied him. That was how we came to know each other,” he said.

Vanguard News

World.title: New York Archdiocese agrees to pay $800m to sex abuse victims
World.content:
The Archdiocese of New York said Saturday it had agreed to a settlement in which the church would pay more than $800 million to hundreds of victims of sexual abuse by clergy.

The agreement, to be formally signed in early November, marks the end of years of negotiations with lawyers representing the plaintiffs, as the American Catholic Church has been mired in sexual abuse scandals since the early 2000s.

“We are on the verge of being able to, please God, bring some measure of healing and reconciliation to all victim-survivors,” New York Archbishop Ronald Hicks wrote in an email sent to his priests and forwarded to AFP by the archdiocese.

According to The New York Times, which broke the story, each of the approximately 1,300 victims will receive at least $250,000, and potentially more depending on the severity of the abuse suffered.

The Archdiocese of New York, which covers Manhattan, Staten Island, the Bronx and several counties north of the city, will now be able to “turn its full attention once again to its mission of preaching the Gospel, healing the sick, caring for the poor and needy, welcoming the stranger, and educating our children,” Hicks’ email said.

Hicks was appointed bishop last year by Pope Leo XIV, replacing the influential conservative Cardinal Timothy Dolan. Before his departure, Dolan had announced the creation of a $300 million fund to compensate sexual abuse victims.

In the 2000s, press investigations revealed that Catholic priests in the United States had committed sexual abuse against thousands of children over several decades, and that church leaders had often covered up these cases or transferred the offending priests instead of reporting them to civil authorities.

Dioceses across the country have had to pay hundreds of millions of dollars in damages, and programs have been created to compensate victims without going to trial.

Last June, the Archdiocese of San Francisco announced it had reached an agreement to pay $395 million to about 530 victims of sexual abuse committed by its clergy in order to settle their lawsuits.

AFP

World.title: ‘We counted over 20 bodies after attackers left’ – Taraba massacre survivors
World.content:
File image

Gunmen swarmed a rural Nigerian village on motorcycles and killed at least 20 people, survivors told AFP on Saturday, in the latest attack in the country’s northeast.

Read Also: 2027: ‘They created the hunger’ — Tinubu slams opponents at Kaduna rally

The attackers opened fire just after Friday prayers in the rural village of Binnari, in Taraba state, residents said.

Northeastern Nigeria is home to a long-running jihadist insurgency, though Taraba, located toward the centre of the country, also faces non-ideological “bandit” gangs.

Bandits raid villages, kidnap people for ransom and levy “taxes” on farmers or miners in rural areas of Nigeria with little state presence.

“People were running in different directions to escape the attack. Nobody knew where it was safe to go,” said Binnari resident Isiyaku Musa.

He and Sa’idu Nuhu both gave a death toll of at least 20.

“After the attackers left, we counted more than 20 bodies, and some people were still missing,” Nuhu told AFP.

Police say 10

Police gave a lower toll, saying 10 bodies had been recovered as of Friday evening.

“The Nigerian authorities continue to leave rural communities in some parts of the north at the mercy of gunmen that are repeatedly commit atrocities with impunity,” Amnesty International Nigeria said.

“Consistent failure of the authorities to bring the suspected perpetrators to justice is clearly emboldening impunity,” the rights group said on social media.

Malam Abubakar Saifullahi, a community leader, said the attackers arrived on about 50 motorcycles, two men apiece, before raiding the village.

“They looted shops and took cash, foodstuffs and other provisions. They also took motorcycles abandoned by people fleeing the attack,” Saifullahi said.

Banditry has become a growing issue in northwest and central Nigeria, with powerful gangs – motivated by money rather than ideology – battling overstretched police and military across hard-to-reach, rural locations.

Separately on Saturday, the Nigerian military said it had killed 15 “terrorists” in northeastern Borno state in an air strike.

Nigeria has been fighting a jihadist insurgency since Boko Haram’s 2009 uprising.

Vanguard News

World.title: Alvarez fires Atletico to win against Deportivo
World.content:
Atletico Madrid’s Argentine forward #19 Julian Alvarez (L) attempts to score during the Spanish league football match between Club Atletico de Madrid and RC Deportivo de la Coruna at Metropolitano Stadium in Madrid on October 24, 2026. (Photo by Oscar DEL POZO / AFP)

Julian Alvarez continued on his road to redemption by scoring the only goal as Atletico Madrid beat Deportivo La Coruna 1-0 on Saturday to close the gap on La Liga leaders Barcelona to two points.

Diego Simeone’s side are second, with champions Barca hosting Real Madrid, third, in the Clasico at Camp Nou on Sunday.

Alvarez netted for the second consecutive game, having grabbed his first of the season in Atletico’s 1-1 Champions League draw at Stuttgart in midweek.

Atletico supporters hounded Alvarez during his first appearances this season after he tried to force his way out of the club in the summer, but the tension has gradually cooled.

Home fans at the Metropolitano stadium directed a few whistles at the team in general after a slow start, with Deportivo having the best chance of the first half.

Atletico goalkeeper Jan Oblak saved well from Lorenzo Amatucci, while at the other end Diego Simeone’s side lacked spark.

Early in the second half Alvarez found the breakthrough. Alejandro Grimaldo fired in a dangerous low pass towards the far post, where the Argentina international turned it over the line.

Alvarez came close to a second after a slick team move, with Alex Baena slipping him in, but Depor goalkeeper Leo Roman saved the striker’s attempted lob with his face.

The former Manchester City striker looked much closer to his best form in this outing after struggling with some fitness problems earlier in the campaign.

Alexander Sorloth lashed narrowly over from a tight angle as Atletico sought to kill off the game, unsuccessfully.

Deportivo might have levelled in stoppage time with Kevin Sanchez volleying well wide from Adama Traore’s cross when well placed to trouble Oblak.

The Galicians’ best chance came with virtually the last kick of the game, with Oblak saving from Sanchez on his line, when the forward seemed destined to score.

Earlier, Georges Mikautadze snatched a late 2-1 win for Villarreal in a derby clash against Valencia, who had midfielder Harvey Elliott sent off as both sides finished with 10 men.

The Yellow Submarine came from behind to triumph, climbing into mid-table and leaving Javier Aguirre’s Los Che 19th, in the relegation zone.

Pepelu sent Valencia ahead from the penalty spot in the first half before American defender Alex Freeman headed the visitors level at Mestalla stadium after 69 minutes.

Inigo Perez’s Villarreal had Pape Gueye sent off when the Senegal international hit Jose Gaya in the face with his elbow.

However, English midfielder Elliott, on loan from Liverpool, was soon dismissed for two quick yellow cards for apparent dissent.

Villarreal striker Mikautadze broke through in stoppage time, racing through and finishing with aplomb to claim the three points.

AFP

World.title: Obama blasts Trump’s ‘chaos and cruelty’ while campaigning for Democrats
World.content:
Former US President Barack Obama

Former US president Barack Obama delivered a scathing critique of his successor, Donald Trump, at a rally Saturday in Ohio to support Democratic candidates ahead of the November 3 midterm elections.

“After two years of chaos and cruelty and corruption and incompetence, the likes of which we have not seen in the modern era, you get a chance to say, ‘Enough is enough,'” Obama declared in Cleveland. “We are voting for change right here in Ohio.”

The 65-year-old Democrat blamed the Trump administration for the rising cost of living, a top voter concern amid soaring fuel prices.

“The current president chose to make a series of bad decisions,” Obama said. “Most importantly, he decided to start an unnecessary war that nobody asked for.”

Obama also urged voters to cast their ballots as soon as possible since early voting is already open in this northern industrial state.

“Don’t procrastinate, don’t equivocate,” Obama said.

The former president retains considerable popularity among the Democratic base, which he is keen to leverage to support his party’s candidates in the upcoming crucial elections that will decide control of Congress.

In Ohio, former Democratic senator Sherrod Brown will attempt a comeback against incumbent Republican Senator Jon Husted, while the race for governor will be contested between Democrat Amy Acton and Republican Vivek Ramaswamy, a former presidential candidate in 2024.

Polls for Ohio give Democrats a slight lead in both those races, but the results are expected to be close.

Nationally, polls also suggest that Democrats could regain control of the House of Representatives but face a much more competitive contest for the Senate.

After Cleveland, Obama will head north to Michigan this evening for a rally in Detroit alongside Abdul El-Sayed, the Democratic Senate candidate.

While both of Michigan’s Senate seats are currently held by Democrats, El-Sayed, from the party’s left wing, is in a close race with Republican Mike Rogers.

AFP

World.title: Trump votes early in Florida for US midterm elections
World.content:
US President Donald Trump speaks to the press at the Palm Beach County Supervisor of Elections office after voting in the midterm elections in West Palm Beach, Florida, on October 24. (Photo by Brendan SMIALOWSKI / AFP)

US President Donald Trump on Saturday voted early in his home state of Florida for the November 3 midterm elections, in which his Republican Party is battling to maintain control of Congress.

Trump and his wife, Melania, cast their ballots ahead of an appearance by the president at a campaign rally in the southern US state of Georgia.

Trump said he voted party line, or exclusively for members of his Republican Party.

Asked by reporters after voting about corruption as a major issue for voters, Trump insisted that it was happening in districts and cities controlled by Democrats.

“You ought to look at the real corruption — it’s Democrat corruption,” he said.

The Republican billionaire, who has consistently refused to accept his defeat in the 2020 presidential election, baselessly alleging widespread voter fraud, reiterated allegations along those lines Saturday.

“I ran and I won in 2016, and I won in 2020, too, but it didn’t work out that way,” he said at the Palm Beach County Supervisor of Elections office in West Palm Beach. “It was a rigged election, but I won by millions of votes.”

With 10 days to go until the midterms, which traditionally favor the party outside the White House, Trump faces dismal polls suggesting the Republicans will lose control of the House of Representatives and possibly the Senate.

Without a Republican majority in Congress, the 80-year-old president would have little room to push through his legislative agenda during his final two years in office.

He or his staff could also face numerous congressional investigations by Democrats, who have said they want to examine business dealings conducted by the president and those close to him through the family’s holding company since his return to the White House.

AFP

World.title: Clashes break out in Paris, other French cities amid fresh protests
World.content:
Police officers try in vain to arrest a protester helped by others in a street by the Campo Santo Antifascist village set as part of a counter-mobilisation “against racism, fascism and imperialism” on the sidelines of the congress of the far-right party Rassemblement National (RN) in Orleans, central France, on October 24, 2026. Amid another Saturday of protests under tight security across France, Orleans is hosting the National congress of the Far-right party Rassemblement National and preparing for a record-breaking demonstration, on the eve of their first major campaign rally. (Photo by SIMON WOHLFAHRT / AFP)

Clashes broke out Saturday in Paris and other French cities amid demonstrations held a week after others that degenerated into street violence and prompted a robust security backlash as President Emmanuel Macron seeks to restore order.

Police arrested nearly 1,000 people as officers were confronted with “an extremely elevated level of violence” from black-clad “ultra-left” extremists, Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said.

Riot police squads fired tear gas at protesters in the capital as well as in Marseille, Lyon, Bordeaux, Lille, Toulouse, Montpellier and Nantes.

Two people were “seriously” injured, Nunez said: one man in Toulouse, who reportedly had fingers blown off, and another person in Clermont-Ferrand. He did not give details of either case.

Authorities had deployed 70,000 security forces across the country for the new marches, called to protest the cost of living.

The violence came a week after rioting that saw public buildings vandalised, hundreds of shops looted and 2,700 people arrested, casting a pall over a country that goes to the polls in six months to choose a successor to Macron after 10 years.

Nunez said Saturday’s outcome was more “positive” than a week ago, with more police on the streets acting more rapidly, conducting more pre-demonstration checks and better protecting businesses.

There was nevertheless widespread anger at the government over a protest crackdown viewed as an assault on the right to protest.

– Police battle ‘rioters’ –

Saturday’s demonstrations drew between 410,000 and 800,000 people across the country, according to different estimates by authorities and the organising CGT union.

The main Paris march had between 110,000 and 250,000 attendees, according to those sources.

Macron’s government has ordered police to prevent protesters reaching city centres, where shops are concentrated, and in Paris and some other cities, partial curfews were imposed in certain urban zones. The French president had ordered non-union demonstrations be banned as “illegitimate”.

In Paris, where many shops had boarded up windows to prevent looting, and the Louvre and the Musee d’Orsay museums shut for the day, the main demonstration passed off largely peacefully.

The march had been pushed to the capital’s southeast rim under a last-minute order by authorities.

Afterwards, though, clashes broke out as the crowd was dispersing. Nunez said the confrontations lasted two hours and involved “500 rioters” at the back of the march.

AFP journalists saw police charge several times and vigorously use tear gas and batons against some, mostly young, protesters.

“The police started moving towards everyone, telling them to get down and back off. They were just taking people down, you know, beating protesters,” one demonstrator bleeding from a baton blow to his face, who gave his first name as David, told AFP.

– Ultra-right vs ultra-left –

In the western city of Nantes, thousands of protesters broke through lines of police firing tear gas and a water cannon to reach the city centre, an AFP journalist there witnessed.

Emma, 23, marching in the northwest city of Rennes, said she was angry at “everything happening at the moment”, denouncing the bans on demonstrations and the “repression” of the high schools student protests.

Marching in the rain at the head of the protest in the northern city of Lille, 47-year-old Delphine insisted: “Neither the president, nor the weather will stop me from demonstrating.”

In Lyon, police used tear gas to disperse around 1,000 people gathered in the south of the city.

“If they prohibit protests then that means we are heading more and more towards a regime that is fascist, that is dictatorial,” said one 20-year-old protester in Lyon, who gave only his first name, Silem.

In the southern cities of Cannes and Montpellier, far-right activists came out onto the streets seeking confrontations with “ultra-left militants”, in what authorities said was an unprecedented development.

There was looting on the sidelines of the marches in Marseille and Grenoble, said police.

Meanwhile, the Yellow Vests, who staged disruptive protests against Macron eight years ago, called for more demonstrations on October 31 for “the freedom to protest”.

Far-left presidential candidate Jean-Luc Melenchon, who marched in the Paris rally, said Macron “is going to understand that this is going to repeat itself every week”.

– Protest against Le Pen’s party –

Tensions were heightened by a rally in the city of Orleans by far-right leader Marine Le Pen’s National Rally party to kick off her campaign for the presidential election.

Thousands of counter-protesters chanting anti-fascist slogans marched in the city. Police put their number at 13,000 while organisers said twice as many participated.

The unrest across France highlighted the febrile political atmosphere ahead of the vote, in which Le Pen leads in surveys.

Inflation in France, particularly affecting the cost of fuel, has surged since the start of the Middle East war in February.

Protests have also been taking place in Italy, Belgium, Spain and Portugal over different issues, yet with some overlap on inflation and education problems. Italy has mobilised 500 troops to Milan after street violence there.

World.title: PSN Advocates Collaboration of Specialised Professionals for Stronger Pharmacy Practice In Nigeria
World.content:
The Pharmaceutical Society of Nigeria (PSN) has urged collaboration of specialised branches of the profession to strengthen pharmacy practice in the country.

Speaking ahead of the society’s 99th Annual National Conference scheduled to hold from November 1st – 7th, 2026 at the International Conference Centre, Awka, Anambra State, PSN President, Pharm. Ayuba Ibrahim Tanko, noted that strengthening pharmacy practice in the country would require advanced practice, clinical collaboration, residency training, education, and the contributions of research pharmacists in pharmacotherapy, medication safety, pharmaceutical preparation and the appropriate use of medicines.

He said that translation of such professional expertise will bring about stronger patient-care services, appropriate competency development, structured practice-based training and effective collaboration with other healthcare professionals.

Tanko recognised the existence of the foundation on which the initiatives can be achieved. According to him, these include the “recognition of the Consultant Pharmacist cadre which creates an opportunity to clarify advanced practice responsibilities.’’

He also identified the PSN –West African Society of Parenteral and Enteral Nutrition (WASPEN) collaboration which offers opportunities for pharmacists to contribute to multidisciplinary nutrition care and specialized pharmaceutical services; as well as the West African Postgraduate College of Pharmacists (WAPCP) – Delta State University Teaching Hospital (DELSUTH) International Pharmacy Practice Residency Programme (IPPR)) which provides practical basis for strengthening supervised postgraduate training, while education, mentorship and research can support development across all these areas.

Bringing these initiatives into a common strategic discussion, Tanko posited, “can help align professional priorities without merging them into a single programme or disregarding their existing governance arrangements.’’

He explained that the Consultant Pharmacist cadre has been recognised within the Federal and State public-service scheme of service. According to him, consistent implementation requires greater clarity regarding the role, competencies, responsibilities, professional development expectations and accountability of Consultant Pharmacists.

‘’A standardised framework could support more consistent appointments, improve workforce planning and strengthen the integration of advanced pharmacists into multidisciplinary clinical teams.’’ Adding that “defining the role, scope of responsibilities, reporting relationships and expected contribution to patient care and healthcare services’’ should be given due attention.

He stressed the importance of ‘’establishing a competency and qualification framework covering advanced clinical practice, leadership, education, research and service development. Clarifying contributions to complex medication-related decisions, therapeutic optimisation, medication safety and coordinated patient care, and defining responsibilities for clinical service development, mentorship, professional education, quality improvement and performance evaluation.’’

Tanko advised said that the framework should draw on relevant international models while reflecting Nigeria’s healthcare system, regulatory environment and workforce needs saying, “any proposed clinical authority or prescribing responsibilities must remain consistent with applicable Nigerian laws and regulations.’’

Explaining the PSN–WASPEN collaboration and the emerging practice opportunities for pharmacists in the country, he said the initiative provides an opportunity to strengthen multidisciplinary nutrition care and identify appropriate roles for pharmacists in clinical nutrition and specialised pharmaceutical services.

Tanko identified areas that offer particular opportunities for professional development and service improvement including identifying and managing medication-related problems that may affect nutritional status, treatment response and recovery, and supporting the safe use of medicines in patients receiving enteral or parenteral nutrition, including compatibility, administration and monitoring considerations, contributing nutrition support protocols, medication safety systems, clinical monitoring and quality improvement.

He also highlighted sterile compounding and specialised pharmaceutical services which the Pharmacy Council of Nigeria (PCN) is involved in. According to him, PSN in collaboration with relevant partners has advanced initiatives to strengthen local pharmaceutical compounding and manufacturing, beginning with non-sterile preparations. Tanko also said that the WASPEN – Pharmaceutical industry collaboration represents the second phase of this broader compounding initiative, focusing on sterile compounding and specialised pharmaceutical services, particularly the safe preparation of parenteral nutrition.

The PSN president listed the benefits to the Nigerian health system including training and competency development in aseptic technique, sterile compounding and clean room practice, developing and implementing quality systems, Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and risk-management processes.

It would also be supporting the safe preparation of parenteral nutrition in collaboration with the wider nutrition support team, exploring centralised admixture services where feasible, appropriately governed and sustainable, as well as promoting technical education, clinical attachments, research and the appropriate introduction of compounding technologies.

The collaboration, he added, can also support joint workshops, webinars, conferences, mentorship and clinical attachments. Any new service should be assessed against local needs, regulatory requirements, staffing, infrastructure and sustainable financing.

On the International Pharmacy Practice Residency Programme (IPPR), he explained that it was launched at Delta State University Teaching Hospital (DELSUTH), Oghara, in May 2022 through the West African Postgraduate College of Pharmacists (WAPCP), in collaboration with DELSUTH and with engagement involving the American Society of Health-System Pharmacists (ASHP). The programme, he said, provides an opportunity to strengthen the practice-based component of postgraduate pharmacy training by connecting theoretical learning with supervised clinical experience. Its development also offers lessons for residency programme leadership, preceptor preparation, competency assessment and service improvement.

The IPPR, he further explained, would focus on strengthening learning objectives, competency assessment and structured clinical experiences., supporting preceptor development, mentorship and consistent resident feedback, and integrating multidisciplinary patient care, medication safety, quality improvement and research.

“The IPPR should complement existing WAPCP postgraduate training and residency pathways rather than be presented as evidence that traditional training lacks practical value. Decisions about expansion should be guided by documented experience, programme readiness, available preceptors, service capacity and applicable accreditation requirements. The DELSUTH programme is under ASHP review following an accreditation survey, with a decision expected by March 2027,’’ he said.

Tanko said, “to advance this initiative, inputs were obtained from relevant stakeholders, including the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, PCN, PSN, WASPEN, WAPCP, the Association of Consultant Pharmacists, the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC), healthcare institutions and academic partners. Adding that a decision to identify which areas require immediate attention and which need further consultation or technical development remains salient in view of the goals and objectives of the initiative.’’

World.title: Device Checker Will Enhance Protection of Customers, Quality of Service, Says NCC
World.content:
Oghenevwede Ohwovoriole in Abuja

The Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC), has assured Nigerians that the Commission’s device checker policy is to enhance consumers safety and the to guarantee quality service delivery.

The Director Technical Standard and Network Integrity, Edoyemi Ogoh made the clarity at the sensitisation programme on key issues in the telecommunications industry and the country’s digital space. Organised by the Commission on Tuesday in Abuja.

The engagement is designed to provide media stakeholders with insights into the Commission’s regulatory initiatives, industry developments, and matters of interest to stakeholders across the telecommunications industry.

Edoyemi Ogoh stated that the integrity of the telecom industry does not depend solely on infrastructure.

“The integrity of the telecommunications industry depends not only on the network infrastructure but also on the quality, safety and compliance of the devices that are assessed and used on these networks. For this reason, type approval is not merely a regulatory requirement, it is a vital mechanism for protecting consumers, safeguarding performance and preserving confidence in Nigeria’s digital economy.

“The Commission has statutory responsibility to ensure that communications equipment deployed within Nigeria meets established standards.” he added

According to him the Commission derived the powers to type as approve telecommunication devices from the Nigerian Communications Act. 2003. “This obligation is reflected in the requirements governing the certification and approval of communication devices intended for use within the country. Under Section 132 Subsection 2 of the Nigerian Communications Act 2003, licenced service providers, facilities providers, equipment manufacturers and suppliers are required to obtain type approval from the Commission before communication equipment may be sold or used in Nigeria. The purpose of this regulatory instrument or requirement is straightforward

“Devices operating on Nigerian networks must meet established technical standards and comply with applicable regulatory requirements. This helps to ensure compatibility with network infrastructure, protect users, improve service quality and strengthen trust in the communications ecosystem.

“We have also ensured that devices currently in stock are appropriately onboarded and that devices imported into Nigeria going forward are properly verified and authenticated. This will provide a more effective mechanism for identifying non-compliant, cloned or fake devices and prevent them from connecting to our networks. Every consumer deserves confidence that the Commission’s devices being purchased and used meet required standards.

He also noted that the implementation of the policy will guarantee consumers confidence on telecom devices in Nigeria “Consumers should not have to worry about whether a device is technically compliant, whether it poses avoidable security risks or whether it may negatively affect their experience on telecommunications networks. By strengthening the type of overall compliance, the Commission helps address these concerns. The implementation creates an environment in which consumers can have greater confidence in the devices available within the Nigerian marketplace.

On the safety of consumers personal data, he said, “it maintains device identification information including IMEI numbers for regulatory purposes. It does not provide the Commission with access to the content of users’ devices nor does it enable the Commission to monitor personal communications. The objective of the initiative is regulatory compliance relating to communications devices strictly.

“It is not a surveillance tool and does not provide access to personal information stored on those devices.

The Head Corporate communications NCC, Olawaiye Olasumbo in her remarks called for the continued support of the media and other stakeholders in creating awareness on the initiative. “We encourage your continued supports in creating public awareness about this initiative.”

World.title: Bishop Akunna Mourns Victims of Ogoja Food Empowerment Stampede
World.content:
The Bishop of Ogoja Diocese, Anglican Communion, The Rt. Rev’d Ifeanyi Akunna, has commiserated with the family of one woman who was reportedly trampled to death on Thursday in a stampede triggered by a food distribution programme organised by the Cross River State government.

In a statement he personally signed, Bishop Akunna, said he was “deeply saddened” by the “distressing news of the tragic loss of lives and injuries sustained during the empowerment distribution in Ogoja.

“On behalf of the Anglican Diocese of Ogoja, we extend our heartfelt condolences to the families who lost their beloved ones in this unfortunate incident. No words can adequately express the pain of losing a loved one, especially under circumstances that could have been avoided,” stated the Bishop.

He continued, “Our hearts go out to the bereaved families, and we pray that the Holy Spirit, our Divine Comforter, will console, strengthen and uphold them in this difficult moment,” stressing, “May the souls of the faithful departed, through the mercy of God, rest in peace. Amen.”

The Bishop equally commiserated with the Government and people of Cross River State, stressing,”it is indeed heartbreaking that an initiative intended to bring relief, hope and assistance to the good people of Ogoja ended in sorrow, mourning and the needless loss of innocent lives.

“What was meant to be a gesture of goodwill and compassion has sadly turned into an occasion of grief,” he regretted.

“While we sincerely commend the Cross River State Government for its various empowerment and welfare initiatives, we also appeal that appropriate measures be taken to ensure that such a tragedy never re-occurs” urged the Bishop.

“The distribution of relief materials and other public welfare interventions must be properly coordinated, with adequate security arrangements, crowd-control measures and respect for the dignity and safety of every human life.”

He appreciated Governor Bassey Otu’s “commitment to bearing the medical expenses of those currently receiving treatment in the hospital,” adding that, “this compassionate gesture is commendable and should be sustained until the victims have fully recovered.”

Bishop Akunna commended the timely intervention of the Nigerian military and the Police, saying the move “brought the situation under control and prevented further casualties.”

World.title: Shettima: Tinubu’s Reforms More About Improving Quality Of Life of Nigerians
World.content:
.Inaugurates ultra-modern teaching hospital, schools in Borno

Deji Elumoye in Abuja

Vice President Kashim Shettima has said President Bola Tinubu’s reform agenda places strong emphasis on building enduring institutions, developing human capital and improving the quality of life of Nigerians.

He stressed why sustainable development must outlive the tenure of political officeholders, maintaining that the Renewed Hope Agenda of President Tinubu is designed to ensure that economic reforms deliver lasting social benefits, with investments in essential public services.

Shettima stated this yesterday while inaugurating the ultra-modern Kashim Ibrahim University Teaching Hospital (KIUTH) and two schools in Maiduguri, the Borno State capital.

He described investments in healthcare and education as essential to economic productivity, national development and the recovery of communities affected by insecurity.

The Vice President stated that true measure of public service lies not in the privileges of office but in the institutions established and the opportunities created for future generations.

According to him, “Someday, and that day is nearer than we imagine, we shall be judged by what survives our time in office. The offices we held, the aides who surrounded us and the length of our convoys will have surrendered their importance. What will endure are the institutions we built, the roads we constructed and the lives made better because we served.”

Commending Borno State Governor, Prof. Babagana Umara Zulum, for prioritising healthcare and education, Shettima said the newly inaugurated facilities demonstrate how purposeful investments can translate into practical benefits for citizens.

He noted that the teaching hospital would bring specialised healthcare closer to communities, reduce the burden of travelling outside the state for treatment and strengthen medical training and research.

“For a family already burdened by illness, the cost and anxiety of travelling outside the state can compound their suffering. This hospital offers the prospect of expert attention nearer home,” he said.

On education, the Vice President observed that rebuilding schools in communities affected by insurgency was fundamental to restoring hope, expanding opportunities and preparing the next generation for productive participation in the economy.

“In a state whose communities have endured the disruption of insurgency, a classroom carries a particular significance. It restores the expectation that tomorrow can be planned for,” Shettima stated.

Drawing from his experience as a former Governor of Borno State, the Vice President acknowledged the challenges of delivering development amid insecurity and praised Governor Zulum’s determination to sustain investment in critical public infrastructure.

“To improve lives and livelihoods in a state that has withstood such a climate of insecurity demands uncommon fortitude. I know the weight of that responsibility. As the street language goes, I have been there and done that,” he said.

Shettima conveyed President Tinubu’s felicitations to the government and people of Borno State, and reaffirmed the federal government’s commitment to supporting the state’s reconstruction, peacebuilding and human capital development efforts.

“Our investment in human capital proceeds from the conviction that a healthier, better educated population can produce more, earn more and contribute more. The federal government will continue to support Borno’s efforts to consolidate peace, rebuild communities and expand opportunities for its people,” he said.

The Vice President noted that Borno’s reconstruction experience offers valuable lessons in rebuilding communities emerging from conflict, particularly through the restoration of essential public institutions.

He commended the state government, healthcare professionals, educators, contractors, development partners and security personnel for their contributions to the projects.

Shettima, however, stressed that the success of the facilities would ultimately depend on their ability to deliver quality services to the people.

“The responsibility now is to keep these institutions worthy of that faith. Their value will be measured in the care patients receive and the education children acquire,” he said.

Earlier, Governor Zulum said the teaching hospital stood as one of the most tangible expressions of his administration’s commitment to providing state-of-the-art healthcare facilities for the people of Borno State.

He explained that the teaching hospital was not merely another building but a centre of learning, a provider of specialised healthcare services and a facility that would bring hope to millions of people across the North-east.

The governor said the facility would serve as a clinical training centre for the College of Health Sciences of Kashim Ibrahim University, providing training for medical students, resident doctors, nurses, midwives, pharmacists, medical laboratory scientists, physiotherapists and other healthcare professionals.

Zulum assured that the Borno State Government would continue to invest in the Kashim Ibrahim University Teaching Hospital, saying, “We have recruited and we will continue to recruit qualified healthcare professionals. We will provide equipment, utility infrastructure and an enabling environment for the hospital to function at the highest standard.”

Also, the Pro-Chancellor of Kashim Ibrahim University, Alhaji Mohammed Indimi, said the inauguration of the teaching hospital represented a remarkable achievement and a milestone in the collective commitment to providing quality healthcare services, medical education, research and professional training.

He expressed optimism that the hospital would strengthen healthcare delivery in Borno State and contribute meaningfully to the well-being of people across the North-east.

On his part, Chairman of the Governing Board of Kashim Ibrahim University Teaching Hospital, Prof. Ahmed Ahidjo, described the hospital as a landmark project of unprecedented significance in the state.

He commended Vice President Shettima for choosing Governor Zulum as his successor and applauded the governor for his bold decision to establish the teaching hospital and equip it with modern, state-of-the-art medical facilities.

Also speaking, Chief Medical Director of Kashim Ibrahim University Teaching Hospital, Prof. Ibrahim Musa Kida, said the greatness of the hospital would be determined not merely by its buildings and equipment but by the quality of its personnel and the dedication of its staff.

He also commended Shettima for his contributions to the progress and development of Borno State and Nigeria, particularly his continued commitment to peace and development in the state.

World.title: WAP TV Receives Multiple Awards in October
World.content:
Sunday Okobi

WapTV, The Family Entertainment Channel, has stated that it has many reasons to celebrate in October, 2026, from its 14th year anniversary to the awards bestowed on the TV channel.

From October 1, 2012, when it stated broadcasting to October 1, 2026, WapTV has celebrated 14 years of non-stop transmission of quality programming to the entire family.

On October 10, WapTV received Best Kiddies/Youth Programme of the Year Award presented to Nnennaand Friends show by 7th Nigerian Broadcasters Merit Award (NBMA) 2026, an award ceremony organized by the prestigious Independent Broadcasters Association of Nigeria (IBAN).

The entertainment channel also received the Voice of Inclusion Award presented by Down Syndrome Foundation of Nigeria on October 16, for WapTV’s dedication to creating awareness of the resourcefulness and astounding characteristics of people living with Down Syndrome.

To crown up the awards season, on October 19, WapTV was presented with a plaque for Outstanding Family Entertainment Media Brand of the Decade by the Edge Awards 2026.

While eulogizing its audience for the accolades, the Director of WapTV, Wale Adenuga Junior, at an event yesterday said: “We are truly grateful to all the advertisers, viewers, management and staff of WapTV who have continued to believe in, and stayed with us for 14 years.

“We implore everyone of them to continue to spread the word about how WapTV has been relentless in broadcasting exciting, entertaining and educative content over the years. The best part is we have just begun.”

WapTV boasts of millions of viewers who watch thechannel on Satellite TV, as well as over 800,000 Subscribers on its YouTube Channel ‘waptvchannel’ which has over 300,000,000 views and counting.

The 24-hour Family Entertainment Channel broadcasts across Nigeria and several African countries on a network of DStv 262, StarTimes 116, GOtv 129 andFreeTV 751.

World.title: NDC Lawyers Demand Probe of INEC Official Over Multiple Inconsistent Reports in Kano
World.content:
Ahmad Sorondinki in Kano

Lawyers to the Kano State chapter of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) have petitioned the Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to investigate the Head of Department, Election and Party Monitoring in Kano, Mrs. Hauwa Buhari, over alleged issuance of multiple inconsistent monitoring reports on the party’s primary elections.

The demand was contained in a press statement dated 19th October, 2026 and signed by Magaji Mato Ibrahim, SAN, I.M. Abdullahi, Siraj Hamza and two other lawyers, on behalf of the NDC Kano chapter.

The lawyers were responding to a public statement issued on 17th October by Bola Aidi, SAN & Co., solicitors to five persons claiming candidature under the NDC in Kano, who had described the petition against the INEC official as political intimidation.

According to the NDC legal team, the petition dated 16th October was issued on the clear instructions of the NDC Kano State chapter and the claims that the leadership was unaware of it are incorrect and unsupported by any documentary evidence.

On the substance of the petition, the lawyers said it complains of an objective documentary problem – the issuance by the same INEC officer of multiple signed versions of a monitoring report on the NDC Kano primary elections.

“The versions are materially inconsistent in content, some are undated, and they list persons who were not screened, cleared or nominated by the party while excluding authentic candidates whose names appear on Form EC9D signed by the National Chairman and National Secretary,” the statement said.

The lawyers added that the officer is said to have previously admitted lacunas in the report and a corrected version was reportedly forwarded to INEC headquarters without formal communication or implementation.

They also accused the five persons claiming candidature of filing suits at the Federal High Court without notice to the authentic candidates of the party, describing it as a violation of fair hearing principles which require that all interested parties must be joined at the commencement of pre-election matters.

The statement described as curious and unusual, the decision of private solicitors to candidates to mount a public defence of an INEC officer.

“Mrs. Hauwa Buhari is an officer of a constitutional body that has the institutional capacity, legal representation and statutory duty to defend its staff and its records,” the lawyers noted.

They further argued that a monitoring report cannot create a candidacy where the party’s own preconditions for participation were not met, nor can it override the official submission under section 29 of the Electoral Act, 2026.

The legal team called on the INEC Chairman to cause an immediate investigation into the circumstances surrounding the issuance of the reports, withdraw all defective versions and issue one authentic, properly dated report that reflects the true candidates nominated by the party.

World.title: Sokoto Residents Challenge ADC Candidate Dan’iya to Present Development Blueprint
World.content:
Onuminya Innocent in Sokoto

Concerned residents of Sokoto State have challenged the governorship candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Manir Muhammad Dan’iya, to move beyond criticism of Governor Ahmed Aliyu Sokoto’s administration and unveil a clear and achievable development agenda ahead of the 2027 governorship election.

In a statement jointly signed by Comrade Ibrahim Umar Kware, Comrade Aminu Hali Tambuwal and Comrade Bello Arzika Dandange, on behalf of the group, the residents said the people of the state deserve more than political attacks from those seeking their mandate.

According to the group, the 2027 election should be defined by competing ideas, credible alternatives and concrete solutions to the challenges facing the state, rather than a campaign built solely on fault-finding and condemnation of government policies.

The residents observed that since his emergence as the ADC governorship candidate, Dan’iya has consistently criticised the policies and programmes of the present administration without presenting a comprehensive policy document detailing what he would do differently.

“Enough of criticism. Sokoto people want to know what you intend to do for them. What is your development agenda and how do you intend to deliver on your promises? It is not enough to criticise the government without providing workable alternatives,” the statement said.

They argued that aspiring to govern a state of over five million people requires thorough preparation, clear vision and a sound understanding of public administration, including realistic funding strategies, implementation timelines and measurable performance indicators.

The group further urged Dan’iya to reflect on his tenure as Deputy Governor under former Governor Aminu Waziri Tambuwal and share the lessons learnt, cautioning him against what they described as the shortcomings of his political mentor whom they accused of assuming office without adequate preparation.

While emphasising the need for accountability on the part of the incumbent administration, the residents acknowledged Governor Ahmed Aliyu’s interventions in security logistics, road construction and rehabilitation, housing and primary healthcare revitalisation as efforts that merit objective assessment.

They noted that the provision of operational vehicles, motorcycles and other security equipment to security agencies has enhanced response capacity in parts of the state, even as they admitted that insecurity remains a challenge requiring sustained action.

According to the concerned residents, while the present government must be judged on its performance, the opposition has an equal responsibility to demonstrate superior capacity and offer better alternatives rather than expecting voters to be swayed by criticism alone.

They therefore challenged the ADC candidate to publicly present his specific plans for strengthening security in vulnerable communities, supporting farmers and small businesses, tackling youth unemployment, attracting private investment and improving service delivery across the 23 local government areas of the state, stressing that Sokoto needs a prepared leader with a clear plan.

World.title: NASENI Trains, Empowers 120 Electricians in Modern Electrical Installation in Kogi
World.content:
Ibrahim Oyewale in Lokoja





The National Agency for Science and Engineering Infrastructure (NASENI) has trained, empowered no fewer 120 electricians in modern electrical installation and maintenance in Kogi State as part of efforts to tackle youths’ unemployment in the country.



The Executive Director/CEO NASENI, Professor Khalid Halilu, disclosed this at the closing ceremony of NASENI Skills Acquisition and Empowerment programme and presentation of certificate to held in Lokoja yesterday.



Professor Halilu explained that NASENI was committed to taking skills acquisition to the door steps of Nigerians, noting that industrialisation goes beyond the machine and structures, but skills acquisition to ignite the industrial revolution in Nigeria.



The executive director however, commended the Kogi State government for their cooperation.



Professor Halilu who was represented by a Coordinating Director of Finance and Account, NASENI, Ibrahim Dauda explained that the agency has trained, empowered a total of 120 electricians in modern electrical installation.



He added that NASENI also gave them money to start their own business, admonished the trainees that their skills placed them in the fastest growing sector of Nigeria economy, the construction sector, so they must key into it immediately.



He warned the trainees not to sell the starter packs, stressing it is a sustainable livelihood tools for them and this will enable start new life.



The traditional ruler and the Chairman of Lokoja Traditional Council, the Maigari of Lokoja, His Royal Highness, Ibrahim Kabir, expressed gratitude to NASENI for the trading of 120 electricians in the modern electrical installation.



“My dear participants, the training you have received from NASENI places a responsibility on you to demonstrate the value of the investment made in your professional development…In this sense, you should regard yourselves as ambassadors of NASENI.



“Your conduct, professional competence; and quality of service will help to shape public perception of the agency and the effectiveness of its training programmes therefore encourage you to put the knowledge and skills acquired here into practical use and allow your work to speak positively about the institution that has invested in you. Be worthy ambassadors through your professionalism, integrity, discipline, diligence, and good conduct.



“Your success will not only benefit you and your families; it will also demonstrate the value of NASENI’s intervention and strengthen the case for similar programmes to be extended to other trades and communities,” the traditional ruler posited.

World.title: Miss SA to Mrs: Inside Mia Le Roux’s wedding
World.content:
Mia Le Roux wed her partner Luke ten Oever in Franschhoek. Images via IG

Mia le Roux is the latest Miss South Africa to go from being a beauty queen to a bride. The 31-year-old wed her longtime partner, Luke ten Oever, last weekend.

INSIDE MIA LE ROUX’S WEDDING

Last weekend, Mia Le Roux – South Africa’s first hearing-impaired title winner – wed her longtime partner Luke ten Oever at La Paris Estate.

The Franschhoek venue was the same location as Vasti Spiller and Dricus du Plessis’s wedding ceremony a week earlier.



Mia wore a stunning lace and satin ballgown, featuring diamante and pearls, which was designed by Anel Botha. She later changed into a more form-fitting dress for the reception.

Her marketing strategist’s spouse wore a classic black tuxedo.

The wedding ceremony and reception featured elaborate floral displays, drapery, and chandeliers in a beige-and-gold theme. The couple cut their large vanilla-and-strawberry wedding cake.

Take a look at her wedding posts…



MR AND MRS TEN OEVER

Mia Le Roux and Luke ten Oever started dating four years ago after meeting at a New Year’s celebration. They announced their engagement last year.

In his first social media post to his wife, Luke shared on IG: “To a life of memories, to a life spent together. Jy is my hart se punt [the apple of my eye], Mrs ten Oever”

Mia has dedicated several sonnets to her husband, whom she claimed was her biggest supporter.

She previously praised her partner, telling the media, “He understood me, and I understood him. It was easy and effortless. He is gentle, kind and sometimes too precious for this world.”
