Why the Outbreak Is Far Away but Not Distant

The outbreak is caused by the Bundibugyo strain of the Ebola virus. By 4 October 2026 the Democratic Republic of the Congo had reported more than 8,600 confirmed cases and 4,148 deaths, according to Contagion Live’s summary of public health data.

Kenya confirmed an imported case on 6 October, the fourth country to do so in this outbreak at that point. The World Health Organization (WHO) has declared the outbreak a public health emergency of international concern.

No vaccine or specific treatment is approved for Bundibugyo. Care relies on isolation and supportive treatment, which makes trained staff and well-run isolation wards the main defence.

What the US Rules Mean for Johannesburg Travellers

South Africa is not on the US list of affected countries. The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) restricts travel from the Democratic Republic of the Congo, South Sudan and Uganda.

From 11:59 pm Eastern on 3 November 2026, all passengers boarding international flights to the United States, wherever they start, must sign a statement that they were not in the DRC in the previous 21 days. That applies to travellers from every country, including those flying out of Johannesburg.

Non-US citizens who visited South Sudan or Uganda within 21 days cannot enter the United States. US citizens who did must arrive through Washington Dulles, Atlanta or New York JFK for screening.

What Would Test the Plan

The public record shows a plan, not a stress test. We found no published list of the 36 hospitals, no count of isolation beds and no NICD turnaround time for results.

A single imported case would test the chain from airport to isolation ward to laboratory. Several cases at once would show whether 36 hospitals can staff round-the-clock isolation care.

Transparency is the cheapest form of reassurance. Regular NICD updates on suspected cases tested and ruled out would let outsiders judge readiness.

Why It Matters for Business and Travel

Johannesburg’s OR Tambo airport is South Africa’s main international gateway. A fast, credible response protects airlines, hotels and business travel, while a visible failure of infection control could trigger flight cuts and traveller avoidance.

Investors should separate health risk from market risk. A contained imported case would likely cause a short disruption, while a hospital outbreak would raise costs for carriers and insurers.

What It Means for You

If you are flying from South Africa to the United States, the new attestation applies to you like every other passenger. Keep a note of where you have been in the past 21 days and follow screening instructions.

A Johannesburg stopover does not by itself trigger the US entry restrictions, which depend on recent presence in the listed countries. Check airline and CDC notices before departure, especially if you connect through central or eastern Africa.

Anyone with a fever after possible exposure should seek medical advice promptly and say where they have travelled. Ebola spreads through direct contact with the body fluids of a sick person, as Motsoaledi stressed in July.

What We Do Not Know

We do not know which 36 hospitals are on the list, how many negative-pressure isolation rooms they hold, or how much protective equipment is stocked. We also do not know the thresholds for flight restrictions.

We found no public report of a confirmed Ebola case in South Africa as of 24 October 2026. The hospital figures date from July, and we found no October update.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is there Ebola in South Africa right now?

We found no public report of a confirmed case in South Africa as of 24 October 2026. The country is in preparedness mode.

How many hospitals are designated for Ebola?

Health Minister Aaron Motsoaledi said in July 2026 that 36 hospitals are designated to receive suspected cases. Of these, 24 are public and 12 are private.

Does the US ban travellers from Johannesburg?

South Africa is not a restricted country. The CDC restrictions cover the DRC, South Sudan and Uganda.

What is the US attestation rule?

The rule starts after 3 November 2026 at 11:59 pm Eastern time. Every passenger boarding an international flight to the United States must then sign that they were not in the DRC in the previous 21 days.

Who confirms an Ebola case in South Africa?

The National Institute for Communicable Diseases is South Africa’s public-health laboratory. It was reported on high alert and preparing to test suspected cases in July 2026.

Is there an Ebola vaccine?

Not for the Bundibugyo strain behind this outbreak. No vaccine or specific treatment is approved for it, so care is supportive.

World.title: Why Vietnam Gold Sells 14% Above World Price
World.content:
VIETNAM · ANALYSIS

Key Facts — What is happening SJC bars sold at VND141.7 million (about US$5,484) per lượng, about 14% above the world price.

— Why it matters Physical gold in Asia can trade far from the dollar price that US investors see.

— The numbers World-price equivalent: VND124.4 million (US$4,815) per lượng, with spot gold at US$3,994 an ounce.

— Who is who The State Bank of Vietnam is the central bank and gold regulator; SJC is the dominant bar brand.

— What to watch Whether the central bank publishes its first new gold bar production licences.

Vietnamese gold bars sell for about 14% more than the world price of the metal, and a change in the law has not closed the gap. The premium shows how tight supply and one trusted brand can cut a local market off from the global one.

Vietnamese households have long held gold as savings, and the local price now sits well above the global one. This analysis explains the numbers behind it, as flagged in our Asia Intelligence Brief.

Our Asia desk follows the story for readers outside Vietnam. The key question is why a global commodity can sell for so much more in one country.

How the Premium Is Calculated

Vietnamese gold is quoted in lượng, a traditional unit of 37.5 grams, or about 1.21 troy ounces. At the spot price of US$3,994 an ounce (RT, Friday 23 October close) and a rate of 25,840 dong per dollar, one lượng of gold is worth about VND124.4 million (US$4,815).

SJC, the Saigon Jewelry Company, sold its bar at VND141.7 million on 24 October, according to Nhân Dân, the Communist Party daily. That is VND17.3 million (about US$669) above the world-price equivalent, or roughly 14%, before taxes and fees.

Buyers also face a dealer spread. SJC offered to buy back at VND138.7 million (US$5,368), so a customer who resold at once at quoted prices would lose VND3 million (about US$116).

Archive photo: the riverfront business district of Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam’s commercial capital.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Vietnam Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

A Market Built Around One Brand

Since 2012 the rules of Decree 24/2012 have given the State Bank of Vietnam, the central bank, control over gold bar production and gold imports. In practice that made SJC the reference bar for the whole country.

Supply was therefore limited by policy, not by the global market. When demand rose, no importer could simply bring in more bullion and sell it at the higher local price.

That is why the usual arbitrage did not work. In an open market a 14% gap would draw in traders until it closed.

The Law Changed, the Gap Did Not

Decree 232/2025, issued on 26 August 2025 and in force from 10 October 2025, ended the state monopoly on gold bar production. It also allows qualified businesses and banks to import gold directly.

The central bank said in April 2026 that it had received 11 applications for gold bar production licences, from companies and banks, as reported by Vietnam News. Firms need at least VND1 trillion (about US$38.7 million) in charter capital and banks at least VND50 trillion.

We found no public list of licences granted. Until new producers actually sell bars, the practical supply picture changes little, which fits a premium that is still wide in late October.

Why Households Pay Up

Many Vietnamese families hold gold as savings, as protection against inflation and as a store of value outside the banking system. SJC bars are the form most buyers know and trust.

A buyer is therefore paying for a recognised, easily resold product, not only for the metal. If the premium looks permanent, more households may buy to avoid missing out.

Why the Local Price Moved Less

World gold fell US$28.2 an ounce on Friday from the previous close, according to Nhân Dân’s report of 24 October, a drop of under 1%. SJC cut its prices by only VND300,000 (about US$12) per lượng, or about 0.2%.

The smaller move shows the gap between the two markets. A global sell-off does not pass through one-for-one when local supply is tight.

What It Means for US Readers

A US investor who owns gold through an exchange-traded fund or futures pays the world price, not the Vietnamese premium. The SJC gap still shows how a regulated physical market can drift away from the dollar benchmark.

For anyone travelling or living in Vietnam, bars carry the same lesson. The price you pay can include a local premium that disappears if supply rules change.

Gold in dollar terms has also been soft. Spot closed at US$3,994 on 23 October, after US$4,126 on 21 October.

What We Do Not Know

No official source publishes a formula for the SJC premium. Our figure is our own calculation from one day’s quotes, a spot price and an exchange rate, and the real gap shifts through the day.

We also do not know when the central bank will decide on production licences, or how many bar brands will win official standing. Prices from other dealers such as DOJI and PNJ were not part of this check.

What to Watch

Watch for the central bank’s first published licences for gold bar production. New supply is the clearest route to a narrower premium.

Also watch the dong-dollar rate and the buy-sell spread at SJC. A weaker dong raises the local cost of imported gold, while a wider spread usually signals dealer caution.

Frequently Asked Questions

Why is Vietnam gold more expensive than the world price?

Supply is tightly controlled and SJC bars carry a trusted brand. On 24 October 2026 an SJC bar sold for about 14% more than the world-price equivalent.

How big is the SJC gold premium?

On 24 October 2026 an SJC bar sold for VND141.7 million (about US$5,484) per lượng. The world-price equivalent was about VND124.4 million (US$4,815), a gap of roughly 14%.

What is a lượng of gold?

A lượng is a traditional Vietnamese unit of 37.5 grams, about 1.21 troy ounces. International gold prices are quoted per troy ounce, so local prices must be converted.

Did Vietnam end its gold bar monopoly?

Yes, on paper. Decree 232/2025 ended the state monopoly on bar production from 10 October 2025, but we found no public list of newly licensed producers.

Can US investors avoid the Vietnam premium?

Yes. Gold funds and futures in the United States track the dollar spot price, not Vietnamese retail quotes, so they carry no SJC premium.

Will the premium disappear?

It could narrow if new licensed producers add supply or if household demand cools. No official timetable for new licences has been published.

World.title: Obama and Trump Hold Rival Midterm Rallies
World.content:
UNITED STATES · ANALYSIS

Barack Obama and Donald Trump spent Saturday, October 24, on opposite sides of the final midterm push. It is the last full weekend of campaigning before the 2026 US midterm elections on Tuesday, November 3, 2026.

The vote will decide control of the House and Senate, which shapes tariffs, sanctions and immigration policy that reach well beyond US borders. Prediction markets and the latest polls both lean toward the Democrats, but neither is a result.

Key Facts — Who Former President Barack Obama and President Donald Trump are campaigning in rival states.

— What Both are making closing arguments for House and Senate races before Election Day on Tuesday, November 3, 2026.

— Where Obama spoke in Cleveland, Ohio, and Detroit, Michigan; Trump held a rally in Perry, Georgia.

— Early vote More than 20 million ballots had been cast by Friday, October 23.

— Prediction markets Polymarket, 4:53 p.m. ET, October 24: Democrats 92% to win the House, 66.5% for the Senate.

This story is part of our coverage of the 2026 US midterm elections. Dates, times and how to follow it are in our guide. Latest: US Justice Dept Sues Over Alaska Ballot

Two Presidents, Two Strategies

Obama rallied in Cleveland with Democratic Senate candidate Sherrod Brown and governor candidate Amy Acton. He told the crowd that “we’re being driven by fear instead of by hope.”

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

He was also due in Detroit with Michigan Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed and governor nominee Jocelyn Benson. Trump held a rally in Perry, Georgia, on Saturday and is due at McMorran Place Arena in Port Huron, Michigan, on Sunday, October 25.

Michigan began early in-person voting on Saturday and runs it through November 1. Both parties are therefore asking for support in a state where ballots are already being cast.

Unsubscribe with one click in any edition. If you stop opening us for 30 days we stop sending by ourselves, as we assume the interest is no longer there. See our privacy policy. We never share your email.

Money and Early Voting

Early voting is already large: AP, CNN and Catalist data showed more than 20 million ballots cast by Friday. Early-vote totals are a media compilation, not an official federal count, and they do not show which party is ahead.

The Congressional Leadership Fund, a Republican House group, is spending US$9 million in Michigan’s 10th District. A Trump-aligned super PAC is spending more than US$3 million in Montana’s 1st District.

AdImpact, an ad-tracking firm, put ad spending and bookings in the Texas Senate race above US$500 million by mid-October. That makes it one of the most expensive Senate races on record.

What the Polls Say

The New York Times/Siena poll released on Wednesday, October 21, found 36% of likely voters approve of Trump and 59% disapprove. Likely voters preferred the Democratic House candidate in their district by 11 percentage points.

The Harvard Youth Poll, with fieldwork from September 30 to October 7, found likely voters aged 18 to 29 favour Democrats 63% to 26%. Nearly half said their finances had worsened since Trump took office.

The US Capitol, where control of the House and Senate is at stake on November 3 (file photo).

Ask Open the full Ask Rio Times →

What Prediction Markets Say

On Polymarket, the House market priced a Democratic majority at 92.0% and a Republican one at 8.5%, with US$21.3 million traded, at 4:53 p.m. ET on October 24. The Senate market priced Democratic control at 66.5%, with US$9.0 million traded.

These prices are bets, not polls, and a 92% price says nothing about how many seats Democrats would win. Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

Election Security

The Justice Department plans to deploy about 1,000 election monitors, said Harmeet Dhillon of the Justice Department. Senate Democrats will send more than 100 staff to observe in nine states.

Republican Don Bacon and Democrat Josh Gottheimer started a bipartisan pledge for House members to accept election results. Polling hours differ by state, so there is no single national closing time.

What It Means for You

If you hold US stocks or Latin American assets, the House outcome matters most for trade and sanctions policy, and the markets already lean one way. A Democratic House would not change who is president, but it would change what Congress can pass or investigate.

Expect results to arrive state by state on the night of November 3, with close races taking longer.

What Is Not Known

Whether the final weekend of campaigning moves turnout is unknown. Senate control is also less certain than House control, with Texas and Michigan among the races to watch.

Frequently Asked Questions

When is the 2026 US midterm election?

Election Day is Tuesday, November 3, 2026. All 435 House seats and 35 Senate seats are on the ballot.

Where are Obama and Trump campaigning?

Obama spoke in Cleveland, Ohio, and was due in Detroit on Saturday, October 24. Trump held a rally in Perry, Georgia, and is due in Port Huron, Michigan, on Sunday.

What do prediction markets say about the House?

On Polymarket at 4:53 p.m. ET on October 24, a Democratic House majority was priced at 92.0%. These are market prices, not forecasts, and they can move quickly.

How many people have voted early?

More than 20 million ballots had been cast by Friday, October 23, according to AP, CNN and Catalist data. It is a media compilation, not an official federal total.

World.title: El Salvador Expands Haiti Rescue Deployment
World.content:
Haitian National Police graduates march on graduation day, 10 January 2025 (Photo: U.S. Embassy Haiti, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons)

HAITI · EL SALVADOR

Key Facts — Troops About 450 Salvadoran troops are reported in Haiti after 350 landed on Friday, 23 October.

— Missing Four Salvadoran aviation technicians vanished on Sunday, 18 October, after an ambush near Port-au-Prince.

— Where The search covers the Plaine du Cul-de-Sac, a gang-held plain north-east of the capital.

— UN toll The UN says 1,123 people died in gang violence from July to early October.

— Why it matters Haiti’s unrest drives Caribbean migration and tests a UN-authorised force that Washington supports.

This story is part of our coverage of the haiti crisis. Dates, times and how to follow it are in our guide. Latest: Salvadorans Say Pensions Stopped in October

Salvadoran Forces Expand Search

El Salvador has sent about 450 troops to Haiti to look for four missing military technicians, according to AP reporting. About 100 special-forces soldiers arrived on Thursday, 22 October, and roughly 350 more landed on Friday, 23 October.

The search is the latest turn in the Haiti crisis, which The Rio Times follows daily. It adds pressure on a UN-authorised police force that is far below its planned strength.

The soldiers support the Gang Suppression Force (GSF) and the Haitian National Police in the Plaine du Cul-de-Sac, north-east of Port-au-Prince. The GSF said the Salvadoran contingent is assisting operations coordinated with the police and other partners.

File photo, 2008: Port-au-Prince and its bay seen from the UN mission’s headquarters. (Photo: US Navy / Chief Mass Communication Specialist James G. Pinsky, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons)

The four men are aviation technicians who supported medical evacuations, not combat troops, President Nayib Bukele has said. They disappeared on Sunday, 18 October, after armed men ambushed their armoured vehicle near Santo, in the Croix-des-Bouquets area.

Bukele announced the rescue operation on 21 October. El Salvador’s armed forces first said the men escaped the burning vehicle before they vanished.

Gangs and Earlier Attempts

The ambush took place where the Chèn Méchan and 400 Mawozo gangs operate. We found no public evidence showing which group holds the men.

Several attempts to reach them by land and air were hampered by heavy fighting. Wilson Joseph, who leads 400 Mawozo, posted a video saying he would wait for the Salvadorans and not flee.

The GSF replaced the Kenyan-led police mission, so this is a major test of how it works in gang territory. Haitian authorities have called the men’s recovery a priority.

UN Counts a Deepening Crisis

The UN told the Security Council on 19 October that gang violence killed 1,123 people and injured 440 from July to early October. The GSF had 1,563 uniformed members as of 12 October, against 5,550 authorised.

Nearly 1.5 million Haitians are displaced, the UN says. More than 35 political parties and 3,500 candidates have registered for a vote that has no firm date.

UN envoy Carlos Ruiz Massieu warned that setting election dates without a realistic check on feasibility would erode public confidence. For background, see our explainers What Is Happening in Haiti? and El Salvador Troops Reach Haiti to Find 4.

What It Means for US Readers

Haiti’s gang war is a Caribbean problem on America’s doorstep, tied to migration pressure and to a UN force that Washington supports. A bigger Salvadoran presence shows regional partners will send troops, though numbers remain well short of the mission’s target.

Readers with ties to the region should watch whether the four men are found, because a failed rescue could weaken support for the force. Travel to Haiti remains unsafe for outsiders.

What Is Not Known

The whereabouts and condition of the four technicians are unknown. Officials have not said whether the expanded search has produced contact, a rescue or an arrest.

The troop total is not officially confirmed. Early reports spoke of about 200 soldiers, while later AP reporting said 350 more landed on Friday, which gives about 450.

Sources

UN News (Security Council briefing, 19 October 2026); The Haitian Times (23 October 2026); The Gleaner (24 October 2026); AP (23 October 2026); Gang Suppression Force statement as reported.

This article was produced by The Rio Times’ automated newsroom system. How we use AI · Report an error · Editorial responsibility: Matthias Camenzind, Editor-in-Chief

Frequently Asked Questions

How many Salvadoran troops are now in Haiti?

About 450, according to AP reporting: roughly 100 arrived on Thursday and 350 on Friday. Earlier reports spoke of about 200, and officials have not confirmed a total.

Who are the four missing men?

They are Salvadoran aviation technicians who supported medical evacuations for the security mission, according to President Bukele. They disappeared after an ambush on Sunday, 18 October.

Which gangs operate where the attack happened?

The Chèn Méchan and 400 Mawozo gangs operate around Santo in the Croix-des-Bouquets area. No group has been publicly shown to hold the men.

What is the Gang Suppression Force?

It is the UN-authorised force that replaced the Kenyan-led mission. It had 1,563 uniformed members on 12 October, against 5,550 authorised.

World.title: Brazil Asks Court to Ease Indigenous Voting
World.content:
The Superior Electoral Court building in Brasília, pictured in December 2007. File photo; it does not show the court's handling of AI posts. Photo: José Cruz / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 3.0 br)

BRAZIL · ELECTIONS

Published Saturday, 24 October, 3:34 p.m. ET · Source: Brazil’s Prosecutor General’s Office (PGR)

Key Facts What happened On Saturday 24 October, Brazil’s attorney general asked the Supreme Court to suspend part of an electoral court order on Indigenous voter transport.

The rule Federal agencies must get a judge’s approval for each trip, with routes and schedules, before carrying Indigenous voters.

Why it matters Some river journeys must start on Saturday, a day before the Sunday 25 October runoff.

Power Index Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 75.0 points (October 2026 edition).

Prediction markets Polymarket gives Flávio Bolsonaro an 83.5% chance of winning the 25 October runoff (24 October, 3:30 p.m. ET). Polymarket puts Flávio Bolsonaro’s chance of winning at 83% and Kalshi at 83% (Lula: 18% and 18% ), as of 24 October, 5:40 pm ET ; prices are bets, not polls.

Still open The Supreme Court had not ruled when the reports were published.

Brazil’s attorney general, Paulo Gonet, asked the Supreme Court (STF) on Saturday 24 October to suspend part of a ruling by the electoral court (TSE) on how Indigenous voters reach polling stations. The ruling, issued on Friday 23 October at 7:06 p.m. ET (8:06 p.m. in Brasília) by TSE president Kassio Nunes Marques, comes one day before the Sunday runoff between President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro.

Brazil Election Data Room Runoff poll average: Flávio Bolsonaro 51.0 %, Lula 49.0 % 43 national polls from 20 pollsters since 4 October, updated hourly. Every poll, free to download. Open the Data Room · Download the CSV · Embed the chart

Our guide to the Brazil runoff date has the full schedule.

The order says federal agencies must ask an electoral judge before each transport operation. In the Brazil election 2026 runoff, that rule reaches some of the country’s most remote voters, including communities that travel by boat for hours.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Brazil ranks 1st of 14 with 75.0 points. Strongest pillar: military means (100); weakest: state capacity & security (56). Alignment group: Hedging. WatchRating below investment grade (BB); public debt at 93% of GDP. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

What the Electoral Court Ordered

Nunes Marques decided that public bodies may carry voters only after prior and express authorisation from the electoral judge, O Liberal reported. The request must name the vehicles or boats, drivers, routes, stops and times.

He refused to treat vehicles and boats of three federal bodies as pre-approved, according to CNN Brasil. They are Funai, the national Indigenous affairs agency, the Indigenous Health Secretariat (Sesai) and the Ministry of Indigenous Peoples.

Why the Attorney General Objects

Gonet argues that the order came on Friday evening, leaving too little time to approve each trip before Sunday. He says some river journeys have to begin on Saturday, Estadão reported.

In the filing, he said that approval within two days amounts, in practice, to no transport at all, according to Folha de S.Paulo. He added that agencies might stop trips for fear of being held responsible.

What the Prosecutor Wants Instead

The PGR asks the Supreme Court to restore earlier decisions by a federal court in Pará state and the federal government’s own transport plan. That plan has Funai, the Indigenous ministry and security forces working together.

Gonet says inspection should protect the neutrality of the vote without blocking anyone from reaching a polling station. He argues the transport plan should go ahead without waiting for case-by-case approval.

The glass facade of the electoral court building in Brasília. File photo. (Photo: Luiz Roberto/TSE, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons)

What It Means for US Readers

For readers following Brazil from the United States, this is a dispute about access to the ballot, not about a candidate. The main risk is to confidence in the process if remote communities cannot reach their polling stations.

Investors in Brazilian assets will watch whether the Supreme Court acts before Sunday, because court fights over voting rules can add noise to a close race.

What Prediction Markets Say

On Polymarket, bettors give Flávio Bolsonaro an 83.5% chance of winning the 25 October runoff, and Lula 16.5% (24 October, 3:30 p.m. ET). The “Brazil Presidential Election” market has drawn about US$195.1 million in bets.

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

Prediction markets · who wins the runoff Implied chance of winning Brazil’s presidency on 25 October, from traders’ prices. Polymarket Flávio Bolsonaro 82.7% · Lula 17.5% (US$195 million traded) Kalshi (regulated in the US by the CFTC) Flávio Bolsonaro 83% · Lula 18% As of 24 October, 5:40 pm ET (22:40 Lisbon), updated every 20 minutes. Prices are bets, not polls, and can move fast. Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them. Want prediction market reports on Brazil? Get yours free, right after you confirm →

What Is Not Known

The Supreme Court has not said when it will rule or which justice will handle the request. It is also not known how many voters depend on state-organised transport and how many trips have already left.

The reports reviewed do not include a public response from the electoral court. This article will be updated if either court publishes a decision.

More: Brazil news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Background: Brazil Election Polls: Flávio 51%, Lula 49%.

Background: Brazil Tax Reform 2026 Replaces Five Taxes With Two VATs.

Frequently Asked Questions

Why did Brazil’s attorney general go to the Supreme Court?

He asked it on Saturday 24 October to suspend part of an electoral court order on Indigenous voter transport. He says the rule cannot be met before the runoff.

What does the electoral court rule require?

Federal agencies need a judge’s prior approval for each trip. Requests must list vehicles or boats, drivers, routes, stops and times.

Who made the ruling?

Kassio Nunes Marques, president of the electoral court (TSE), issued it on Friday 23 October, at 7:06 p.m. ET (8:06 p.m. in Brasília).

When is Brazil’s runoff?

Brazilians vote on Sunday 25 October. The runoff is between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro.

Has the Supreme Court ruled yet?

Not in the reports we reviewed on Saturday 24 October. We will update this article if it does.

World.title: Brazil Court Orders Lula Shirt Videos Pulled
World.content:
The Supreme Federal Court building in Brasília seen from the side at night (Photo: Dasfour2022, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons)

BRAZIL · ELECTIONS

Published Saturday, 24 October, 2:25 pm ET · Source: Brazil’s electoral court decision, as reported by SBT News

Key Facts The country Brazil, Latin America’s largest country, elects its president in a runoff on Sunday 25 October.

What happened On Friday 23 October, electoral court minister Estela Aranha ordered the removal of social media videos linking Lula’s party to drug suspects.

The videos They show three detainees, two adults and a 17-year-old, in shirts backing Lula after an arrest in Piracicaba, São Paulo state.

The dispute Military police are accused of forcing the shirts on the detainees, and the police ombudsman is investigating.

Power Index Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 75.0 points (October 2026 edition).

Prediction markets Kalshi, regulated in the US by the CFTC, prices a Flávio Bolsonaro win by at least 1 point at 78% and a Lula win by at least 1 point at 14% (24 October, 2:25 p.m. ET). Polymarket puts Flávio Bolsonaro’s chance of winning at 84% and Kalshi at 83% (Lula: 17% and 17% ), as of 24 October, 6:40 pm ET ; prices are bets, not polls.

Still open The court has not ruled on the facts, and the origin of the shirts is disputed.

Brazil’s electoral court has ordered the removal of videos that show suspected drug dealers in campaign shirts of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, two days before the runoff. Minister Estela Aranha of the electoral court (TSE) decided on Friday 23 October that the posts wrongly tie Lula’s Workers’ Party (PT) to crime, SBT News reported.

Brazil Election Data Room Runoff poll average: Flávio Bolsonaro 51.0 %, Lula 49.0 % 43 national polls from 20 pollsters since 4 October, updated hourly. Every poll, free to download. Open the Data Room · Download the CSV · Embed the chart

The order lands in the last weekend of the Brazil election 2026 campaign, between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro, senator for Rio de Janeiro. For readers abroad, it shows how far Brazilian judges will go to police online campaign content, which matters for platforms and investors watching the vote.

What the Court Ordered

The videos show three people detained in Piracicaba, in São Paulo state: two adults and a 17-year-old, SBT News reported. The shirts read “Professores da Apeoesp com Lula”, or “Apeoesp teachers with Lula”, according to SBT.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Brazil ranks 1st of 14 with 75.0 points. Strongest pillar: military means (100); weakest: state capacity & security (56). Alignment group: Hedging. Senators-elect Guilherme Derrite of the Progressistas party (PP) and Carlos Jordy of the Liberal Party (PL), which backs Flávio Bolsonaro, published the videos, Tribuna do Sertão reported. They also spread on the WhatsApp channel “Tropa do Flávio”.

Lula’s coalition filed an urgent petition, SBT News reported. The order covered posts on X, Instagram and the WhatsApp channel.

Why the Judge Said the Posts Went Too Far

Aranha wrote that the content uses a specific police episode to present a link between the PT and crime as fact, O Antagonista reported. She said suspects wearing a candidate’s shirt does not allow the conclusion that a link exists with that candidate or his party, Bahia Notícias reported.

The images, in her words, “exceed, in principle, the limits of political-electoral criticism”, Tribuna do Sertão reported. The Portuguese original is “ultrapassa, em princípio, os limites da crítica político-eleitoral”.

The Dispute Over the Shirts

Military police officers are accused of forcing the three to wear the shirts after the stop, SBT News and Tribuna do Sertão reported. Bahia Notícias said the decision did not weigh the detainees’ testimony.

The teenager’s mother told SBT News that her son left home in a blue sleeveless shirt and that police forced him to change. The Civil Police registered the case as possible threat, coercion and abuse of authority, and the Military Police ombudsman opened an investigation, O Antagonista reported.

What It Means for US Readers

The ruling shows Brazil’s electoral court acting against campaign content on social platforms in the final days. If you follow Brazilian markets or ADRs, more such orders are possible until the result is certified.

Decisions like this one can also feed each side’s claims of bias before and after the vote. Our Brazil election polls page tracks the race itself.

It is not known who put the shirts on the detainees, which police and the ombudsman are investigating. It is also unclear whether Derrite, Jordy or the channel will appeal.

World.title: Panama Names Soldier Lost in US Invasion
World.content:
Panama: History and Justice

Key Facts Who. Roberto Adolfo Aparicio Oliva, a 21-year-old Panamanian soldier, identified by DNA.

What. Remains identified after more than 36 years of his family’s search.

Where. He died in El Chorrillo, Panama City, on the day of the US invasion.

When. Died 20 December 1989; commission announced the identification on 24 October 2026.

Status. As of 24 October 2026, 18:10 GMT

Panama has put a name to a young soldier who died on the first day of the US invasion in 1989, and whose family never stopped looking for him.

Panama’s state commission on the 1989 invasion announced on 24 October 2026 that DNA has identified the remains of Roberto Adolfo Aparicio Oliva. He was a 21-year-old soldier who died in the El Chorrillo district of Panama City on 20 December 1989, the day of the US invasion.

The US military invaded Panama that day to remove General Manuel Noriega. For American readers, this identification is a reminder that a US military operation left a human aftermath that Panama is still working through.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Panama ranks 11th of 14 with 34.2 points. Strongest pillar: state capacity & security (64); weakest: military means (11). Alignment group: Closer to Washington. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

What We Know

The Comisión 20 de Diciembre de 1989 is the Panamanian state commission that investigates the victims of the invasion. It said the remains were identified through DNA after more than 36 years of searching by his family.

According to the commission’s account, Aparicio served as an agent, meaning an enlisted soldier, of Batallón 2000, a unit based in Chepo. He was assigned to the reconnaissance section at the Cuartel Central, the headquarters of the Panama Defence Forces.

He was promoted after his death to cabo segundo, or second corporal, by Decree 228 of 31 May 1990. His parents were Félix Adolfo Aparicio Pérez and Lidia Maritza Oliva Gómez, and the family lived in Cerro Batea, in the San Miguelito district.

The newspapers La Prensa, La Estrella de Panamá and El Siglo, all in Panama City, reported the news on 24 October 2026. El Siglo described the case as 36 years of pain and waiting.

His family had been told that he died, but they could never find his body. They searched hospitals and cemeteries and followed exhumations for 36 years.

Sunset over the Pacific in Panama. File photo. Photo: Héctor Ruíz Palma, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

Why the Search Took 36 Years

His remains were buried in a common grave at the Jardín de Paz cemetery. They were heavily carbonised, which made recovering genetic material a scientific challenge.

The Fundación de Antropología Forense de Guatemala, a forensic anthropology foundation, extracted the DNA and built a genetic profile. Panama’s Instituto de Medicina Legal y Ciencias Forenses, the national forensic medicine institute, then compared that profile with reference samples from the family.

The comparison took place within an investigation by the Ministerio Público, Panama’s prosecutors. The reports do not say how long the laboratory work took.

This case follows earlier work that we covered when Panama began exhuming victims of the 1989 invasion. On 19 December 2025, La Prensa reported that prosecutors had identified 11 people from remains exhumed at collective graves in the Jardín de Paz and Monte Esperanza cemeteries.

La Prensa added that 21 samples had been sent to the Guatemalan foundation at that point. The identification of Aparicio is a further result of the same slow process of DNA comparison and justice.

What Is Not Known

The commission has not said on which date the DNA match was completed. It has also not said whether the remains will be handed to the family, or when.

It is not known how many people are still missing. Details about the cause of his death are also not known.

The announcements reported so far do not settle these questions. We will report further details once Panama’s authorities publish them.

What It Means for US Readers

The invasion was a US military operation, and its victims are still being identified more than three decades later. The total number of dead has never been settled, so each identification matters to the historical record.

In December 2025, commission president Rolando Murgas Torraza said the commission should become permanent to preserve historical memory. La Prensa also reported that the commission’s funding for 2026 was uncertain.

The inquiry runs through Panamanian prosecutors and forensic scientists. Experts from Guatemala supplied the genetic analysis that made this match possible.

Identifications are slow because many remains lie in collective graves. What happens next for the commission and for this family has not been announced.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who was Roberto Adolfo Aparicio Oliva?

He was a 21-year-old enlisted soldier of Batallón 2000 who died in El Chorrillo, Panama City, on 20 December 1989. He was promoted after death to second corporal.

How was he identified?

A Guatemalan forensic foundation extracted DNA from his heavily carbonised remains. Panama’s forensic medicine institute then compared it with samples from his family.

Who announced the identification?

Panama’s Comisión 20 de Diciembre de 1989, the state commission on the invasion victims, announced it on 24 October 2026. It followed more than 36 years of searching by his family.

Will the remains be returned to the family?

The commission has not said whether the remains will be handed over, or when. That detail has not been announced.

World.title: Rosado Got To Go: House Speaker calls for removal of Alexis Rosado — ‘Unconscionable form of gaslighting’ for complainant; ‘Powerful men are protected, they matter more’
World.content:
Rosado Got To Go: House Speaker calls for removal of Alexis Rosado — ‘Unconscionable form of gaslighting’ for complainant; ‘Powerful men are protected, they matter more’

By Breaking Belize News Staff: In an extraordinary public statement that puts her directly at odds with Prime Minister John Briceño and Foreign Minister Francis Fonseca, Speaker of the House of Representatives Valerie Woods has made a forceful case for Ambassador Alexis Rosado’s removal as Belize’s Co-Agent before the International Court of Justice (ICJ), arguing that his continued appointment while facing serious sexual offence charges compromises the country’s credibility and inflicts further distress on the complainant.

Woods, a longtime member of the People’s United Party (PUP), has publicly challenged the position of her own party’s leadership, questioning whether Rosado’s continued appointment represents an exception being made for a powerful individual.

In her statement titled “The Co-Agent Exception,” Woods writes:

“If, at this stage, there is still an insistence on his keeping the position, it raises the question whether the high-profile title is being used as a kind of unspoken influence.”

She goes further, stating:

“The message to anyone who is observing is that Mr. Rosado is an extremely important person in the eyes of the state and exceptions should be made for him.”

Her remarks follow Prime Minister Briceño’s public defence of Rosado earlier this week, when he declared that removing the ambassador at this critical stage would not be in Belize’s national interest.

“The ‘existential’ nature of Belize’s ICJ case cannot be used to justify keeping him as Co-Agent,” Woods counters.

She maintains that removing or replacing Rosado, based on the information publicly available, would not prejudice Belize’s territorial case against Guatemala.

Woods also directly challenges Foreign Minister Francis Fonseca’s explanation that the Government is following the advice of Belize’s lead agent, Assad Shoman, who considers Rosado vital to the ongoing preparation of the case.

“Whatever value Mr. Rosado brought to the preparation of the case is largely spent. He is not the lead Co-Agent and will not argue the case,” Woods states.

She argues that Belize’s written submissions have already been filed, hearing dates have been established, and responsibility for presenting the case rests with experienced international lawyers.

She consequently describes claims that Rosado is indispensable to the country’s case as exaggerated.

But perhaps the most striking aspect of the Speaker’s intervention is her defence of the complainant and her criticism of the message being sent to women and girls by the Government’s continued support for Rosado.

“For the complainant, this must be an unconscionable form of gaslighting that is unfolding publicly and compounding the distress of the proceedings,” Woods declares.

She warns that retaining Rosado in such a prominent position undermines the country’s efforts to confront sexual violence.

“It sends troubling messages, particularly to women and girls, that high ranking, powerful men are protected, they matter more, they are shielded from institutional consequences.”

Woods also invokes Belize’s commitments under the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child, the 2022 national parliamentary Domestic Violence in Belize Motion, the 2026 Blue Teddy Bear campaign and the annual 16 Days of Activism to End Gender-Based Violence.

She questions how the Government can reconcile those commitments with its decision to maintain Rosado in his prominent international assignment while he faces serious criminal charges. Her argument raises questions about the consistency of Belize’s commitments rather than establishing a legal violation of any convention.

The Speaker further points out that Rosado resigned from his diplomatic postings after being charged in April 2022, arguing that the same considerations that justified protecting the integrity of those offices should apply to his continued ICJ appointment.

Woods acknowledges that Rosado remains innocent until proven guilty, but maintains that the presumption of innocence does not prevent a public official from stepping aside while criminal proceedings are pending.

The intervention comes just hours after Breaking Belize News raised this very issue in a public discussion on Saturday morning, comparing Rosado’s continued professional appointment with the situation involving Pastor Kevin Tzib, founder of Dunamis Ministries, who was recently charged with seven sexual offences and subsequently released on bail.

BBN asked whether Tzib should similarly be allowed to continue his ministry if Rosado can remain in his ICJ role with the support of the Prime Minister and Foreign Minister, and questioned what distinguishes the two situations. Dunamis Ministries has announced that it will take administrative measures, although the precise restrictions on Tzib’s ministerial duties have not been publicly established.

Woods’ statement addresses the broader questions of the presumption of innocence, public accountability and whether individuals facing serious criminal allegations should remain in positions of trust.

The statement is especially significant because it places the Speaker of the House in direct public disagreement with the Prime Minister and Foreign Minister on a matter involving Belize’s most consequential international legal proceedings.

Woods concludes by rejecting the suggestion that the importance of the ICJ case should shield any individual appointment from reconsideration.

“No individual appointment is beyond recall,” she declares.

“The importance of Belize’s case before the ICJ is not a reason to tolerate the avoidable reputational risk of retaining Mr. Rosado in the position of Co-Agent.”

She maintains that, as Belize prepares to present its case before the ICJ, it is precisely the importance of those proceedings that demands a rethink of Rosado’s continued appointment.

World.title: Mayor of Belmopan, councilors complete Good Governance Training at Galen University
World.content:
Mayor of Belmopan, councilors complete Good Governance Training at Galen University

By Zoila Palma: Belmopan Mayor Pablo Cawich and councilors of the Belmopan City Council have completed a 14-week Good Governance Training programme at Galen University, in collaboration with the U.S. Embassy.

The training focused on strengthening leadership and governance as the council continues its work to serve residents and advance development in the capital.

The council emphasized that leadership carries a responsibility and commitment to public service, noting that continued learning and growth are essential to improving governance and moving Belmopan forward.

World.title: International News: Thousands rally for Lula and Bolsonaro as Brazil braces for tight Presidential runoff
World.content:
International News: Thousands rally for Lula and Bolsonaro as Brazil braces for tight Presidential runoff

By Zoila Palma: Thousands of supporters of Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and right-wing senator Flávio Bolsonaro took to the streets today as the candidates made their final appeals ahead of a closely contested presidential runoff election. Lula supporters filled Rio de Janeiro’s Copacabana beach with the red colours of his Workers’ Party, while hundreds of bikers and other supporters rallied behind Bolsonaro in Belo Horizonte.

The rallies capped a bitter campaign that has deepened political divisions in Latin America’s largest country, AFP reports.

Lula, who turns 81 next week, waved a large Brazilian flag from a campaign truck as he addressed the crowd in Rio de Janeiro. He urged voters to choose between someone who respects Brazil’s national flag and someone who embraces the American flag.

Meanwhile, Bolsonaro’s supporters expressed confidence in his chances after he secured 47 percent of the vote in the first round, compared with Lula’s 45 percent.

A Datafolha Institute poll released during the week showed the candidates tied at 50 percent of voting intentions.

The election has drawn attention across the region as Brazil considers whether to continue under left-wing leadership or join a broader political shift toward the right.

World.title: BDF’s Lt. Col. Kenroy Smith receives prestigious Brazilian military aviation honour
World.content:
BDF’s Lt. Col. Kenroy Smith receives prestigious Brazilian military aviation honour

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): A Belize Defence Force officer has been honoured by the Brazilian Air Force.

Lieutenant Colonel Kenroy Smith, Commanding Officer of the BDF Air Wing, was awarded the Order of Aeronautical Merit in the grade of Grand Officer.

The award was presented by Brazil’s Ambassador to Belize, His Excellency Olyntho Vieira, during a ceremony at the Embassy of Brazil in Belmopan on Friday, October 23, as part of Brazilian Aviation Day.

The Order of Aeronautical Merit is a distinguished decoration of the Brazilian Air Force, recognizing outstanding service and exceptional contributions to military aviation and aeronautical development.

The BDF says the honour reflects Lt. Col. Smith’s significant contributions to military aviation, regional cooperation and stronger ties between the BDF and Brazil’s armed forces.

The Commander and members of the BDF congratulated him, saying his dedication and professionalism continue to bring distinction to the Force and to Belize.

World.title: International News: Vance becomes 11th Pacific hurricane this season
World.content:
International News: Vance becomes 11th Pacific hurricane this season

By Zoila Palma: Hurricane Vance became the 11th major hurricane of the 2026 central and eastern Pacific hurricane season on Friday, as meteorologists monitored its movement toward Mexico’s west-central coast.

According to AccuWeather, the storm briefly reached Category 3 status on the Saffir-Simpson Hurricane Wind Scale, with maximum sustained winds of at least 111 miles per hour. Forecasters are tracking multiple possible scenarios, including one in which the hurricane remains offshore and another in which it turns toward the Mexican coast.

Vance developed after an area of disturbed weather strengthened into a tropical depression on Wednesday before becoming a tropical storm four hours later. It intensified into a hurricane early Friday, with sustained winds reaching 90 miles per hour by 9 a.m. Friday.

AccuWeather Hurricane Expert Alex DaSilva said the storm could remain over open waters but warned that a northeast turn toward Mexico’s west-central coast could result in more dangerous conditions.

World.title: Belize Coast Guard cadet Elvis Solis completes major milestone in Mexico
World.content:
Belize Coast Guard cadet Elvis Solis completes major milestone in Mexico

By Zoila Palma: The Belize Coast Guard (BCG) is congratulating Cadet Elvis Solis on successfully completing four years of academic and military training in Naval Nursing at the Centro de Estudios Navales en Ciencias de la Salud (CENCIS), under Mexico’s Naval University. The achievement marks a significant milestone in his journey toward becoming a qualified naval nurse.

Solis’s accomplishment reflects the Belize Coast Guard’s continued investment in developing its future leaders and specialized personnel. The training equips cadets with the academic knowledge and military skills necessary to support healthcare services within the naval force.

Following the successful completion of this phase of training, Solis will be commissioned into the Belize Coast Guard at the rank of Lieutenant Junior Grade before proceeding to his fifth and final year of professional training.

Upon successfully completing the final year, he will qualify for a Bachelor’s Degree in Naval Nursing.

The Belize Coast Guard commended Solis for his dedication, perseverance and commitment to excellence.

The Belize Coast Guard also expressed appreciation to the Government of Mexico and the Mexican Navy for their continued partnership and support in advancing the professional development of Belizean personnel.

World.title: BDF officer cadets participate in selection process for U.S. Army Officer candidate school
World.content:
BDF officer cadets participate in selection process for U.S. Army Officer candidate school

By Zoila Palma: Belize Defence Force (BDF) officer cadets have participated in a selection process for the opportunity to attend the United States Army Officer Candidate School (OCS), marking an important step in their military careers and professional development.

The process provides aspiring officers with an opportunity to demonstrate their readiness for the responsibilities of commissioned service.

The selection process is intended to identify candidates prepared to meet the demands of military leadership and serve with dedication. For the participating cadets, the opportunity represents more than selection, as it also involves preparing to lead with integrity, accept responsibility and uphold the professional standards expected of a BDF officer.

The Commander of the Belize Defence Force commended all participating officer cadets for their dedication and willingness to undertake the challenge of pursuing professional development through OCS. The Commander noted that their ambition reflects the importance of developing capable leaders who can contribute meaningfully to the Force and the country.

The BDF Force Headquarters and Training and Doctrine Battalion extended their best wishes to the candidates as they continue their journey toward commissioned service.

World.title: Belize Defence Force Air Wing commander receives Brazilian Order of Aeronautical Merit
World.content:
Belize Defence Force Air Wing commander receives Brazilian Order of Aeronautical Merit

By Zoila Palma: Lieutenant Colonel Kenroy Smith, Commanding Officer of the Belize Defence Force (BDF) Air Wing, has been awarded the Order of Aeronautical Merit in the grade of Grand Officer (Grande Oficial) by the Government of Brazil.

The award was presented by Brazil’s Ambassador to Belize, Olyntho Vieira, during a ceremony at the Brazilian Embassy in Belmopan on October 23, 2026, as part of the observance of Brazilian Aviation Day.

The Order of Aeronautical Merit is a distinguished Brazilian Air Force decoration that recognizes outstanding service and exceptional contributions to military aviation and aeronautical development.

Smith’s recognition highlights his contributions to advancing military aviation, strengthening regional cooperation and building professional ties between the Belize Defence Force and Brazil’s armed forces.

The BDF congratulated Smith on the achievement, commending his dedication, professionalism and commitment to excellence.

The BDF also expressed appreciation to the Government and people of Brazil for their longstanding support in defence, security, training and military professional development.

World.title: Beenie Man faces Trinidadian backlash again, seeks to clear air
World.content:
Dancehall artiste Beenie Man

For the second time in just under two years, dancehall superstar Beenie Man is seeking to clear the air after offending the people of Trinidad and Tobago.

The Girls Dem Sugar deejay stirred controversy earlier this week when, during an interview on New York’s Hot 97, he apparently suggsted that Jamaica started carnival celebrations before Trinidad and Tobago, attributing its origins to late Jamaican music pioneer Byron Lee.

Carnival has deep historical roots in Trinidad and Tobago and several other Caribbean islands, with the celebration originating during the period of slavery. In contrast, Jamaica only began celebrating carnival on a national level in the early 1990s.

Against that background, Beenie Man has been chided across social media since his remarks surfaced online.

On Saturday, in a video posted to social media, he said his comments were misconstrued.

“Let me clear up this with love for you, I was just only speaking about my experience with carnival in Jamaica and the role that Byron Lee play in our carnival,” Beenie Man said. “I could never ever come and steal away nothing from Trinidad.

“I don’t speak with Trinidad with hate, I love Trinidad… and I know that Trinidad loves me,” he added.

He further clarified: “My experience with Byron Lee and what he has done for carnival is the big [truck] and the road march, and marching with the streets with the music… this is my experience that I grew up in my country… So please don’t get me wrong, Trinidad carnival is Trinidad carnival, it started from way back when.”

In February 2025, the dancehall icon apologised to Trinidadians over comments he made on ‘doubles’, a popular food item in the twin island republic.

READ: Beenie Man gives heartfelt apology to Trinidadians in ‘doubles’ spat

In an interview on popular US podcast Drink Champs, the Who Am I singer said that a soca artiste had told him that stray dogs won’t eat doubles and he decided to try a little behavioural experiment to test the hypothesis with the channa-and-bara favourite. But the stray dog declined.

World.title: Security forces reacted to deadly force at Sligoville – McKay
World.content:
Jason McKay

Criminologist Dr Jason McKay has warned against “Monday-morning-quarterbacking” in the wake of the deadly shootout involving members of the security forces last week, which resulted in the death of two policemen and three alleged gunmen in Sligoville, St Catherine.

McKay, a trained hostage negotiator and serving member of the Jamaica Constabulary Force (JCF) assigned to the St Catherine South Special Operations team, pointed to questions raised in the media by former commissioner of police, Rear Admiral Hardley Lewin, and Security Consultant Robert Finzi-Smith.

Addressing the deadly standoff in which a 10-year-old girl was shot and injured, allegedly used as a human shield by the occupants, Rear Admiral Lewin questioned whether “there was an alternative way of dealing with this?”, suggesting the security forces had enough time to coax a possible surrender.

“There was, available to the operation, some 12 hours of daylight,” Rear Admiral Lewin remarked, referring to the firefight sparked by a 5:15 am attempt by the security forces to apprehend “criminals and wanted persons” in the Five/Six Mile area of Sligoville.

“It’s not something that was dusk. There are things that would have to be looked at, in any hot-washer that the police would do, to look at whether there was an alternative way of dealing with this. Did the men have a chance of escaping? Who was in that room that might be innocent?” Rear Admiral Lewin asked, questioning the tactics employed by the security forces.

However, McKay, who stood by as an International Cricket Council-required JCF hostage negotiator for any eventuality that might have arisen at the 2007 Cricket World Cup staged in Jamaica, pointed to specific circumstances under which a negotiator would be called in as opposed to additional support from tactical teams.

“Hostage negotiators generally get involved if there is a lull during a shooting. There was no lull. It was either constant or sporadic gunfire coming from the house, even during what appeared to be conversations between the occupants and the security forces, creating a high level of distrust among the police during which two of their own were shot and killed.

“Hostage negotiations do not take place in the middle of shootouts. Once there is sustained or sporadic shooting, it is the tactical operators who handle active shooting scenes,” McKay pointed out.

A widely-circulated 18-minute long telephone conversation involving two men engaging members of the security forces, indicating their willingness to leave the house, while claiming there was only one shooter, has been the subject of widespread debate.

One of the men was overheard encouraging the 10-year-old to scream, which, McKay said, could have been coercion to deceive the police, pointing out that even while the men were engaging the security forces a shot rang out from inside the house, triggering gunfire from what was by then a joint military-police team.

Finzi-Smth, former senior director, safety and security, at the University of Technology, alluded to the number of rounds fired by the security forces while there were “non-combatants in the house”, an assertion McKay called out as being not from an informed position.

“It became obvious that there were non-combatants in the house,” said Finzi-Smith. “You fire aimed shots. You don’t fire shots that find wherever they want to find, especially when there are non-combatants in the way,” he stated.

McKay, however, pointed out that before such an assertion can be made, one would have to determine at which point the greater volume of firepower was laid down by the police, whether the gun battle intensified after the child was removed.

“It is difficult to determine whether the bulk of the police’s shooting was during or after the child was out of the house. There was a point in time that the situation would have become a subject barricaded with a high-powered firearm.

“It is easy to Monday-morning-quarter back but, it is my personal opinion that if you are not the one going through the experience, being mindful that two of your fellow officers were killed after the initial engagement, enough gunfire to wound other security-forces personnel, the rate of return-fire would have been unquestionably above average.

“It was a threatening situation that had already proven to be deadly,” McKay reminded, pointing to his experiences of being involved in high-risk entries as a member of a special-operations team for almost 25 years.

World.title: Holness signals imminent changes to tackle red tape
World.content:
Prime Minister Dr Andrew Holness speaks during the official launch of the Jamaica Reconstruction and Resilience Oversight Committee (JAMRROC) at Jamaica House in Kingston, where he addressed the ongoing recovery of Jamaica’s education system and defended the use of outdoor spaces for learning while some schools undergo repairs following Hurricane Melissa. (Photo: Karl Mclarty)

Prime Minister Andrew Holness says in the coming days the government will be announcing measures aimed at increasing efficiency across Government, making the bureaucracy more functional and improving service delivery to Jamaicans post-Hurricane Melissa.

The prime minister says the changes are necessary to increase the capacity of the Government to respond to current challenges.

Holness gave the update when he addressed a group of private sector leaders who attended an event on Thursday at the Terra Nova Hotel in St Andrew. The event was hosted by Cabinet Minister Daryl Vaz.

“We are a free country socially, but we are not a free country economically,” Holness said. “If we are going to address the issue of poverty in our country, we must address the issue of our bureaucuracy.

“We can’t get rid of bureaucracy, but we must make our bureaucracy make sense, it must be efficient,” the prime minister said.

The prime minister pointed to red tape for the lengthy time it has taken for the delivery of modular homes to families impacted by Hurricane Melissa.

“We imported the modular houses almost six months ago, and we are still not able to have them rolled out and built quickly… between the logistics, the contracting, the permitting, procurement, it is as if no one cares that it’s an emergency,” Holness said.

He said it was critical that Jamaicans in need are able to receive assistance much more quickly to mitigate their distress and improve their well-being and welfare.

“In the coming days, the government will be making certain announcements which will signal a change in how we do business,” Holness said.

World.title: Derrick Harriott, celebrated singer and producer, dead at 87
World.content:
Derrick Harriott

KINGSTON, Jamaica — Derrick Harriott, the reggae and rocksteady singer and producer known for hits including The Loser, has died.

The iconic Jamaican singer began his career as part of a duo in his teens alongside Claude Sang, gaining recognition after winning the Vere Johns Opportunity Hour talent contest as early as 1957.

Harriott would become part of a group, the Jiving Juniors, before going solo in the 1960s and releasing hits including What Can I Do and I’m Only Human.

He was also a talented producer, presiding over successful albums for several other artistes including DJ Scotty and Dennis Brown.

Harriott, whose discography encompassed sounds of ska, rocksteady and reggae, was awarded the Order of Distinction in 2009 for his contribution to the development of music locally.

Harriott was 87 at the time of his passing

World.title: Money worries
World.content:
JETS moved to allay fears that its MultiLink system, on which automated banking machines (ABMs) heavily rely, was not impacted by a recent cyberattack on its systems.

THERE were jitters in Jamaica’s financial sector on Friday as the operators of the MultiLink debit card and Automated Clearing House (ACH) networks confirmed that sections of its system had been the subject of a cyberattack.

In an early morning release Jamaica Electronic Transfer Services (JETS) said the cyberattack, which had been circulating as a rumour since Thursday, involved a limited part of its internal administrative systems, but the MultiLink and ACH networks were not affected and both remained fully operational.

“The JETS Cyber Monitoring Team detected suspicious activity within a limited portion of the company’s domain and immediately shut down the administrative system, isolated and launched a full forensic investigation in coordination with specialist cybersecurity consultants.

“While payment networks were not affected, there were reports with payment transactions accessed by the hackers that contain information that may have exposed the names of some customers who received transfers via ACH, as well as some card numbers from historical administrative data files on the debit network,” said JETS.

“It is important to note, however, that personal identification numbers (PINs), card verification values (CVV), and expiry dates are never stored and would not have been impacted,” added JETS as it sought to allay fears of people in the financial sector and members of the public.

According to JETS, both it and its member institutions have employed necessary and vital steps to protect the integrity of the payment systems and customer information.

“Customers of member institutions are, however, encouraged to observe standard digital-safety practices and contact their individual financial institutions should they receive unsolicited communication about their card or account,” said JETS.

By mid-afternoon Friday, the Bank of Jamaica (BOJ) also moved to quiet fears in the financial sector with a media release stating that it has been engaged with JETS, its member financial institutions, and the relevant national authorities since being informed of the incident.

According to the BOJ, with JETS confirming that the MultiLink and ACH networks were not affected and remain fully operational, customers can continue to use their debit cards and make ACH payments as usual.

“The bank’s first priority is the protection of Jamaican consumers and the integrity of our payments system. The bank is working closely with JETS, the member financial institutions, and our national partners to support the response to this incident and to protect customers.

“We support JETS’ decision to inform the public. Transparency and coordinated action are the right response, and the bank will provide further updates as appropriate,” said the BOJ.

It added that as a precaution, and consistent with the guidance issued by JETS, members of the public are encouraged to:

• review their accounts or credit card transactions via their respective online platforms regularly, also closely monitor bank alerts and report any unfamiliar transaction to their financial institution promptly;

• be cautious of unsolicited calls, text messages, e-mail or social media messages about their card or account, including any that claim to be from their bank, JETS or Bank of Jamaica, as these may be attempts at fraud;

• never share a PIN, CVV, one-time password, or online banking login with anyone. Legitimate institutions will not request these details.

• contact their financial institution directly, using the number on the back of their card or on the institution’s official website if they have any concerns.

“Bank of Jamaica, in its oversight of the national payments system, will continue to monitor developments closely and will take such action as is necessary to safeguard the safety and efficiency of the system. The payments system continues to operate normally,” the release added.

In the meantime, Opposition spokesman on science, technology, and digital transformation Christopher Brown expressed concern over the issue, which he said may have exposed personal and financial information belonging to customers.

While noting JETS’ assurance that the MultiLink and ACH payment networks were not compromised, Brown said the potential exposure of customer names and debit card information raises legitimate concerns about data protection, cybersecurity safeguards, and the security of Jamaica’s critical financial infrastructure.

He pointed out that this incident comes against the background of the Government’s own disclosure that Jamaica recorded more than 49 million attempted cyberattacks in 2025 and another 5.4 million in the first quarter of 2026.

“We have heard repeated announcements about a National Cybersecurity Strategy and the establishment of a Cybersecurity Council. While these initiatives are important, we remain deeply concerned that the comprehensive legislative framework necessary to strengthen cybersecurity standards, institutional accountability, and the protection of critical digital infrastructure remains absent,” said Brown.

He underscored that, despite the escalating threats, Jamaica has still not enacted the proposed Cybersecurity Act.

“Strategies, councils and policy announcements, however well-intentioned, cannot substitute for a robust and enforceable legislative framework. The Government must urgently accelerate the enactment of the Cybersecurity Act and provide a clear timetable for its passage,” added Brown.

He also called on JETS and the regulatory authorities to ensure a thorough investigation, establish the full extent of any exposure of personal and financial information, and provide timely notification and appropriate protection to affected customers.

World.title: Senate gives nod to Mediation Bill
World.content:
Clause 12 of the Bill allows for people to qualify to become licensed mediators.

THE Mediation Bill, 2026, which formalises the use of alternative dispute resolution in the criminal justice system, received bipartisan support during its passage in the Senate on Friday.

In piloting the Bill, Leader of Government Business in the Senate Kamina Johnson Smith noted that, while mediation takes place in Jamaica, “the framework within which it is offered has long needed streamlining and strengthening in order to harness its full potential”.

“This Bill seeks to establish a comprehensive framework governing the conduct of mediation in Jamaica. It provides for the registration of mediators, the licensing and regulation of mediation providers for continuing professional development, and the establishment of the necessary institutional machinery,” said Johnson Smith.

She described the new legislation as “another practical addition to our toolkit as we address our national challenge of managing conflicts, settling disputes and building peace in our homes, communities and workplaces”.

“Very importantly, it establishes the legal framework required for Jamaica to ratify the United Nations Convention on international settlement agreements resulting from mediation, commonly known as the Singapore Convention on Mediation,” added Johnson Smith, who is also the minister of foreign affairs and foreign trade.

Leader of Opposition Business Senator Donna Scott-Mottley welcomed the establishment of a public register of mediators in the Bill during her contribution to the debate. She observed that “citizens should be able to check whether someone is registered and whether a service provider is licensed. There needs to be a certainty about that,” she stated.

The Opposition lawmaker indicated her liking of clause 12 of the Bill which allows “other training” whereby people can qualify to become licensed mediators. She also expressed her liking for clause 29 which outlines a range of disciplinary responses, including warnings, corrective action, and further training.

“I like that, too, because not every breach should attract the same sanction,” she said.

Government Senator Christian Tavares-Finson described the Bill as “a significant piece of legislation with the potential to strengthen our justice system, promote peaceful conflict resolution, preserve relationships, and contribute to Jamaica’s social and economic development”.

“At its heart, this Bill is about more than regulating a profession. It is about how we choose to settle our differences. Must every disagreement become a battle? Must every conflict end in confrontation? Must justice always require a courtroom?” he said.

Arguing that justice must be accessible, timely, fair, and responsive to people’s needs, Tavares-Finson posited that mediation offers an important means of achieving these objectives. He said a comprehensive legal framework for mediation is therefore a welcome step towards modernising Jamaica’s justice system while building a society that values dialogue, accountability and peaceful settlement.

Tavares-Finson outlined that mediation increases access to justice, in particular for a person looking to recover a debt, a small business pursuing payment, a family resolving a property dispute, or neighbours involved in a boundary disagreement.

“The cost and duration of litigation can make justice difficult to obtain,” he said, adding that mediation also reduces the pressure on the courts, preserves families, relationships and communities, and supports economic development.

Tavares-Finson also pointed out that Jamaica’s economic progress depends partly on investor confidence, reliable contracts, and the ability of businesses to resolve disagreements efficiently.

Government Senator Kavan Gayle, a trade unionist, cited that the society faces disagreements arising from economic pressures, workplace conflicts, family disputes, community tensions, and competing interests.

“The Government’s promotion of mediation recognises the need for peaceful, timely and cost-effective alternatives to prolonged confrontation and litigation,” said Gayle.

“Mediation can reduce the burden on courts and public institutions, preserve relationships, improve productivity, and strengthen public confidence in dispute resolution,” he argued.

According to Gayle, “Mediation must complement, not replace justice, collective bargaining, established grievance procedures, and the protections of workers’ rights.

“The fundamental objective is to build a society where disagreements can be resolved fairly and constructively without unnecessarily damaging relationships or escalating into prolonged disputes,” he said.

The Bill was eventually passed with four amendments. It was passed in July in the House of Representatives where it was piloted by the Minister of Justice and Constitutional Affairs Delroy Chuck.

World.title: Empty Five Miles greets pastors one week after deadly firefight
World.content:
Bishop Rohan Edwards leads members of his team into the house which was the scene of a major firefight between gunmen and the security forces one week ago. (Photos: Jason Cross)

A ghost town would be an appropriate description of Five Miles, in Mount Morland, Sligoville, St Catherine on Thursday, almost one week after two members of the Jamaica Constabulary Force (JCF) and three alleged gunmen were killed during a firefight.

With no residents in sight, a mission by pastors of the 10,000 Men and Families Movement and the Spanish Town Minister’s Fraternal fell flat as their hops of meeting and praying with people who were affected emotionally by the traumatic event at a house in the community fizzled.

That did not stop Bishop Rowan Edwards, founder of the 10,000 Men and Families Movement, and Pastor Dalbert Simmonds, chairman of the Spanish Town Ministers’ Fraternal from offering up prayers.

They said this was in the hope of blessing the space so that nothing similar to what unfolded last week happens again at the location or in the community.

They also prayed for God to cover and protect the police as they go about serving, protecting, and reassuring Jamaicans.

“I’m so sorry to know that this is happening in my country, at this juncture, when crime and violence has taken a nosedive.

It is frightening to know that this incident happened in this peaceful community. I’m very saddened to know that these two policemen were killed,” said Edwards.

“I do extend our condolence to the family members of these two policemen but I need some questions to be answered. Couldn’t the tactical team from the JCF organise a better approach? What I have noticed overseas, when there’s gunmen at one location, the approach is different,” Edwards said as he expressed hope that this incident will cause the JCF to bring more tactical training to its members who have to face hardened criminals.

Edwards was disappointed that no one could be located in the area to directly receive spiritual counselling when his team visited on Thursday.

“You see, because the area is so deserted, we can’t find who the family members are so we could counsel them. So, that’s our next move, to find the family members,” added Edwards.

In the meantime, Simmonds of the Spanish Town Ministers’ Fraternal said he was looking forward to praying for members of the family of the people involved in the incident and he was also disappointed that there were none in sight.

“Today, we are here, right on spot where this gruesome incident took place. The intent, really, was to bring some sort of comfort and prayer and counselling to persons affected in the area. But as Bishop Edwards said, the area is deserted at the moment, so we are not able to carry out that function as we want to,” said Simmonds.

“I want to take this opportunity, as the chairman of the Spanish Town Ministers’ Fraternal, to say to my brothers and sisters in this space, and the wider Jamaica, don’t allow the criminal elements to access or occupy your space.
