World.title: What’s Going on With the Potential Šibenik Airport?
World.content:
October the 24th, 2026 – The idea of a future Šibenik Airport sounds feasible and very reasonable, but it seems like there’s been more than a few spanners thrown in the works…

The feasibility study and the revision of the conceptual design were supposed to be completed by the end of July this year, but almost three months later there is no public confirmation that the documents have been finished. As SibenikIN reports, in the meantime, the issue of the planned airport’s impact on the habitats of protected bird species has also been raised.

At a joint thematic session of the parliamentary committees for tourism and for maritime affairs, transport and infrastructure, held on Thursday the 22nd of October, the operations of Croatian airports, investments, their financial sustainability and future development were discussed. Representatives of the competent ministries, airports and the aviation sector took part in the discussion, and among the topics were the seasonality of traffic, the development of regional airports and the need for better transport connections.

However, the official parliamentary report fails to mention the Heart of Dalmatia airport project at Pokrovnik, in which Croatia holds a majority ownership stake. Although this does not rule out the possibility that the project was mentioned in passing during the session, it was not singled out among the development topics in the official summary.

the documentation should have been completed by july

Back in June this year, local portal ŠibenikIN reported on the status of the planned airport project at Pokrovnik. At that time, Šibenik Deputy Mayor Danijel Mileta, referring to a report by the company Zračna luka Srce Dalmacije that had been submitted to the City as one of the co-owners, confirmed that the feasibility study and the revision of the conceptual design with technical details were in preparation. According to the announcements at the time, both documents were supposed to be completed by the end of July 2026.

However, almost three months after the announced deadline expired, no publicly published confirmation has been found that the documents have been finished and handed over to the client. Such information is also not available on the company’s official website. At the same time, on 30 December 2025 the preparation of the environmental impact study and the main acceptability assessment of the intervention for the ecological network was contracted, with an 18-month deadline, i.e. approximately until mid-2027. According to the information obtained from the month of June, a geodetic elaborate, a climatological study and a project for a meteorological station had already been prepared, while the procedure for obtaining special conditions for the station itself was still ongoing.

protected bird habitats could become a serious problem…

In addition to the questions of deadlines and documentation, an additional obstacle has appeared that could affect the future of the project. As ŠibenikIN wrote in July, in the process of amending the Spatial Plan of Šibenik-Knin County the question of the planned airport’s impact on the habitats of protected bird species was raised.

Particularly highlighted were the calandra lark, the short-toed lark and the stone-curlew, whose habitats could be threatened by the construction and use of the airport. In the spatial-planning documentation it was warned that, due to nature-protection requirements, it might be necessary to re-examine the location or the category of the planned airport. Such a warning doesn’t mean that the ambitious Šibenik Airport project has been rejected or that construction at Pokrovnik has been banned. However, it opens the question of whether the existing conceptual design will be acceptable from the point of view of nature protection and whether additional changes will be required. It isn’t yet known whether these warnings have affected the preparation of the documentation that was supposed to be finished in July.

the state is the project’s majority owner

The Heart of Dalmatia airport project is being developed by the company of the same name, in which the Republic of Croatia holds a 55 percent ownership stake, while the remaining 45 percent belongs to Šibenik-Knin County and five cities. Josip Skelin was appointed director of the company back in May 2025.

Interestingly, State Secretary of the Ministry of Maritime Affairs, Transport and Infrastructure Tomislav Mihotić, who earlier participated on behalf of the state in the establishment of the company for the development of the Šibenik Airport, also took part in today’s parliamentary session on the future of Croatian airports. The Pokrovnik project has for years been presented as a possible contribution to transport connectivity and tourist development of this part of Dalmatia, but before any possible realisation a series of professional, spatial, environmental and financial questions still need to be resolved.

After the expiry of the July deadline for the key documentation, questions now remain open as to whether the feasibility study and the revision of the conceptual design have been completed, how much money has so far been spent on the project, what its current status is in the state transport plans, and whether nature-protection requirements will lead to a change in the planned location or category of the airport.

World.title: After Decades of Decay, Rijeka Torpedo Launch Station Will Rise Again
World.content:
October the 24th, 2026 – Following years of decay, the famous Rijeka torpedo launch station will be given back its full glory and turned into a tourist site.

Rijeka has an exceptionally rich industrial history, and one of its most important monuments is located on the western part of the city waterfront, in the former Torpedo factory complex. As Ivana Vasarevic writes for Putni Kofer, right next to the sea, stands an unusual reinforced-concrete structure – the historic torpedo launch station. This is the exact place where weapons intended for navies around the world were once tested. After very many years of deterioration, this building, protected as a cultural asset of Croatia, will finally receive the restoration it deserves. The current plans also include transforming the entire surrounding area into a new tourist attraction.

turning the clock back to the 1860s…

Commons/Muzej Rijeka

Sea salt, waves and weather over the decades seriously damaged the ramp, so the conservation department as early as 2019 ordered urgent protection measures. Fortunately, it was decided that the launch station would not be demolished and replaced by a replica, but that the original structure would be preserved. Works should begin in the last quarter of 2026 and be completed during 2027.

The answer as to precisely why this structure is so historically significant takes us 160 years into the past, when an invention that changed naval warfare was born in Rijeka. During the early 1860s, Rijeka native Giovanni Luppis was developing the idea of a defensive weapon with which enemy ships could be stopped before they approached land. He called it the “coast saver”, but he lacked the technical knowledge and funds for its realisation.

rijeka torpedos were sought after around the world

He presented the idea to Robert Whitehead, a British engineer and the former manager of the Rijeka Technical Institute. He then developed a torpedo resembling a metal fish that moved independently under the surface of the sea. The first usable torpedo was successfully tested in Rijeka in 1866, and nine years later the Institute became the R. Whitehead & Co. factory, the first torpedo factory in the world.

Rijeka torpedoes soon became sought after around the world. They were ordered by Great Britain, France, Italy, Germany, Sweden, Japan, Russia and many other countries. The factory expanded its business, opened plants abroad, and production in Rijeka continued until 1966. Of course, before delivery to customers the torpedoes had to undergo a series of demanding tests. That is precisely what the launch stations were used for, from which trial launches were carried out and the behaviour of the torpedoes in the sea was monitored.

The first launch ramps were wooden structures from the 19th century, and over time they were replaced by a more solid reinforced-concrete station. According to data from the Museum of the City of Rijeka, it was built in 1930, and four years later a section intended for testing torpedoes launched from aircraft was added. Thus the station served for simulating the launch of torpedoes from ships as well as from the air: Rijeka, after all, did not yet have its own airport at that time.

Although production ceased long ago, the ramp still reminds us of the time when Rijeka was an international centre of technological innovation. Its importance goes beyond local frameworks because it testifies to the development of an invention that changed world naval history. In addition to the restoration of the launch station, plans also include the arrangement of the Torpedo Visitor Centre. As the portal Fiuman recently reported, it would exhibit full-size torpedoes, their parts and technical elements, while a special virtual room would bring the history of this Rijeka invention closer through multimedia content.

transforming history into a tourist site

As for the architectural solution, it is conceived as a combination of industrial heritage and contemporary design. The façades of the centre should be adorned with archival photographs and technical drawings of torpedoes, while steel elements would in shape recall the plating of a submarine. Along the waterfront a promenade with a beautiful view of Kvarner and the launch station is planned, a viewpoint reached by stone steps, as well as a small square and the surrounding public areas.

World.title: Capped Prices Introduced for Pula Advent This Year
World.content:
October the 24th, 2026 – Good news for lovers of festive cheer as capped prices will be introduced for certain food and drink items sold at Pula Advent this year.

The City of Pula has decided to limit the prices of the most popular products at Advent stalls in order to make them more affordable. A city decision has set maximum amounts for part of the hospitality offer during the upcoming Advent. Index reports that rather unsurprisingly, this decision has been welcomed by all.

a new (capped) price list for pula advent

Under the new rules, the price of a hot dog, hamburger and bakalar (dried cod) will be limited to five euros. Mulled wine, hot chocolate and cocoa may cost a maximum of three euros, while the maximum price for tea and water will be two euros. The sweet offer, which includes fritule (fritters), pancakes and Christmas cookies, is also limited to three euros per portion. Deputy Mayor of Pula Siniša Gordić explained how the system will work. “It is about one product that caterers must have on offer, as stated in the public call. For the entire rest of the offer, if they want to have something additional, they can set the prices themselves if there is interest,” Gordić said. He added that a minimum quantity or portion has also been defined for the products with limited prices.

Danijel Britvić, who has been taking part in Pula Advent for years, considers the idea good, but warns that the quality of ingredients affects the final price. “Hot dogs are 80-gram items, an ordinary frankfurter that I already had for five euros in a large bun. We have a 100-gram sausage and it cannot cost five euros, but six or seven. I will have the same prices as last year, but I will also include a hot dog at the set price in the offer,” Britvić said.

What is new in Pula has already been a proven model in Poreč. There, part of the offer has been sold at limited prices for years, which has proven to be a successful practice. “We’ve adjusted those prices over the years according to market conditions, but always so that they remain within a framework that allows each of us to go out with friends to Advent, treat everyone to a drink and eat something, without it being too great a financial burden and so that they come back again,” said Ajna Temimović from the City of Poreč.

The first test of the new decision by the Pula city administration will be visible soon, as the public call for the lease of Advent stalls ends at the end of October.

World.title: Anušić: Ukraine is Showing the Bravery Croatia Did in the 1990s
World.content:
October the 24th, 2026 – Speaking in Vukovar, Defence Minister Ivan Anušić has stated that Ukraine is currently going showing the bravery Croatia did back during the 1990s.

Defence Minister Ivan Anušić spoke in Vukovar about how Croatia must continue to help Ukraine because its defeat or the imposition of an unjust peace could lead to a new war on the borders of the European Union.

“Such heroism, sacrifice and respect for one’s homeland is what we also saw in our Homeland War back in 1991. That is why we must continue to help the Ukrainian people who, unfortunately, are going through the same wartime fate we experienced in the 1990s. Because if Ukraine loses this war or if it’s forced into an unjust peace, we’ll once again have war on our own borders,” Anušić said, according to a statement from the Ministry of Defence (MORH). Index reports that the minister made the remarks at the premiere of the documentary film “Glory to the Heroes”, which tells the story of two Ukrainians of different political convictions who fought and died for the independence of their country.

After the premiere, Anušić took part in a panel discussion on the Homeland War and the war in Ukraine. Alongside him were Croatian defenders Fanika Janko and Ivan Lukić Zolja, as well as the documentary’s director Alceo Marti. The conversation was moderated by Goran Rotim.

Anušić stressed that Croatia, because of its own wartime experience, particularly understands what the Ukrainian people are going through today. “There are a great many parallels between our Homeland War and the war in Ukraine. The Croatian people, who themselves lived through the sufferings of war, have a special understanding for the Ukrainian people. Just as Vukovar in 1991 put up heroic resistance against a superior Greater Serbian aggressor and became a symbol of Croatian freedom, so Ukraine today is heroically fighting against Russian aggression and keeping the war away from the borders of the European Union,” Anušić said.

He added that Vukovar, because of its defence in 1991 and the suffering it endured during the Homeland War, is a particularly appropriate place for the premiere of a film about Ukrainian defenders. Speaking about the two Ukrainians whose destinies are shown in the documentary, Anušić emphasised that, despite their different political views, they defended their country together.

“One of your interlocutors in the film says that war brings out the worst in people, but it also brings out the best. Two young men who were politically on different sides, when the freedom of Ukraine was at stake, then had only one side – their common struggle for Ukraine,” the minister concluded. He added that similar stories of courage, sacrifice and unity can also be found among Croatian defenders from the Homeland War.

World.title: Iraqi PM adviser accuses Iran of severe border violations and smuggling
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – A senior adviser to Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi has openly accused Iran of orchestrating deliberate security breaches, widespread drug smuggling, and illicit financial flows across the border, marking a rare and pointed public rebuke from within Baghdad’s executive circle as Iraq shuttered key commercial crossing points.

Speaking to domestic media, prime ministerial adviser Abdelamir Taiban stated that Tehran has actively undermined Iraqi internal stability by allowing unauthorized, affiliated networks to bypass border protocols, inciting borderland disorder.

Taiban noted that Iraqi nationals have faced abductions after entering Iranian territory, identifying the areas surrounding the Shalamcheh terminal in Basra and the Al-Sheeb terminal in Maysan as high-risk corridors. He urged the federal government to aggressively scale electronic monitoring and comprehensive automation across every operational terminal along the shared 1,599-kilometer frontier.

The adviser characterized the inbound traffic of narcotics and counterfeit currency as the most damaging economic threat facing the nation, asserting that the resulting market sabotage has inflicted financial disruption outpacing the economic fallout previously caused by ISIS.

The remarks follow the indefinite closure of the Al-Sheeb port of entry in Maysan governorate to both travelers and commercial cargo—a measure following the precautionary shutdown of Shalamcheh in September amid regional drone incidents—which prompted demonstrations by local transport operators and cross-border truckers concerned over disrupted trade in fresh produce and construction materials.

In response, Prime Minister Al-Zaidi convened the Ministerial Council for National Security, ordering security units to safeguard peaceful assemblies while maintaining stringent checks to intercept illicit trafficking channels.

World.title: US dollar dips to 168,500 IQD following Zaidi’s remarks on cash inflows
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate of the U.S. dollar against the Iraqi dinar retreated by approximately 1,000 dinars per $100 across parallel market trading desks on Saturday, October 24, 2026.

The softening followed public statements delivered on Friday by Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi, in which he disclosed that Washington will dispatch $1 billion in physical cash shipments to Iraq and assured the public that parallel rates will soon decline toward 155,000 dinars per $100.

The remarks stemmed upward momentum that had pushed dollar transactions across domestic exchange bureaus to 169,500 dinars on Thursday and Friday, driving the prevailing market benchmark down to 168,500 dinars.

Across major trading hubs in Baghdad, Erbil, and Basra, foreign exchange desks and licensed counters posted identical rates on Saturday morning, listing cash selling quotes at 169,000 dinars against buying bids of 168,500 dinars per $100.

Despite the temporary retreat, parallel figures continue to maintain a notable spread over the Central Bank of Iraq’s official statutory cash peg, which remains set at 152,000 dinars per $100.

The divergence highlights persistent liquidity dynamics and demand pressures outside central electronic settlement channels, even as executive assurances of incoming dollar consignments aim to stabilize market sentiment and curb speculative price premiums.

World.title: US State Department reissues Level 4 ‘Do Not Travel’ advisory for Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The U.S. Department of State issued a renewed travel advisory on Saturday, October 24, 2026, maintaining its highest “Level 4: Do Not Travel” warning for Iraq and urging American citizens to avoid travel to the country under any circumstances.

According to the advisory, Washington cited the inability of Iraqi authorities to guarantee the safety of foreign nationals in the event of sudden armed conflict or localized violence, while emphasizing the U.S. government’s severely constrained capacity to execute emergency evacuations or consular relief operations inside Iraqi territory.

The State Department warned of acute security and public health vulnerabilities, citing risks from terrorism, kidnappings, civil unrest, and frequent asymmetric strikes. It specified recurring hazards from improvised explosive devices (IEDs), unmanned aerial systems, and indirect rocket fire conducted by Iran-aligned armed groups and remnants of ISIS against U.S. personnel, diplomatic compounds, commercial companies, energy installations, and commercial airports.

The advisory also drew attention to regional escalation vectors—including cross-border hostilities conducted by the Houthi movement—as well as widespread unmarked minefields and UXO hazards, aviation restrictions implemented under Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) notices, and severe structural shortages across Iraq’s trauma and emergency medical infrastructure.

In response to sustained security threats, strict operating restrictions remain enforced on U.S. diplomatic personnel, requiring special authorization for in-country travel and residency within heavily fortified protocols.

For private American citizens currently residing in Iraq, the State Department urged immediate contingency planning independent of U.S. governmental assistance, including enrolling in the Smart Traveler Enrollment Program (STEP), drafting emergency wills and power-of-attorney designations, leaving DNA reference samples with family medical providers, securing private medical and emergency evacuation insurance, and developing comprehensive personal departure protocols.

World.title: Iraqi FM Fuad Hussein condemns deadly church attack in Jordan’s Karak
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein held a telephone conversation on Friday, October 23, 2026, with Jordan’s Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs and Expatriates, Ayman Safadi, strongly condemning the deadly armed attack that targeted mourners at a church in Jordan’s southern Karak Governorate.

During the call, Hussein conveyed Iraq’s full solidarity with the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan in confronting terrorism and violent extremism.

The Iraqi foreign minister extended the government and people of Iraq’s heartfelt condolences to the leadership, government, and citizens of Jordan, as well as to the families of the victims, while wishing a swift recovery to those injured.

The diplomatic outreach followed a shooting incident earlier on Friday, in which unidentified gunmen opened fire during a funeral service at a Greek Orthodox church in the village of Hmoud, located in Karak Governorate approximately 180 kilometers south of Amman.

The attack left at least seven people dead and dozens wounded, prompting heightened security deployments and an active manhunt by Jordanian security agencies.

World.title: Ukraine says two soldiers died after arrested girl sent Russian poison
World.content:
Kyiv – Ukrainian police said Friday they had detained a 17-year-old girl suspected of helping Russia’s security services to poison Ukrainian soldiers and that two had died.

Ukraine and Russia have throughout their war since 2022 accused each other of recruiting minors for sabotage acts including poisoning.

The girl, who was not named, is suspected of having packaged deadly drugs and sending them to Ukrainian soldiers she contacted by Telegram, said a police statement.

She was arrested by police in Zhytomyr, west of Kyiv, after allegedly following instructions from a Russian handler in exchange for at least 5,000 hryvnias ($111), they said.

After receiving packages with “free drugs”, the soldiers were “instructed to take them on camera”, the statement said.

“The recipients did not know that the capsules contained a lethal dose of methadone,” it said, adding that “two soldiers died from poisoning in the Zhytomyr region.”

Police said they had identified other recipients of the packages, which “prevented four more murders” across the country.

“The young woman was notified that she is suspected of aiding and abetting the premeditated murder of two people as part of a prior conspiracy,” the police statement said.

She was also suspected of “shipping drugs and psychotropic substances for the purpose of distribution”, it said, adding that she faced up to 15 years in jail if found guilty.

Police cautioned that Russia aims “to kill our people and destabilise the situation within the country”.

“Do not accept medication or other substances, as well as food or drinks of dubious origin, from people you do not know well,” police cautioned.

Since the start of Russia’s full-scale invasion in February 2022, Ukrainian authorities say they have opened thousands of investigations into collaboration with the enemy, and frequently arrest individuals accused of working for Moscow.

In 2023, Ukraine accused Russia of poisoning the wife of Kyrylo Budanov, who was then head of Ukraine’s military intelligence and is now a presidential advisor.

World.title: Volvo Cars shares plunge on losses, job cuts
World.content:
Stockholm – Shares in Swedish carmaker Volvo Cars plunged Friday after it said US tariffs and strong competition from local brands in China pushed it into a third-quarter loss.

The company also said it would cut about 2,500 jobs worldwide.

Volvo Cars, controlled by Chinese group Geely, reported revenue of 66.9 billion kronor ($6.7 billion) for the third quarter, down nearly 23 percent from the same period last year.

It swung to a net loss of 5.7 billion kronor for the quarter from a net profit of 4.5 billion kronor a year earlier.

Shortly after 0800 GMT, Volvo Cars shares were down almost 30 percent.

“We continue to operate in a very tough environment with strong external challenges: de-globalisation, hypercompetition and climate change,” chief executive Hakan Samuelsson said in a statement.

In response, the company announced a new five-billion-kronor savings plan it said would lead to about 2,000 job cuts in Sweden and 500 more globally, “through natural attrition and by targeted exit packages to employees”.

The company, which had bet heavily on electric vehicles, said the removal of consumer incentives for EVs in the United States under President Donald Trump had also hit its margins.

In 2024, Volvo Cars dropped a plan to transition to exclusively EV sales by the end of the decade.

“We are convinced that we have the right long-term strategy addressing these challenges,” Samuelsson said.

“However, in the short term, with severely challenged volumes, we need to reinforce our turnaround plan with additional decisive actions, lowering our break-even point and improving cash flows to make us more resilient.”

Struggling along with other European auto companies in the face of a difficult global landscape, Volvo Cars last year announced an 18-billion-kronor cost-cutting plan.

The company said in September that Samuelsson would resign when his contract ends, with Skoda Auto CEO Klaus Zellmer set to replace him “no later” than October next year.

World.title: France braces for new protests as Macron seeks to restore order
World.content:
Paris – France was on Friday bracing for a weekend of new protests after some of the worst urban violence in years erupted on the sidelines of demonstrations a week ago, as President Emmanuel Macron sought to reclaim the initiative and restore order.

Macron, who on Thursday announced that only union demonstrations would be authorised this weekend, was to hold a meeting of his defence council of top ministers and officials and also meet security forces.

He was also set to host for the first time representatives of high school pupils, whose protests over conditions at their schools sparked a movement that has broadened nationwide into a show of anger against the government at the rising cost of living.

The protests have come at a critical moment for France six months ahead of elections to replace Macron, with a new poll underlining far-right candidate Marine Le Pen is the frontrunner and showing her position has been strengthened by the latest events.

Adding to tensions, Le Pen is at the weekend due to host her National Rally (RN) party congress in Orleans, with thousands of supporters expected but local authorities fearing clashes as opponents head to the city.

Macron is due to announce “additional decisions” after hosting the meeting of his defence council, on top of the limited curfews already announced, his office said.

At the meeting with students, “we will present our demands to him — which remain the same: the state of school infrastructure and an overhaul of the Parcoursup (university admissions) system,” Nathanael Combary, president of Renouveau Lyceen (High School Renewal) told AFP.

Pierre Sourzat, who heads the organisation Les Lyceens (The High School Students), was sceptical: “He’ll listen to us, pretend he’s understood us, and then nothing will come of it.”

Macron’s government has sought to draw a line between the legitimate demands of protesters and the looting, burning and ransacking that erupted on the sidelines of protests last Saturday.

In a judicial response of unprecedented firmness, courts have already sent 217 people, half of them first-time offenders, to prison over the events on Saturday, Justice Minister Gerald Darmanin said.

On Thursday, Macron called for “the utmost severity” against “acts of delinquency”, accusing “ultra-left” groups of having sought to “bring down the republic” last weekend.

– ‘Police have a responsibility’ –

Demonstrations in Marseille in the south and Lyon in the southeast have been banned at the weekend, while in Paris protesters will only be allowed to march a limited route between Bastille and Nation squares.

Marseille authorities however reversed a decision to halt all public transport in the city on Saturday. But in the capital, leading museums including the Louvre will be closed on Saturday while the Art Basel art fair is being cut short.

Some 20 percent more members of the security forces will be deployed this weekend after heavy criticism of the anticipation and intelligence gathering of police last week.

“In a country governed by the rule of law, the police have a responsibility both to ensure that protests can take place peacefully and safely and to protect the public from violent disorder,” said Eva Cosse, senior Europe researcher at Human Rights Watch, expressing alarm over reports of children being severely injured by crowd-control weapons.

The violence has tarnished the image of France ahead of elections that could be a turning point in its modern history, with the government’s debt pile also troubling investors.

A new poll by Harris Interactive for M6/RTL made after the violence showed Le Pen soaring ahead on 33-35 percent in the first round of voting for the presidential elections.

It predicted that hard-left leader Jean-Luc Melenchon was on course to face her in the run-off where Le Pen would emerge as an easy winner on some 70 percent of the vote.

World.title: Kering shares tumble as Gucci fails to reassure investors
World.content:
Paris – Kering shares were down more than 10 percent in Paris Friday after the French luxury group published results that failed to reassure investors about a turnaround at its key Gucci brand.

At 0730 GMT, Kering shares were down 10.8 percent at 190.40 euros, their lowest since June 2025. The market’s CAC40 index was down 0.3 percent.

Kering reported late Thursday that third-quarter sales were flat at 3.34 billion euros ($3.75 billion).

Sales at Gucci, by far the group’s largest single brand, fell by four percent to 1.29 billion euros, worse than the three-percent decline registered in the second quarter.

“Gucci has not shown convincing signs of stabilisation,” Deutsche Bank analysts said in a note.

Italy-based Gucci is key to Kering’s fortunes, but has been in freefall since 2023 as the brand lost its luxury cachet.

World.title: Rs 10 lakh cover for 45 paise: Counter rail ticket buyers get insurance option
World.content:
At present, the optional travel insurance facility is available only for reserved tickets bought online.

NEW DELHI: From Tuesday (Oct 27), all railway passengers buying reserved tickets from reservation counters can opt for travel insurance. At present, optional travel insurance facility is available only for reserved tickets bought online.The insurance premium is only 45 paise per passenger, including taxes, with coverage of Rs 10 lakh in case of death and permanent total disability in a train accident.The scheme has provision for payment of Rs 7.5 lakh for permanent partial disability and up to Rs 2 lakh for hospitalisation expenses arising from injuries, as well as Rs 10,000 towards transportation of mortal remains of deceased passengers. The Railway Board has directed all its zones to implement the facility.It said, âWhere a passenger opts for insurance, the applicable premium shall be collected along with the ticket fare through digital means only. Staff shall ensure that where the person is opting for insurance, payment is done through digital means.âReservation staff will inform passengers about the availability of the optional insurance facility and facilitate the exercise of their choice.The board said reservation staff will ensure that the mobile number (mandatory) along with other requisite passenger particulars are captured accurately so as to facilitate transmission of relevant details to the insurance firm for issuance of the policy.Passengers opting for insurance shall be informed that the policy details will be communicated to their registered mobile number.It covers specified railway accidents and untoward incidents, including train collisions, derailments, violent attacks, robbery, arson and accidental falls from trains. Coverage extends to diverted routes and alternative transport arranged by the railways in certain cases of train diversion or short termination.Normal second class or general class passengers are not covered under the insurance policy. It is also not applicable to children below the age of 5 years for whom tickets are issued without a berth or seat. But it is applicable to children in 5-11 age group who have reservation with berth or without berth.

World.title: CBI files FIR against IL&FS Energy, top execs in Rs 212cr Canara Bank loan fraud case
World.content:
CBI has named M/s IL&FS Energy Development Company Ltd, its MD and directors.

NEW DELHI: CBI has registered an FIR against a Mumbaibased firm and its top executives for allegedly cheating Canara Bank of Rs 212 crore, officials said on Saturday. Searches were conducted in Delhi, Mumbai and Noida, and incriminating documents seized.CBI has named M/s IL&FS Energy Development Company Ltd, its MD and directors â Sunil Wadhwa, Anoop Seth, Hari Sankaran, Ramesh Chandra Bawa and Arun Kumar Saha â and unknown public servants and private individuals as accused. The case was registered on Oct 21 following a complaint by Canara Bankâs circle office in Bandra.According to CBI, the accused allegedly entered into a conspiracy to secure a term loan of Rs 100 crore from erstwhile Syndicate Bank, now merged with Canara Bank, at its Large Corporate Branch in Mumbai, along with a foreign currency loan of $50 million from its London branch.The company allegedly diverted and siphoned the funds through associate entities instead of using them for sanctioned purposes, causing an estimated wrongful loss of Rs 212.3 crore. The FIR invokes charges of conspiracy, cheating.

World.title: No EC nod needed for voter to sue candidate over false information: Supreme Court
World.content:
NEW DELHI: A voter can now not only cast a vote in an election but can also drag an election candidate to court and initiate criminal proceedings for lying and furnishing a false declaration as Supreme Court has ruled that a complaint filed by a private person alleging an offence under Section 125-A of Representation of People Act (filing false affidavit) is maintainable and the Election Commissionâs nod was not needed.

Explaining the interplay between Section 125-A of Representation of People Act and Section 195(1) of the CrPC which says that no court shall take cognisance of any offences punishable under sections 172 to 188, including the offence of furnishing false information to a public servant, the top court held that Section 125A of RoP Act does not come within the ambit of Section 195 of CrPC and a court can take cognisance of a private complaint.

The courtâs ruling will further empower the electorate against candidates who lied in their affidavits.

A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu quashed the Karnataka HC order which had held that âright given to the voter is only to file an election petition, and not to register a private complaint of crime which is the duty of the Election Commission, if it wants to do soâ.

SC said that Section 125-A was inserted in the RoP Act in 2002, while Section 195 of CrPC was amended in 2006, and that the omission of the legislature to include Section 125-A of the RoP Act in Section 195 of CrPC was deliberate and no court would be barred from taking cognisance of an alleged offence under Section 125-A of the RoP Act, even on the complaint lodged by a private person.





âShould we read into Section 195 of CrPC a prohibition in respect of Section 125-A of the RoP Act also, apart from those expressly included? If indeed it were the intention of the legislature that cognisance of any offence relating to furnishing of false information by a candidate in an affidavit with intent of being elected in an election (referred to in Section 125-A of the RoP Act) could only be taken if the complainant were a public servant, the same could have been provided by an amendment of Section 195, CrPC since Section 125-A of the RoP Act is of fairly recent origin.

â

SC also refused to give credence to the ECâs press note that it can take cognisance of such complaints and refer such matters to the relevant investigating authorities on a case-to-case basis. â...Even though the ECI is supreme in its own sphere and has, indeed, issued guidelines/press notes based on its understanding of the statutory provisions, interpretation of statutes is primarily the task of the courts and such guidelines/press notes do not bind us,â the court said.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

It said that Karnataka HC erred in holding that a private complaint cannot be filed for an offence under Section 125A of RoP Act which is punishable up to six months of jail term. The HC had interpreted the provision solely upon reading the letter issued by the Election Commission of India on the issue which was rejected by the apex court.

Allaying the apprehension that allowing the lodging of a criminal complaint by a private person would be misused and frivolous cases would be filed by political rivals, SC said, âIf at all a complaint is lodged to harass an elected candidate or frivolous allegations are levelled therein, the laws of the country duly empower the competent magistrates to pass such order(s) as they deem fit and proper commensurate with the facts and circumstances of each case.

â

World.title: Farooq Abdullah's comments on Pakistan and Kashmir draw flak
World.content:
SRINAGAR: National Conference (NC) president Farooq Abdullah on Saturday declared that Pakistan had âsavedâ Kashmiris by keeping the issue alive at international forums, while being careful to say that âotherwise their (Pakistanâs) intentions are not goodâ.

His statement drew flak from BJP, which slammed it as âseditious and anti-nationalâ.

âIf you do not remain (committed to NC), you will be erased. Even our identity will disappear. Nothing will be left. They are silent today because there is noise in the world and our neighbour is constantly behind it. Everywhere they say âthe decision regarding Kashmir has not been madeâ. That is what is saving usâ¦,â Farooq told a meeting of NC workers in Baramulla.

The words âtheyâ and âtheirâ were seen as an allusion to the Centre.

Farooqâs son, J&K chief minister Omar Abdullah, had not reacted to his fatherâs remarks till late Saturday.

Farooq urged NC workers and legislators to remain loyal to the party, whether in power or not, as he touched on a range of issues in his speech. âHold on to the truth. Speaking the truth is not easy, but unless you remain truthful and stand up for what is right, your future will never be secure,â the veteran said.





Citing the 1947 tribal invasion, Farooq condemned the âatrocitiesâ inflicted on Kashmiris by the raiders from Pakistanâ. He paid tributes to Maqbool Sherwani, an NC worker who died staving off the intruders, saying his âsacrifice helped stop the raiders in Baramulla and save Kashmirâ.

Farooq also mentioned the Chittisinghpura massacre in which 36 Sikhs were killed in south Kashmir on March 20, 2000, during then US President Bill Clintonâs visit to India.

He said a subsequent judicial inquiry had found that five men accused of carrying out the killings were not the perpetrators but shopkeepers âwho had been picked up by police and killedâ. According to Farooq, the inquiry judge should have investigated the massacre itself but was âtold from Delhiâ not to.

World.title: Daughter’s inheritance rights can’t be defeated by limitation: J&K and Ladakh high court
World.content:
The dispute dates back to Sept 14, 1982

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

JAMMU: The high court of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh has restored a womanâs right to inherit her fatherâs property after a 44-year-long legal battle, holding that an adverse revenue entry recorded during when she was a minor cannot automatically defeat a legitimate inheritance claim on limitation grounds.The dispute dates back to Sept 14, 1982, when Themu, daughter of late Sonu, filed a civil suit claiming half share in land measuring 58 kanals and 11 marlas left behind by her father.She challenged mutation no. 43 dated Oct 15, 1966, which had been entered exclusively in favour of one Shib Devi and sought declaration of her inheritance rights along with consequential possession.On March 9, 2004, the sub-judge court in Kishtwar passed a decree recognising her entitlement. However, the district judge reversed the decree on Nov 7, 2012, primarily on the grounds of limitation and failure to establish paternity.Justice Shahzad Azeem of the HC, while allowing the appeal filed by Themu, set aside the judgment of the district judge, Kishtwar, observing that limitation cannot be determined on presumptions and conjectures, particularly where the claimant was a minor when her rights were initially disputed and the defendants failed to establish when the cause of action actually arose.

World.title: Indonesia cuts pipeline gas exports to Singapore by about 9%
World.content:
Indonesia cut 31 million standard cubic feet ​of gas per day (mmscfd) from its pipeline natural gas exports ‌to Singapore starting on Saturday (October 24, 2026) to divert supply ​to the domestic power sector, upstream ⁠oil and gas regulator SKK Migas said.

Indonesia cut 15 mmscfd from its supply to Singapore from Natuna and another ‌16 mmscfd of gas from Sumatra, SKK Migas chairman Djoko Siswanto told Reuters on ‌Saturday (October 24, 2026).

Singapore’s Energy Market Authority said the ‌total reduction ⁠amounts to 17 bbtud over a ⁠period of 18 days, which is “less than 2% of our total daily gas demand of more than 1,000 bbtud”.

“EMA understands that ​our importers will ‌pursue all relevant recourse in their contracts for the gas supply disruption,” the Energy Market Authority spokesperson said. Singapore’s Energy Market Authority said state gas ‌buyer GasCo is ready to import more LNG ​at any time and that the country has sufficient energy supplies for national demand

⁠Most of Indonesia’s gas exports to Singapore are delivered via pipeline, and the cuts would account for ‌around 9% of that supply. “In order to safeguard the reliability of domestic gassupplies for electricity generation, effective today, gas supplies previously destined for Singapore are being redirected for domestic use,” said Djoko

The gas is being redirected to meet electricity needs in Batam, ‌Bintan and Sumatra, he said. Batam and several cities ​in Indonesia’s Riau Islands province suffered a blackout that lasted 16 hours earlier this month.

Indonesia ⁠energy minister Bahlil Lahadalia earlier this week said he ⁠would prioritise natural resources use for domestic needs, and review contracts to maintain energy security. ‌Singapore generates up to 95% of its electricity from natural gas

World.title: Trump casts his midterm ballot early in Florida
World.content:
President Donald Trump cast his ballot in the midterm elections Saturday (October 24, 2026), saying he voted for all Republicans in Florida before speaking at a Georgia rally.

Mr. Trump and First Lady Melania Trump arrived at their West Palm Beach polling location at the Palm Beach County Supervisor of Elections office together after the President spent the morning at his nearby golf course. Mr. Trump has been criticised in the past for voting by mail despite his long history of railing against that method of submitting ballots.

Asked if he voted the party line, Mr. Trump, who was wearing an “I Voted” sticker, said, “Very much so.”

Speaking to reporters at the poll site, Mr. Trump again defended an ad from Ohio Republican gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy. The ad has faced intense blowback for featuring the estranged mother of Democratic rival Dr. Amy Acton, who lost custody of her children after her husband, the children’s stepfather, was indicted for raping Acton when she was 12.

Mr. Trump also defended his decision to instruct his administration to file its lawsuit to block certification of the U.S. Senate race in Alaska if Republican Senator Dan Sullivan loses over the inclusion of a second candidate named Dan Sullivan on the ballot.

As for the war in Iran, he said, “I may have to finish it off. Or maybe they’ll make a deal, but I’m not sure. Either way, we win.”

Melania Trump, who this week brokered a ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine in the ravaged, Russian-occupied Ukrainian city of Oleshky so that humanitarian aid could be delivered and civilians evacuated, was asked whether she might travel to Ukraine.

“We will see,” she told reporters.

In Florida, Mr. Trump has endorsed Republican Representative Byron Donalds, who is running against David Jolly, a Republican-turned-independent-turned-Democrat, to succeed term-limited Gov. Ron DeSantis.

He has also campaigned for Republican Senator Ashley Moody, who is running to fill the last two years of Secretary of State Marco Rubio’s former Senate term against progressive state lawmaker Angie Nixon.

World.title: Houthis say attacked Saudi Arabia, Yemen’s Aden after deadly strikes
World.content:
Yemen’s Houthis launched fresh attacks on Saudi Arabia and the seat of Yemen’s internationally recognised government on Saturday (October 24, 2026) after blaming the kingdom for strikes that the Iran-backed group said killed 17 people.

Saudi Arabia and the government it backs in Yemen have come under sustained attack in recent weeks from the Houthis as a years-long truce broke down in the summer, shifting the focus of the wider U.S.-Iran war that erupted in February.

Over the past 24 hours, the Yemeni fighters said they targeted three Saudi airports, including the international airport in capital Riyadh, energy installations, a pipeline and an air base.

Military spokesman Yahya Saree said the group launched missiles at “King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, the capital of the Saudi enemy, in two phases”, the airports in Dammam in the east and Najran in the south.

The international airport on Saturday (October 24, 2026), however, said it would resume domestic and international flights “effective Sunday” in a post on X, after it was closed following several deadly attacks this month.

The Houthis also launched attacks on the southern Khamis Mushait air base as well as “crude oil pumping stations and the crude oil pipeline from east to west”.

The Saudi civil defence agency said it had also responded to falling debris in the Mecca and Medina regions on Saturday (October 24, 2026) after intercepting two Houthi missiles. The Houthis denied targeting the cities, the two holiest in Islam, calling the Saudi claim a “huge lie”.

The Houthis also fired at the southern Yemeni city of Aden, the interim seat of the Saudi-backed government, saying they targeted a naval base and military camp overseen by Saudi forces.

Authorities said the coast guard’s headquarters and a second building of theirs, as well as Aden airport had been targeted.

The fresh attack claims came after the Houthis’ Al-Masirah TV channel accused the kingdom of separate strikes in Yemen that killed more than a dozen people. Riyadh has not claimed responsibility for the alleged strikes.

The Houthi broadcaster said a strike on a house in Sanaa killed at least four people, another at a residential building for cement factory workers killed eight and another outside the city of Hodeida killed five from the same family.

Yemen’s civil war, pitting the Iran-backed Houthis against the Saudi-supported and internationally recognised government, had been dormant since a ceasefire in 2022, but erupted again in July as the wider Middle East war roiled the region.

Diplomats evacuated

Earlier Saturday (October 24, 2026), the Saudi-led coalition said it had intercepted two missiles targeting Saudi cities Taif and Yanbu in the kingdom’s west.

Saudi Arabia’s civil defence had broadcast warnings of “potential danger” for four western regions, including Taif and Yanbu as well as Mecca, home to Islam’s holiest city.

The warning was lifted minutes later.

The group has also targeted the kingdom’s oil infrastructure as well as its airports and tankers.

Yanbu is a major oil export hub on the Red Sea coast that has allowed Riyadh to bypass Iran’s blockade of the Strait of Hormuz for much of its crude exports via the east-west pipeline.

An attack on Riyadh airport earlier this month killed 13 people and forced it to shut, while this week the U.S. ordered non-essential embassy staff and their families to leave Saudi Arabia, citing the Houthi threat.

Riyadh leads a military coalition that first intervened in 2015 in the conflict, which has devastated Yemen and created one of the world’s worst humanitarian crises.

The dramatic escalation in Yemen, with the Houthis taking control of the entire Red Sea coast in a lightning offensive last month, has further destabilised the region and disrupted oil markets.

In July, a fragile 2022 truce fell apart after the Houthis allowed an Iranian plane to land in Yemen’s capital Sanaa in defiance of Saudi control over Yemeni airspace, setting off a spate of attacks.

The Houthis then declared a maritime blockade of Saudi Arabia and began hitting its ships, territory and oil facilities, before launching a major offensive in September in which they seized Yemeni government-held territory along the Red Sea coast.

In response, the Houthis have also reported frequent Saudi strikes targeting areas under their control.

Egypt has suggested sending troops to help defend Saudi Arabia, while Britain and France have offered their forces to protect the Gulf kingdom.

On Saturday (October 24, 2026), the U.S. Mission to the United Arab Emirates and U.S. embassy in Riyadh said Washington’s travel advisories for both Gulf countries were “updated to reflect an increase in potential armed attacks by the Iranian-supported Houthis”.

World.title: Life convicts can avail 40 days of annual leave in two instalments, rules Madras High Court
World.content:
CHENNAI

Life convicts, who had completed 14 years of incarceration, are entitled to avail 40 days of ordinary leave in two instalments annually and they cannot be forced by the prison authorities to avail the leave only once every year, the Madras High Court has ruled.

Justices Anita Sumanth and Sunder Mohan said, the Tamil Nadu Prison and Correctional Services department was denying leave to life convicts in instalments due to the use of the term ‘spell’ in both Rule 22(2)(c) and 22(3) of the Tamil Nadu Suspension of Sentence Rules, 1982.

In order to remove the ambiguity that had arisen because of the use of the same term in both the provisions, the Division Bench ordered that the word ‘spell’ found in the proviso to Rule 22(2)(c) must be read as ‘instalment’ so that it could be distinguished from the word ‘spell’ in Rule 22(3).

The judges further clarified that that the maximum period of 40 days of annual ordinary leave could be availed by an eligible prisoner in two instalments within one year from the first day of the first instalment of such leave and that their next annual entitlement would begin a year after the last day of the second instalment.

The verdict was passed while allowing a writ petition (criminal) filed by life convict S. Babu who was denied 14 days of ordinary leave on the ground that he had already been granted 26 days of ordinary leave in April 2026 and therefore, would have to wait till April 2027 to avail his next entitlement to ordinary leave.

Authoring the judgement, Justice Sumanth said, the proviso to Rule 22(2)(c) states that “the maximum period of 40 days of ordinary leave may be availed in one spell or in two spells of any duration.” Rule 22(3) states that a prisoner shall be granted the second or subsequent spell after one year from the last leave.

Highlighting that the intention of the law makers was to give the prisoners the right to avail ordinary leave in two instalments within a year, the judge said, the use of the term ‘spell’ instead of ‘instalment’ in Rule 22(2)(c) had made the prison authorities interpret that the 40 day leave period must be availed in one go every year.

“Certainly, this cannot be the intention behind the grant of 40 days leave and the facility permitting the prisoner to avail the leave in two instalments. The unfortunate situation has arisen by virtue of the use of the word ‘spell’ in both Rule 22(2)(c) and 22(3) and we hence clarify that the word ‘spell’ in the proviso to Rule 22(2)(c) be read as ‘instalment’ to contra distinguish it from the word ‘spell’ used in Rule 22(3),” the Bench wrote.

On the other ground raised by the prison authorities that the petitioner, who had completed 18 years of incarceration, had absconded in 1997 and also between 2004 and 2014 when he was granted ordinary leave without escort, the judges said, they had already held in another case in June this year that the offence of absconding would not disentitle a convict from availing ordinary leave five years after committing such an offence.

The Bench took note that a trial court had on July 2, 2026 sentenced the petitioner to two months of imprisonment for the charge of escaping from lawful custody and he had already undergone that sentence too along with his life imprisonment.

Further, stating that the petitioner had so far undergone 18 years of incarceration (excluding the period he had gone absconding after availing leave) since the life imprisonment imposed on him in 1992, the court held that he would be entitled to 40 days of annual ordinary leave in two instalments.

After the petitioner had absconded during his leave period in 1997, he was recaptured on November 23, 2000. Thereafter, he was granted 30 days of leave in January 2004. He absconded during that period too and was recaptured on September 6, 2014. Further, he had so far availed 456 days of both ordinary and emergency leave, government counsel C.R. Malarvanan told the court.

World.title: ‘Modification in pavement goes unnoticed in Nanganallur ‘
World.content:
During the day, the ramps are visible. After sunset, the ramps are difficult to spot due to poor lighting. Even when trying to avoid a speeding motorist or a motorcyclist, pedestrians can fall over them during daylight. A commercial establishment next to the confectionery has constructed a cement ramp. Pedestrians can skid while trying to negotiate it (climb up and down) to avoid speeding motorists.

In addition, the walkway along the carriageway is sliding, and pedestrians can slip and fall. Residents and commercial establishments have carried out the modifications and ramp installation in the walkway, and Greater Chennai Corporation must take action.

B. Ramachandran is a long-time resident of Nanganallur

World.title: ‘Widen Pammal Road’
World.content:
Suburban areas from Pallavaram to Kundrathur, a stretch of about 8 kilometers, are linked by only one main road, Pammal-Anakaputhur-Kundrathur Road, running through Pammal and Anakaputhur and ending at the Kundrathur region.

This stretch has been narrow for over four decades and is becoming more congested because of encroachments and traders unwilling to give up land for road widening.

Open gutters, increasing two-wheeler ridership, heavy vehicle traffic, public transportation, many schools in the area, a lack of traffic signals, and full-time police officials add to congestion on the road almost throughout the day.

Population growth in the area is fuelled by the continued proliferation of apartment complexes.

Things get worse even with a drizzle, and the roads are now pockmarked with countless potholes. There are no alternate routes or wide enough bylanes, and one has to endure the pain of driving on the narrow main road.

The authorities need a strong-willed approach to develop a long-term arrangement that enables smooth traffic movement.

World.title: Tree falls near school in Ashok Nagar; a lucky escape for students
World.content:
A tree near Sixth Avenue (near the entrance of GRT school) in Ashok Nagar fell on October 21. As luck would have it, it was a holiday for the school on account of the rains. This road comes under the purview of Ward 135 in Zone 10 (Kodambakkam).

Earlier, on October 18, another tree had fallen, and this was on 86th Street in Ashok Nagar. In this incident, a bike was damaged.

From time to time, a road is dug up several times for various works including stormwater drain construction, laying water pipes, sewage pipes and telecommunication cables. This could damage the roots of trees, and as a result, they get uprooted.

Hence, the Parks Department of the Greater Chennai Corporation should take necessary measures without any delay and prevent the occurrence of untoward incidents.

Mohammed Yusufdeen is a resident of Ashok Nagar

World.title: Another alleged hooch tragedy claims over 10 in Madhya Pradesh district; administration denies
World.content:
The Congress on Saturday (Saturday 24, 2026) accused the Madhya Pradesh Government of shielding the liquor mafia after the Dewas district administration dismissed the claims made by residents of two villages that at least 10 people had died there due to consuming spurious liquor in the past few weeks.

Residents of Chandana and Binjana villages in Dewas have alleged that they have lost several members to spurious liquor, while many have had their vision damaged. State Congress president Jitu Patwari also visited the village.

The matter came to light after a local Hindi daily reported that nine people had died in Chandana and four in Binjana since September 27, after which Mr. Patwari visited the affected families.

Mr. Patwari, however, claimed that around 22 people have died so far in Chandana and nearby villages.

“Recently in Sagar district [in September] and before that in Morena [in 2021], people died due to poisonous liquor but the government did not learn a lesson. After talking to people, around 22 deaths have been verified in Chandana and nearby villages of Dewas due to spurious liquor. At least 35-40 people have had an impact on their vision,” Mr. Patwari told reporters in Dewas.

He said that he spoke to the in-charge Collector Dalip Kumar, who told him that “it was yet to be ascertained if the water was poisonous or the liquor”.

​Drinking to death: On illicit liquor cases

“But the families are saying that these people had passed away or damaged their vision after drinking alcohol only. If there was something wrong with the water, why did only those who consumed liquor die? Despite that, if the administration tried to hide it, there cannot be greater sin then,” Mr. Patwari said.

“This means the government want to protect the liquor mafia who sell poisonous liquor and kill people. What were the police doing when counterfeit liquor was being sold in the area?” he alleged, demanding removal of the District Collector.

Highlighting the mass deaths in various tragedies across Madhya Pradesh in the past year, like Indore, Chhindwara and Balaghat, the Congress leader said that the State had become the “biggest den of mass deaths”.

The district administration has, however, denied that the deaths were caused by the liquor while attributing them to regular illnesses and overdose of legal liquor.

In a fact-check statement late on Friday (October 23, 2026), the administration said that no case of a person being admitted to any hospital due to spurious liquor has been reported in the district.

“Liquor seized during the investigation was from licensed shops, and chemical tests and post-mortems did not confirm the presence of poison. No patient was admitted to any health centre or hospital in the district or nearby for cases of consumption of poisonous liquor, visual impairment, or poisoning,” it said, terming local news reports as “misleading”.

Mr. Kumar, the Dewas Municipal Commissioner who is currently in-charge Collector, told reporters that viscera samples of the deceased who underwent post-mortem examinations have been sent for forensic testing to ascertain the causes of deaths.

“Any legal action will be taken if the FSL reports confirm that the liquor consumed by the deceased was spurious. The Excise department is also collecting samples of liquor bottles from the area to conduct tests,” he said, adding that action will be taken against those responsible if the test reports confirm poisonous material in the liquor.

Meanwhile, Kavita Parmar, wife of the deceased Rahul Parmar, said, “He died after consuming alcohol. He had consumed alcohol, after which he passed away. He used to drink only a little. He had never experienced chest pain or vomiting before, but this time he did. The liquor shop here should be shut down. What happened to me should not happen to anyone else.”

His father, Ram Chandra Parmar, said that his son also had “foam coming out of his mouth” after he collapsed due to dizziness. “When some officials came and asked me about his death, I told them that my son had died due to alcohol only,” he told a wire agency.

Taking cognisance of news reports, Ujjain Divisional Commissioner Asheesh Singh late on Saturday (October 24, 2026) formed an investigation committee to probe the alleged deaths in Chandana and Binjana villages in the past one month.

The five-member panel headed by Ujjain Additional Collector Pratham Kaushik has been asked to conduct a detailed investigation into the causes of death, circumstances and other facts of the matter, and submit its report within 15 days.

The panel includes all officials from outside Dewas, including an Additional Superintendent of Police, a sub-divisional magistrate, and one senior official each from the Excise and Health departments.

Earlier in September, more than 25 people had died in Sagar district’s Banda and Shahgarh subdivisions after drinking counterfeit liquor made under the name of a popular brand in the region.

World.title: Islamabad rebuts Kabul's stance on ‘lacking capacity’ to fuel insecurity in Pakistan, slams 'diversionary allegations'
World.content:
The information ministry on Saturday rebutted the Afghan Taliban’s stance that it lacked the “capabilities” to fuel insecurity in other countries and criticised it for resorting to “diversionary allegations” instead of preventing the use of Afghanistan’s soil for terrorist attacks against Pakistan.

The ministry’s rebuttal comes after spokesperson for the interim Taliban administration in Afghanistan, Zabiullah Mujahid, said in a statement on X last night that it was not in his country’s “interest to create insecurity in Pakistan or to support any acts of instability there”.

He further contended that the Taliban “do not possess capabilities or resources to foment or finance insecurity in other countries”, and claimed that Islamabad’s “misguided approach distracted Pakistan’s security forces from their own duties”.

On Saturday, the information ministry said the Afghan Taliban “once again resorted to diversionary allegations instead of addressing Pakistan’s legitimate and longstanding security concerns”.

“Pakistan’s concerns are not based on conjecture,” it asserted, adding that the “assertion that Afghanistan lacks either the capacity or the interest to destabilise Pakistan does not address these documented concerns”.

It backed its stance on cross-border terrorism from Afghanistan by citing a report by the United Nations Security Council’s (UNSC) Analytical Support and Sanctions Monitoring Team and another report submitted to the United States Congress.

The UNSC team, in its 16th report, “examined the presence and activities of terrorist groups in Afghanistan”, the ministry said.

It further noted that the report by the US Lead Inspector General’s Operation Enduring Sentinel for January-March 2026 stated that the Afghan Taliban continued to allow the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) to operate from Afghan territory.

The ministry also highlighted other findings from the report, which stated that the Taliban continued to allow TTP “greater liberty and support, resulting in increased TTP attacks against Pakistan”. It added that TTP remained the “largest in number” among those groups.

Screengrab from US Lead Inspector General’s Operation Enduring Sentinel’s report for January-March 2026.

“The report estimated TTP strength at 4,000–6,000 fighters. These assessments underscore the seriousness of Pakistan’s concerns regarding terrorist sanctuaries and support networks operating from Afghan soil,” the information ministry emphasised.

“Repeated attempts by armed terrorists to infiltrate across Pakistan-Afghanistan border, the killing of Afghan nationals and members of terrorist groups during Pakistan’s counterterrorism operations, and the recovery of foreign-origin weapons from terrorist elements, all warrant serious scrutiny,” the ministry stressed.

It noted that Pakistan had also raised concerns over “alleged facilitation of terrorist groups by Afghan Taliban officials, including officials in Kandahar”. “Such concerns cannot be dismissed through blanket denials; they require credible explanations and verifiable action.”

The ministry further said that “blaming Pakistan’s security institutions does not absolve the [Afghan Taliban] regime of its responsibility to prevent Afghan territory from being used for terrorism against Pakistan”.

‘Legitimate security concerns’

The ministry clarified that Pakistan’s “security measures are directed against terrorist threats, not the Afghan people”.

“Attempts to portray Pakistan’s legitimate security concerns and necessary defensive measures as hostility towards Afghanistan will neither deflect attention from the issue nor resolve it,” it stressed.

Pointing out that peace and stability were closely linked, it highlighted that Afghan people stand “as much to gain from a region free of terrorism as their Pakistani neighbours”.

“The Afghan Taliban regime must end any tolerance, facilitation or support for terrorist organisations, including TTP, BLA (Baloch Liberation Army) and their affiliates, and ensure that Afghan territory is not used to plan, prepare or launch attacks against Pakistan,” the ministry demanded.

It declared that Islamabad “will continue to take all necessary measures to protect its citizens, sovereignty and territorial integrity”.

The ministry affirmed that Pakistan “remains open to responsible engagement based on mutual respect, verifiable commitments and concrete action against terrorist sanctuaries, support networks and cross-border infiltration”.

“However, Afghan Taliban regime must understand that peace can only prevail in the region if Pakistan’s core concern of terrorism originating from Afghanistan is verifiably addressed by the Afghan Taliban,” the statement concluded.

Ties between Pakistan and Afghanistan have been strained in the past few years as Islamabad continues to voice its concern over cross-border terrorism.

Islamabad has repeatedly urged the Taliban administration in Kabul to dismantle terrorist sanctuaries on Afghan soil, particularly those linked to the banned TTP, that are used for attacks in Pakistan. Officials say those appeals have gone unheeded.

September witnessed another bout of conflict between the two neighbours, with Pakistan carrying out calibrated airstrikes in the border region in response to terrorist attacks in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

This was followed by drone incursions from across the border, which Islamabad said were shot down, and two further rounds of retaliatory airstrikes.

Pakistan rejects Khalilzad’s allegations of arming Afghans

Earlier in the day, the information ministry rejected former United States envoy Zalmay Khalilzad’s “baseless and misleading allegations” that Pakistan was “arming Afghans to fight the Taliban”.

Zalmay Khalilzad, then-special envoy for Afghanistan Reconciliation, testifies before the Senate Foreign Relations Committee during a hearing on Capitol Hill in Washington, US, on April 27, 2021. — Pool via Reuters

The ministry’s response came a day after Khalilzad, who served as special representative to Afghanistan during the first Trump administration, claimed on X that there were “ many reports that Pakistan is arming Afghans to fight the Taliban in Afghanistan”. He further alleged that Pakistan was now “recruiting Afghans to fight against anti-Pakistan insurgents”, adding that ties between the two countries were likely to “get much worse”.

“His sweeping baseless assertions merely recycle speculative narratives as part of his personal agenda to prop [the] terrorism-supporting Taliban regime,” the information ministry’s fact-check account said on X.

It rebuked Khalilzad, saying his “[peddling] of such unsubstantiated allegations only exposes his skewed agenda-based views”.

The ministry highlighted that it was “particularly misleading to conflate Pakistan’s legitimate counterterrorism operations against terrorist organisations operating from inside Afghan Taliban regime-controlled areas threatening its citizens with allegations of recruiting Afghan nationals or sponsoring armed groups inside Afghanistan”.

“Pakistan remains at the forefront of the fight against terrorism and has made enormous sacrifices in protecting regional peace and security,” it emphasised.

It went on to point out that successive monitoring reports issued by the United Nations had documented the continued presence and activities of terrorist organisations, including the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) and Al-Qaeda, inside Afghanistan.

“Khalilzad’s allegations conveniently divert attention from the Afghan Taliban regime’s responsibility to prevent its territory from being used by India-sponsored proxies for terrorism against Pakistan,” the statement added.

Khalilzad, who negotiated a US deal with the Taliban that led to the withdrawal of Nato forces from Afghanistan, has previously called for Islamabad and Kabul to enter a negotiated settlement multiple times, as recently as January this year.

In November last year, the information ministry criticised Khalilzad for “creating a false impression” of the militant group Islamic State-Khorasan (IS-K) having a presence in Punjab.

The ex-US envoy had claimed an IS-K commander was killed in Punjab’s Akhtarabad. The ministry later clarified that a man had been killed during a dacoity/robbery-related incident, not a counterterrorism operation, and that there was no evidence linking him to IS-K.

In March 2023, the Foreign Office (FO) reacted strongly to a series of suggestions made by Khalilzad, saying Pakistan did not need “unsolicited advice” on the challenges it faces.

That statement by Khalilzad also prompted the US State Department to clarify that the former envoy did not represent the country’s foreign policy and did not speak for the administration of then-president Joe Biden.

World.title: In Berlin meeting, Siemens affirms support for strengthening Pakistan's healthcare infrastructure
World.content:
The executive vice president of technology giant Siemens on Saturday met with President Asif Ali Zardari in Berlin and expressed his readiness to enhance support for strengthening existing healthcare infrastructure in Pakistan, the Presidency said.

The meeting took place on the third and final day of President Zardari’s official visit to Germany, which came as the two countries are set to mark the 75th anniversary of their diplomatic relations.

According to a statement by President Zardari’s office, he was called on by executives from the health company, including Siemens Executive Vice President Daniel Frisch.

The executive briefed the president on his company’s accomplishments in Pakistan and acknowledged the difference in health services as a positive outcome of the Sindh health department’s “rationally networked steps”.

According to the Presidency, Frisch “expressed his readiness and desire to enhance existing support through innovative solutions and technological applications for strengthening existing healthcare infrastructure of Pakistan”.

“The Siemens delegation told the president that their representatives will soon visit Pakistan to sign MoUs (memoranda of understanding) with their partners in capacity building and technological domains in the health industry of Pakistan,” the Presidency said.

“The delegation told the president that the technological infrastructure cooperation of the company extends to cancer, stroke and other diseases.”

Meanwhile, President Zardari called for the absorption of research-based and technology-driven solutions to improve health services in Pakistan.

He affirmed that Islamabad highly values German industrial, technological and infrastructural support from organisations like Siemens’ health division, which has been present in Pakistan for decades, with over 100 employees in three major cities.

President Zardari expressed appreciation for Siemens’ presence in Pakistan and noted that the “long-awaited mutual desire of expanded and augmented bilateral partnership” between Islamabad and Berlin was affirmed during his meeting with German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier yesterday.

He also opined that “affordable, yet qualified and highly standardised health service delivery, stays fundamental to enable each and every citizen to realise unhindered potential”.

“We strive for broadened and all-inclusive provision of quality healthcare, particularly for poverty-stricken people in remote areas,” the president was quoted as saying by his office.

President Zardari encouraged Siemens to further engage with Pakistan and diversify its investment across multiple sectors across the country. He also assured the company’s upper echelon of the “fullest institutional cooperation” through the Special Investment Facilitation Council (SIFC).

Sindh Chief Minister Sindh Murad Ali Shah, Senator Saleem Mandviwalla, the Ambassador of Pakistan to Germany Salman Sharif and Sindh provincial ministers were also present during the meeting.

‘Significant advancement’ in bilateral ties

Later, President Zardari departed back home from the airport in Berlin, where he was bid farewell by senior German officials and Sharif.

“President Asif Ali Zardari’s visit to Germany, after a hiatus of more than two decades, marks a significant advancement in the bilateral relations between the two countries,” the Presidency said.

It expressed confidence that the trip will pave the way for further promotion of goodwill and ties between Islamabad and Berlin.

The statement further noted that the high-level meetings between President Zardari and President Steinmeier reflected a “shared commitment to further broadening bilateral relations”.

On Friday, Zardari and his German counterpart discussed bilateral relations, with Steinmeier praising Pakistan’s “rising diplomatic profile in the resolution of regional and global disputes”.

They also discussed challenges related to Afghanistan, with President Zardari stressing that while Pakistan “has no conflict with the Afghan people”, it would not allow terrorists to use Afghan soil to attack Pakistan’s citizens and violate its sovereignty.

Steinmeier appreciated Pakistan for facilitating the verification of 500 Afghans “destined to be repatriated to Germany” and also commended its humanitarian assistance to “millions of Afghans” over more than four decades, President Zardari’s office said.

He also took a “significant interest” in the Makkah defence pact signed between Pakistan, Turkiye and Saudi Arabia, which is aimed at collective deterrence.

Pakistan and Berlin formally established diplomatic ties on Oct 15, 1951. Both countries remain actively engaged in the areas of economy, defence, education and culture.

Exports to Germany dipped 3.53 per cent to $1.369 billion in the first 10 months of the previous fiscal year (FY2025-26) from $1.419bn in the same period the year prior.

World.title: Former skipper Shan Masood axed as Pakistan turn to youth for Sri Lanka Tests
World.content:
Pakistan have dropped former Test captain Shan Masood as selectors turn to youth and domestic performers for the two-match ICC World Test Championship series against Sri Lanka, with Babar Azam retaining the captaincy of a revamped 14-member squad announced by the country’s cricket board on Saturday.

Three batters — Mohammad Taha, Mohammad Suleman and Sameer Minhas — have earned maiden Test call-ups, while Ali Usman and Salman Ali Agha have also been included in the squad for the series to be played in Rawalpindi and Lahore from Nov 9 to 21.

Shan’s omission marks a significant change in Pakistan’s top order as the selectors look beyond established international players amid the team’s struggles in the current WTC cycle.

The left-handed opener scored 109 against the West Indies in the opening Test in Trinidad in July before missing the second match with a finger injury.

Against England later in the year, he managed scores of 29 and five at Leeds, 26 and one at Lord’s, and 95 and five at Edgbaston, finishing the three-Test series with 161 runs in six innings.

Shan has scored 2,926 runs in 50 Tests at an average of 30.80, including seven centuries and 15 half-centuries.

His exclusion, alongside those of several other established players, points to a renewed emphasis on domestic performances as Pakistan seek to strengthen their red-ball fortunes.

Taha, 26, has been the leading run-scorer in the ongoing President’s Trophy Grade-I competition, accumulating 730 runs in seven matches since September. His tally includes three centuries and a highest score of 225.

Suleman has also impressed in the tournament, ranking fifth on the batting charts with 652 runs in seven matches, including three centuries. Sameer, playing his maiden first-class season, has scored 405 runs in seven matches after impressing for Pakistan’s Under-19 side.
